Moreover, structural relaxation of Fe₂(MoO₄)₃ containing an oxygen vacancy indicates that oxygen diffusion from the bulk to the surface may occur very rapidly, such that the local symmetry remains effectively unchanged. This interpretation is in line with the absence of measurable peak shifts or broadening in the experimental Raman spectra.

articles.title: Metastable polar order and phase competition in Carpy-Galy LaTaO4
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.06943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Carpy-Galy LaTaO₄ undergoes a structural sequence linking the antipolar monoclinic P2₁/c ground state and the polar orthorhombic Cmc2₁ phase through an incommensurately modulated regime. First-principles calculations identify a metastable polar monoclinic P2₁ phase as a commensurate intermediate in the phase-transition landscape. As a common subgroup of P2₁/c and Cmc2₁, P2₁ provides a symmetry-connected route between the established polymorphs. Mode-resolved energy surfaces for these symmetry-breaking pathways show that coupling between the respective primary order parameters and an isosymmetric relaxation stabilizes the P2₁ minimum along both pathways. Consequently, the P2₁/c→ P2₁ transformation has a finite energy barrier, while a restricted soft-mode model retains competing P2₁ and Cmc2₁ basins over an illustrative range of harmonic stiffness. Lattice-metric and neutron-diffraction comparisons indicate a shared displacement character between the calculated commensurate state and the experimental IC-o modulation, supporting the use of P2₁ as a commensurate structural reference for IC-o. Finally, composition-dependent energetics suggest chemical routes for tuning polar-antipolar competition.

articles.title: Residual diagnostics for detecting the breakdown of the single power-law approximation in photoelectron yield spectroscopy: application to doped silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11331v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Our automated analysis of photoelectron yield spectroscopy (PYS) estimates the threshold Ith and the exponent n of a single power law for every spectrum. When this model fits poorly, however, the analysis cannot tell whether the data or the model is at fault. Here we present residual diagnostics that separate the two causes. The exponent is scanned continuously on a 1/n-power fit with an Akaike information criterion (AIC) based on the mean absolute error (MAE), and the spread of the resulting Akaike weights (P × Δ n) quantifies the uncertainty of the estimate. The normalized MAE (NMAE) and the RMSE-to-MAE ratio (RMR) assess the data quality, the Durbin-Watson (DW) statistic assesses the model adequacy, and the three checks are reported in parallel. With criteria set from an Au reference, the diagnostics were applied to 60 continuous measurements in air of four HF-treated Si samples. For heavily doped p-type Si, DW fell below its criterion, whereas the means of NMAE and RMR remained within their criteria. Prompted by this flag, we fitted the spectrum with a two-component model with fixed exponents (n = 1 and 2.5); the AIC decreased by 56, DW increased from 0.86 to 1.99, and the two components set in at 4.70 and 5.28 eV. For heavily doped n-type Si, the change during air exposure was consistent with a single component. The diagnostics thus identify the spectra that require a multi-component analysis without assuming an emission mechanism.

articles.title: Exponential clustering of bipartite quantum entanglement at arbitrary temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2108.12209v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Macroscopic quantum effects play central roles in the appearance of inexplicable phenomena in low-temperature quantum many-body physics. Such macroscopic quantumness is often evaluated using long-range entanglement, i.e., entanglement in the macroscopic length scale. The long-range entanglement not only characterizes the novel quantum phases but also serves as a critical resource for quantum computation. Thus, the problem that arises is under which conditions can the long-range entanglement be stable even at room temperatures. Here, we show that bi-partite long-range entanglement is unstable at arbitrary temperatures and exponentially decays with distance. Our theorem provides a no-go theorem on the existence of the long-range entanglement. The obtained results are consistent with the existing observations that long-range entanglement at non-zero temperatures can exist in topologically ordered phases, where tripartite correlations are dominant. In the derivation of our result, we introduce a quantum correlation defined by the convex roof of the standard correlation function. We establish an exponential clustering theorem for generic quantum many-body systems for such a quantum correlation at arbitrary temperatures, which yields our main result by relating quantum correlation to quantum entanglement. As a simple application of our analytical techniques, we derived a general limit on the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information and the quantum Fisher information, which will attract significant attention in the field of quantum metrology. Our work reveals novel general aspects of low-temperature quantum physics and sheds light on the characterization of long-range entanglement.

articles.title: Bottlenecks in quantum channels and finite temperature phases of matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2412.09598v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an analog of the "bottleneck theorem," well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel's steady state, then states initialized on one side of this barrier will take a long time to relax, putting a lower bound on the mixing time in terms of an appropriately defined "quantum bottleneck ratio." Importantly, this bottleneck ratio involves not only the probabilities of the relevant subspaces, but also the size of off-diagonal matrix elements between them. For low temperature quantum many-body systems, we use the bottleneck theorem to bound the performance of any quasilocal Gibbs sampler. This leads to a new perspective on thermally stable quantum phases in terms of a decomposition of the Gibbs state into multiple components separated by bottlenecks. As a concrete application, we show rigorously that weakly perturbed commuting projector models with extensive energy barriers (which include certain classical and quantum expander codes) have exponentially large mixing times

articles.title: Mean-Field Dynamics of the Bose-Hubbard Model in High Dimension
articles.abstract: arXiv:2501.05304v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Bose-Hubbard model effectively describes bosons on a lattice with on-site interactions and nearest-neighbour hopping, serving as a foundational framework for understanding strong particle interactions and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition. This paper aims to rigorously establish the validity of a mean-field approximation for the dynamics of quantum systems in high dimension, using the Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice as a case study. We prove a trace norm estimate between the one-lattice-site reduced density of the Schrödinger dynamics and the mean-field dynamics in the limit of large dimension. Here, the mean-field approximation is in the hopping amplitude and not in the interaction, leading to a very rich and non-trivial mean-field equation. This mean-field equation does not only describe the condensate, as is the case when the mean-field description comes from a large particle number limit averaging out the interaction, but it allows for a phase transition to a Mott insulator since it contains the full non-trivial interaction. Our work is a rigorous justification of a simple case of the highly successful dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for bosons, which somewhat surprisingly yields many qualitatively correct results in three dimensions.

articles.title: Circuit-based characterization of finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.15204v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum phases at zero temperature can be characterized as equivalence classes under local unitary transformations: two ground states within a gapped phase can be transformed into each other via a local unitary circuit. We generalize this circuit-based characterization of phases to systems at finite-temperature thermal equilibrium described by Gibbs states. We construct a channel circuit that approximately transforms one Gibbs state into another provided the two are connected by a path in parameter space along which a certain correlation-decay condition holds. For finite-dimensional systems of linear size L and approximation error ϵ, the locality of the circuit is rm polylog(rm poly(L)/ϵ). The correlation-decay condition, which we specify, is expected to be satisfied in the interior of many noncritical thermal phases, including those displaying discrete symmetry breaking and topological order. As an application, we show that any system in the same thermal phase as a zero-temperature topological code coherently preserves quantum information for a macroscopically long time, establishing self-correction as a universal property of thermal phases. As part of the proof, we provide explicit encoding and decoding channel circuits to encode information into, and decode it from, a system in thermal equilibrium.

articles.title: Development of a Particle Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook Method for Rarefied Monatomic Gas Mixtures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method has long served as a reliable numerical approach for simulating rarefied and non-equilibrium gas flows. Its computational cost, however, increases rapidly as the flow approaches the near-continuum regime. This limitation has motivated the development of kinetic model equations that replace binary collisions with simplified relaxation processes. This paper presents a particle multi-relaxation unified BGK (UBGK) model for monatomic gas mixtures. The model retains pairwise species relaxation and determines the target velocity, temperature, shear stress, and heat flux by matching the corresponding production terms to those of the Boltzmann equation. A stochastic particle algorithm is developed. The model is implemented in SPARTA, and two validation problems are considered: homogeneous relaxation and a Mach 3 flow over a cylinder. In both cases, the UBGK solution reproduces the DSMC reference behavior, including species-dependent relaxation and non-equilibrium shock structure.

articles.title: Noise Correlation Spectroscopy: A Review
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The frequency noise of an ordinary diode laser, often a nuisance in spectroscopy, can be used to measure atomic coherence. When atoms are prepared in a coherent superposition of two ground states, each random shift in laser frequency changes how much light they absorb, so the transmitted light carries a record of that coherence. Correlating the intensity fluctuations of two fields, each linking one ground state to a shared excited state, reads this record out, a technique known as noise correlation spectroscopy. The correlation signal is narrower than the transparency window the same fields create and switches sign as their frequency difference is tuned. Its width is set by the rate at which the atoms lose coherence and, over a wide range, does not grow with laser power. Over two decades the method has spread from warm vapors to cold atoms, to multi-field schemes, and to diamond and rare-earth-doped crystals. This review, to the author's knowledge the first, brings together its theory, experiments and applications, and examines its limits, the challenges that remain, and the opportunities that could make it a standard spectroscopic tool.

articles.title: Advanced computational methods for simulating the classical hydrogen atom in stochastic electrodynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic electrodynamics (SED) is a theory of nature that seeks to derive key aspects of quantum mechanics and quantum electrodynamics from a purely classical physics perspective. While SED has been successful in many areas, it has largely failed to stably simulate the 3D classical hydrogen atom. The computational methodology presented here overcomes these foundational challenges. We develop a pseudo-wave formulation that integrates the solid angle in k-space utilizing symmetry, resulting in a significantly reduced memory footprint and lower computational overhead for generating the zero-point radiation spectrum. This optimization is paired with a logarithmic frequency grid, a sliding window tracking the instantaneous Keplerian frequency, and a Tukey smoothing function to eliminate discrete force discontinuities. Integrated via an adaptive RKF45 solver across highly dense grids of up to 100-million bins, these techniques demonstrate the asymptotic convergence of ensemble stability. We show that increasing the grid resolution in the high-frequency domain systematically mitigates artificial electron decay, yielding a simulated probability density function that closely aligns with the quantum mechanical ground state P(r).

articles.title: Nonrelativistic quantum theory of non-dipole effects in a multielectron atom: radiation transition operator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the work of Hopersky A.N. et al., arXiv: 2609.33494v1 [physics. atom-ph] in the Loudon integral representation, the general analytical structure of the complete operator of a multipole radiation transition taking into account non-dipole effects for a multielectron atom is established. In this Letter this structure is converted to the sum only for all multipoles.

articles.title: Thermo-viscous feedback in heat transport through fracture-matrix systems with finite thermal capacity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In geothermal systems, injected fluid flows along preferential fracture pathways and exchanges heat with matrix blocks. Reduced models often neglect temperature-dependent viscosity and assume unlimited matrix storage, although the thermal capacity accessible to the flow is finite. This work analyzes thermo-viscous feedback in a planar fracture-matrix system where viscosity controls discharge through the integrated hydraulic resistance, while finite capacity enters through an effective single-timescale memory fixed by initial uptake and total capacity. The reduced model gives parsimonious semi-analytical predictions with physically based parameters, verified against the nonlinear solution. A perturbation hierarchy separates matrix storage from the hydraulic response it induces, while an exponential velocity reconstruction preserves the exact terminal discharge and bounds front-moment errors within the front-moment limit model. At fixed pressure difference, heating accelerates and broadens the front, whereas cooling delays and sharpens it. The terminal discharge depends only on the endpoint viscosity ratio, while matrix uptake, storage and contrast determine its approach time. At fixed rate, viscosity alters only the pressure drop, not the thermal response. Finite thickness controls the transition to capacity-limited equilibration, and strong matrix uptake collapses the isoviscous response onto a two-variable similarity surface.

articles.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO₂ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio 10 μm diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of 400 nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

articles.title: An improved limit on ¹⁷¹Yb electric dipole moment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Searches for permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe new sources of CP violation beyond the Standard Model. The atomic EDM of ¹⁷¹Yb, which is sensitive to its nuclear Schiff moment, is a promising candidate, but previous measurements were limited by noise and systematic effects induced by the optical dipole trap (ODT) that holds the atoms. Here we report a substantially improved search enabled by a dual-ODT configuration with orthogonal polarizations, and spin measurements for precise alignment of static and optical fields. By suppressing the key parity-mixing systematic effect and vector light-shift noise, we achieve a limit of |d(¹⁷¹Yb)| < 7.5 × 10⁻²⁸ ecdotcm (95% C.L.), which represents a 20-fold improvement over the previous work. We also present the first calculation of the nuclear structure factors of the Schiff moment of ¹⁷¹Yb. The experimental and theoretical advances combine to tighten constraints on CP-violating pion-nucleon couplings in a global analysis. Moreover, this work demonstrates a pathway toward future measurements in ²²⁵Ra, where nuclear deformation offers exceptional sensitivity to physics beyond the Standard Model.

articles.title: Azimuthal Instability in Oscillating Liquid Jets by the Weber Number Variations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the dependence of azimuthal mode growth rate of oscillating liquid laminar jets on the Weber number. The oscillating liquid laminar jets were simulated over a range of Weber numbers. The simulation setup was validated by comparing the instantaneous interface shapes and the visible azimuthal mode from experimental measurements. As the Weber number increases, the spreading angle rises due to the small surface tension, and higher azimuthal modes are observed. Fourier Transform analysis is used to find the exact azimuthal mode of the simulation results. The dominant azimuthal mode increases as the Weber number increases. A power-law dependence of the growth rate on the Weber number is identified, with the obtained exponents showing good agreement with linear instability analysis. Furthermore, the rescaled Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) results collapse onto a single growth curve for each azimuthal mode, validating the proposed power-law for predicting the growth rates of oscillating liquid jets.

articles.title: Improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response in athermal phonon detectors: implications for quasiparticle dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our detectors for Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino--Nucleus Scattering (CEνNS) use photolithographically patterned superconducting athermal phonon sensors that are coupled to kg-scale absorbers of different materials (germanium, silicon, sapphire). Following a particle interaction, athermal phonons from the bulk absorber break Cooper pairs in a superconducting aluminum film that surrounds a tungsten Transition Edge Sensor (TES) in equilibrium through electrothermal feedback. This sensor design is called Quasiparticle-trap-assisted Electro-thermal-feedback Transition-edge-sensor (QET). The QET aluminum film that absorbs the athermal phonons is patterned into fins with lengths limited by the quasiparticle diffusion length in aluminum. Improving the quasiparticle diffusion length in the superconducting aluminum is an area of vigorous research to improve phonon collection efficiency and increase the signal strength for lower-threshold searches. We report significantly improved aluminum films that show systematically larger grain sizes and residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) compared to detectors we have fabricated in the past. The improved RRR and grain sizes were expected to improve the collected signal for a given energy. We report higher signal strength achieved in a detector in comparison to another detector in which all other fabrication parameters were kept identical except for the aluminum film deposition.

articles.title: Streamwise dispersion with interphase mass transfer through a tube
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reactive solute transport in shear flows is of broad importance in chemical engineering, liquid--solid chromatography, and environmental mechanics, particularly in flow reactors and fluidic devices involving interphase mass transfer. Based on the recently developed streamwise dispersion theory for inert solutions (Guan & Chen, 2024, J. Fluid Mech., vol. 980, A33), we present an analytical model for reactive dispersion of chemically active solutes characterized by first-order, irreversible surface reactions. The extension is not a simple perturbation because the reactive boundary destroys mass conservation with streamwise and radial derivatives coupled. The model establishes how the microscopic kinetic reactivity and radial eigenmodes combine to determine a newly defined (effective) local exchange rate. We derive rigorous explicit solutions for the local moments, concentration, and phenomenological transport coefficients at arbitrary reactivity, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations across all regimes. For tube Poiseuille flows, we reveal pre-asymptotic behaviours including sign-changing radial exchange, reactivity-enhanced drift, reactivity-reduced dispersivity, and non-Gaussian concentration profiles. Small- and large-Damköhler-number asymptotics for the local and global transport coefficients identify the reaction-limited and diffusion-limited regimes, connecting the conservative case to the Dirichlet limit at infinite reactivity. This streamwise perspective could advance our understanding of macroscale transport in chemically active systems.

articles.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.

articles.title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The impact of droplets, such as rain and sea sprays, on wind turbine blade surfaces can cause severe damage through leading-edge erosion (LEE). Current industrial practice has largely relied on empirical fatigue models to predict damage progression and guide maintenance. However, an important limitation of existing models is the assumption on ideal impact conditions, including perfectly spherical droplet and normal incidence, which rarely occur in reality. This study develops a fluid-structure interaction (FSI) model that couples incompressible multiphase flow simulations with finite element (FE) analysis of blade materials. Using this framework, we investigate the impact dynamics of droplets with arbitrary shapes and orientations. The results reveal a positive correlation between the peak impact pressure, the influential area at the pressure peak, and the peak impact force. In contrast, the time of peak force scales inversely due to momentum conservation. From these findings, we propose a universal scaling law that relates all key impact loadings to the simple parameter of the droplet projection area, which can be determined solely from the initial droplet geometry and orientation. This law provides a predictive framework for impact loading dynamics of non-ideal shapes, offering new insights into the mechanisms of LEE and improving the accuracy of erosion predictions for wind turbine blades.

articles.title: Single-electron fluorine bonding. II. Benchmarking Minnesota density functional approximations and popular ab initio methods for binding energies (BEs) and F-bond distances
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Companion paper I (Khanal and Arunan, in this issue; arXiv:2610.16629 [physics.chem-ph]) reported reference BEs and F-bond distances for two new databases SEFB-15 (DFcdotsCH₃) and CSFB-14 (DFcdotsNH₃). Here, we assess performance of popular ab initio methods (MP2, MP3, MP4(DQ), MP4(SDQ), CCSD, and QCISD) with valence- and full-electron correlation treatments, and sixteen Minnesota DFAs, including M06-2X already assessed in companion paper I. CCSD/AVDZ reproduces reference F-bond distances closely, although BEs predicted by it deviate more. Among the 16 Minnesota DFAs, M08-HX reliably reproduces both reference values for DFcdotsCH₃ and DFcdotsNH₃, comparable to M05-2X and M06-2X for DFcdotsNH₃. Selected meta-GGAs (M06-L, M11-L, and MN15-L) exhibit spurious fractional charge transfer in cationic complexes even at infinite separation, whereas hybrid Minnesota DFAs do not, except M05 and M06 for NH₃F⁺cdotsCH₃ and NH₂F₂⁺cdotsCH₃. Although M08-HX shows slightly larger monomer delocalization error than M05-2X and M06-2X, it is more reliable for predicting BEs of SEFB complexes, indicating that monomer delocalization error alone does not govern DFA performance. Bader's intermolecular delocalization indices (DIs) further support M08-HX as more reliable than M05-2X and M06-2X for SEFB, while the larger DIs from M05-2X and M06-2X explain the degraded performance of their dispersion-corrected variants for DFcdotsCH₃, with only a minor impact for DFcdotsNH₃, highlighting the system-dependent nature of functional delocalization error. Present work reveals that M08-HX is more reliable than M05-2X and M06-2X for open-shell DFcdotsCH₃ complexes, while all three functionals show comparable reliability for closed-shell DFcdotsNH₃ complexes.

articles.title: Vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy via cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a vibro-polaritonic Raman activity from third-order cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory (CBO-PT) accounting for weak interactions between electrons and low-frequency cavity modes in the vibrational strong coupling (VSC) regime. This work extends the recently presented CBO-PT linear response approach [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2024, 15, 2262-2269] from infrared (IR) to vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy. In a first step, we discuss cavity-induced corrections to the static dipole polarizability tensor, which manifest as molecular and cavity mode contribution determined by the polarization-projected static hyperpolarizability tensor. We then obtain the corresponding vibro-polaritonic Raman activity in double harmonic approximation, which contains molecular, cavity and mixed contributions similar to previously discussed CBO-PT IR intensities. The cavity Raman activity can be interpreted as effective transmission component, which is exclusively determined by the polaritonic Raman response. The methodology and its relation to vibro-polaritonic IR spectroscopy is illustrated for a formaldehyde molecule under VSC. An implementation of the CBO-PT linear response approach for vibro-polaritonic Raman and IR spectroscopies is provided via the open-source Python package CBOvibSpec.

articles.title: Geometry-Dependent Electronic Coupling and Singlet Fission Pathways in Carotenoid Dimers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the density matrix renormalization group method, we solve the Pariser--Parr--Pople model of π-electron systems to determine the character and energies of the low-lying eigenstates of a lycopene dimer comprising two 22-carbon-atom chains. To complement these calculations, we use the molecular-exciton, valence-bond model of polyene systems to derive selection rules governing interchain coupling, which provide a physical framework for interpreting the DMRG results. We find that dimer geometry strongly influences both the character and energetics of the low-lying eigenstates. In vertically stacked dimers, neither the bright-dimer state nor the triplet-pair states contain any interchain charge-transfer (CT) character. In contrast, in slip-stacked dimers, both the bright-dimer state and triplet-pair states do contain interchain CT character. We also find that increasing the interchain coupling preferentially stabilizes states with greater interchain character, leading to a reordering of the low-lying eigenstates. These results have direct implications for energetically possible singlet fission (SF) mechanisms in carotenoid aggregates. For vertically stacked dimers, the only energetically viable pathway identified here proceeds through intermediate intrachain triplet-pair states, whereas slip-stacked geometries allow an additional SF pathway mediated by interchain CT states. Our results establish a direct connection between carotenoid packing geometry, symmetry-controlled electronic coupling, and the energetically accessible pathways for SF.

articles.title: Bayesian Geophysical Inversion using Stein Mixture Variational Inference for Multimodal or Complex Solutions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian geophysical inversion provides a probabilistic framework to estimate subsurface properties, in which uncertainties are represented by a so-called posterior probability density function (pdf). Estimating this pdf is computationally challenging when it is high dimensional or complex, particularly if it may be multimodal. We introduce Stein mixture variational inference (SMVI) for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion with multimodal or complex posterior solutions. The method combines parametric variational inference with Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD). In SMVI, the posterior pdf is approximated by a mixture (sum) of distributions, in which component distributions are optimised jointly using the SVGD update rule. This construction combines computational efficiency with the flexibility to represent a range of plausible Earth models and allows components to be updated in parallel. Here, SMVI is first tested on two synthetic seismic inverse problems, demonstrating that SMVI can recover non-Gaussian, complex and multimodal posterior solutions accurately and efficiently. Then, we apply SMVI to real seismic data by performing Love wave tomography of the British Isles, and obtain inversion results that are consistent with previous Monte Carlo solutions. Around the East Irish Sea sedimentary basins, SMVI captures bimodal uncertainty associated with ambiguity in basin boundary locations, revealing alternative subsurface structures compatible with the observations. These results indicate that SMVI generalises various previous variational methods, and provides a practical and effective framework for quantifying complex uncertainties and supporting geological interpretation of seismic images.

articles.title: Broadband chiroptical sensing with two-mode subwavelength grating waveguides
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Engineering local optical chirality in planar photonic structures offers a route to selective and enhanced light-matter interactions with chiral media. Here, we introduce periodic dielectric waveguides that support chiral evanescent fields through the interaction of two nearly degenerate waveguide modes. We develop a perturbation theory for such a waveguide covered by a chiral layer, relating chirality-induced modal coupling and propagation-constant corrections to measurable intermodal power conversion and differential transmission. Whereas modal detuning confines the chiral response of a symmetric waveguide to a narrow spectral range, mode hybridization in an asymmetric waveguide creates individual eigenmodes that carry nonzero local chirality over a broad spectral range. We show that modal dichroism in realistic lossy waveguides can produce a significant background differential transmission signal. Such a background, however, can be suppressed by comparing transmission through two asymmetric waveguides with opposite structural asymmetries, allowing the chiral response to be reliably extracted. Together, these findings provide a basis for developing integrated photonic components with locally chiral fields, including waveguides, metasurfaces, and resonators.

articles.title: Effects of Spanwise Curvature on Hypersonic Boundary Layer Transition in Görtler-driven Flows
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The influence of spanwise convex curvature on hypersonic boundary-layer transition over a streamwise-concave surface is investigated using direct numerical simulation and Mach 7 experiments. Smooth doubly curved geometries with fixed streamwise concavity and increasing spanwise convex curvature isolate the effects of three-dimensional wall curvature on a centrifugally unstable boundary layer. Increasing spanwise curvature delays transition while preserving a Gortler-dominated route to breakdown. As spanwise curvature increases, the boundary layer thins, reducing the effective Görtler number and weakening centrifugal amplification of streamwise vortices. Consequently, growth of the primary Görtler instability is reduced, vortical structures remain closer to the wall, and secondary instability and turbulent breakdown shift downstream. Spectral proper orthogonal decomposition confirms that low-frequency vortical dynamics remain dominant in controlling transition, with sinuous secondary instability of Görtler vortices providing the principal route to breakdown. Meanwhile, boundary-layer thinning modifies acoustic instability dynamics: the second Mack mode shifts to higher frequencies and higher-frequency supersonic disturbances become increasingly prominent near breakdown as spanwise curvature increases. These acoustic disturbances remain subdominant and do not replace the Görtler-sinuous mechanism as the primary transition pathway. Numerical and experimental results exhibit consistent trends in transition location, thermal-streak organisation and disturbance evolution, supporting a common physical interpretation. These findings demonstrate that spanwise convex curvature stabilises hypersonic Görtler-dominated boundary layers, primarily by suppressing centrifugal amplification and delaying secondary instability, while leaving the transition pathway qualitatively unchanged.

articles.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning Δ(t) and Rabi frequency Ω(t) at frequencies ω₁ and ω₂=ν ω₁ respectively with ν in Z. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for |rm vacrangle (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), |mathbb Z₂rangle, and |mathbb Z₃rangle (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that |rm vacrangle shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while |mathbb Z₃rangle exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the |mathbb Z₂rangle initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with |mathbb Z₃rangle state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.

articles.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.

articles.title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.

articles.title: The Atmospheric Chemistry and Surface Interactions on Mars (ACSIOM) Workshop 2025
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ACSIOM workshop was held in Cambridge from 10th-12th November 2025. Its primary aims were twofold: 1) to gather UK researchers involved in Mars atmospheric science to identify current shortcomings and challenges in the field, and 2) to discuss possible collaborations and future steps needed to maximise the research output from current and future Mars missions. Workshop attendees spanned a wide range of subjects and disciplines, from atmospheric modellers and surface scientists to experimental chemists and Earth/Venus/exoplanet scientists. One of the primary outcomes of the workshop as identified by the attendees was the need for more collaborations between these different communities. It was agreed that we currently lack sufficient interaction between disciplines and this is a key challenge we need to overcome in order to properly utilise and exploit the vast pool of martian expertise available in the UK. Modellers need reaction rates from experimentalists; experimentalists need modelling context to prioritise their experiments; geologists need modelling context to understand the features they see; modellers need geological context to constrain their results. Attendees stressed that the UK Mars community has a critical mass which is internationally recognised, and improving the communication between communities would allow significant progress to be made in martian research, allowing the UK to maintain leadership in Mars science for years to come. We highlight that this is a pivotal moment for such investments as many planetary missions, both for Mars and other terrestrial bodies, are about to be launched or are being considered in the coming years. Having a strong and close-knit community will be key to better identifying needs and capabilities in order to optimise investments in missions and to have the best scientific return possible.

articles.title: Distributional signatures of computation: inferring mechanisms from computation time distributions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational complexity theory provides a framework for analysing abstract models of computation, whereas computational systems operate as finite physical implementations whose behaviour is shaped by their architecture and physical substrate. In such systems, computational organisation cannot be directly characterised from algorithms or internal representations. Building on the use of reaction time distributions to constrain mechanisms in cognitive science, we introduce an empirical framework for investigating computation in physical systems by inferring computational mechanisms from observable computation time distributions. The framework combines empirical benchmarking, which characterises computational efficiency through the scaling of computation time with problem size, with distributional analysis, which treats computation time distributions as signatures of the stochastic dynamics generated by different computational mechanisms. We demonstrate the framework using a scalable visual search paradigm, comparing human performance with three computational models that employ distinct mechanisms of evidence accumulation. Benchmarking reveals broadly similar scaling behaviour for the models and human observers, whereas distributional analysis distinguishes between these models. We show that computation time distributions provide an empirical level of description linking observable computational behaviour to underlying computational mechanisms. This framework complements computational complexity theory by extending the empirical study of computation from measuring computational performance to characterising computational organisation. It provides an empirical approach for comparing finite computational systems across diverse physical implementations, including biological, classical, neuromorphic, and quantum systems, without requiring access to their internal algorithms or architectures.

articles.title: Equiprobability Anomaly Detector Using Angular Distributions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the angular distribution of top quark pairs (tbart) in the semileptonic final state bbarb,ellν qbarq' to construct an anomaly detector for non-tbart events. Wigner D functions expand the distribution with coefficients determined by orthogonal series density estimation. Its equiprobable surfaces bin the events, the non-tbart concentrate at low tbart density. The separation is quantified by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which makes connection to variational autoencoders. The performance is comparable to normalizing flows at parton level, but is limited by jet assignments at reconstruction level.

articles.title: Gauss' law for arbitrarily moving Gaussian surfaces: A revisit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2412.13221v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We have re-examined the integral form of Gauss' law for arbitrarily moving charges inside and outside an arbitrarily expanding (or contracting) and deforming Gaussian surface. We have explicitly calculated the time-dependent Gauss' flux integral for such a generic non-static case with the Maxwell equations under consideration. We have obtained an evolution equation fracddtointₛ₍ₜ₎vecEcdotdvecs(t)=fracI⁽s⁾ᵢₙ(t)ϵ₀ for the time-dependence of the flux-integral. We have demonstrated pedagogically that while the flux integral is dependent on the expansion/contraction of the surface, it is independent of its deformation.

articles.title: Towards Low-Energy Electron High-Resolution Spectroscopy with Transition-Edge Sensors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.21694v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a study of the energy resolution of transition-edge sensors (TESs) for the detection of electrons in the 100~eV kinetic energy range. The TES is a Ti-Au bilayer with an active area of (60 × 60) μm² and a critical temperature of sim 80~mK. The electron source is based on vertically-aligned multiwall carbon nanotubes located inside the cryostat, with electrons generated via field emission. For electrons in the (92 - 99)~eV kinetic energy range, we obtain a Gaussian energy resolution for fully-absorbed electrons of (0.48 ± 0.04 ± 0.06)~eV, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic}. When considering the full-width at half-maximum of the peak textcolorblackof the signal amplitude distribution, the corresponding resolution is of (1.4 ± 0.2 ± 0.3)~eV. The former represents an improvement of (47-60)% with respect to previous results, and is mainly attributed to the reduction in the TES active area. The latter is instead an improvement of over a factor of 21, and is mainly due to the reduction in the emitting area of the electron source, which significantly suppresses electron back-scattering in proximity of the TES. These results represent a major milestone towards high-precision spectroscopy on low-energy electrons, which is a key objective for the PTOLEMY experiment.

articles.title: Offset Dual Microcombs in a Single Microresonator: Kerr-Raman Interleaved Combs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.18640v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated Kerr microcombs have emerged as a central platform for chip-scale nonlinear photonics. One of their most compelling applications is dual-comb technology, which enables fast, high-resolution, coherent optical spectroscopy, precision metrology, ranging, and ultrasensitive sensing by interfering two frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates. However, no effective strategy yet exists to synergistically excite multiple spatial mode families, manage mode competition and energy partitioning, and precisely engineer dispersion, leaving offset co-propagating dual-microcombs in a single resonator elusive. Here we demonstrate a new mechanism for offset dual microcombs formation via Kerr-Raman interleaving for the first time, by leveraging single Raman-active thin-film lithium niobate microrings. Two spatial mode families with high loaded Q factors up to 5 million are dispersion engineered to have nearly identical free-spectral-ranges but a designed relative frequency offset. Stimulated Raman scattering efficiently generates a Raman comb in one family alongside a Kerr comb in the other. The two combs interleave with a fractional offset to form a broadband, densely interleaved spectrum. Pumping the microring at only 320 mW yields Kerr-Raman interleaved dual combs both featuring nearly identical repetition rates around 102 GHz with a small difference of 675 MHz, a relatively flat envelope exceeding 29 nm and an intrinsic comb-line linewidth of 410 Hz. Our results establish offset dual-comb generation in a single microresonator, enabling compact dual-comb sources for chip-scale precision spectroscopy, Vernier-enhanced sensing, and advanced quantum photonics.

articles.title: ADT: All-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete structural tokenization provides a promising route to autoregressive 3D molecular generation. Yet, existing tokenizers face a trade-off between compact representation and all-atom reconstruction: atom-level tokens preserve atomic details but produce long sequences, while compact residue-level protein tokens typically omit side-chain geometry. To overcome this limitation, we propose All-atom Diffusion Tokenizer (ADT), which decouples token granularity from reconstruction resolution. ADT uses one structural token per atom for small molecules and one token per protein residue that jointly represents backbone and side-chain geometry. To mitigate geometric distortion introduced by quantization, we leverage the generative capacity of diffusion models to recover fine-grained atomic geometry beyond deterministic decoding from discrete tokens. Extensive experiments across small molecules and proteins demonstrate that ADT achieves strong reconstruction from compact discrete representations while enabling high-quality autoregressive generation of both small molecules and all-atom protein structures. These results establish compact structural tokens as an effective discrete interface for all-atom molecular reconstruction and generation.

articles.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence. Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence. We study per-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full-memory behavior. To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural-language decisions, and exact sufficient-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost-ordered group-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records. On 6,912 exact conditions, cost-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum-cost sufficient set in 100.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30.00 to 11.13 (62.9%), and achieves 87.8% active-memory savings. Across four 12B-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10.28 versus 16.00 model queries and 50.6% versus 43.1% minimum-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion. Both methods preserve full-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface. Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior. JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment-ready memory compression.

articles.title: GRAFT-EEG: Gauge-Aware Physical Field Transport for Cross-Dataset Motor-Imagery EEG
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-dataset EEG decoding often treats montage, reference, and active-sensor changes as representation shift, although they also alter the observation operator. We study target-statistics-blind transfer: fitting receives no target signal, label, or empirical statistic, and electrode coordinates only instantiate a fixed prediction operator. method removes the active-set common-reference gauge and transports each native mask through a template motor leadfield. A source-fitted spectral classifier anchors the decision; a bounded state-space-model (SSM) residual is secondary. We establish restricted identifiability and an operator-perturbation bound. Across five leave-one-dataset-out targets (253 participants), dynamic method achieved 60.865% equal-target balanced accuracy versus 52.684% for strict-clean 5/5 BIOT (hierarchical difference +8.182 points; 95% CI +6.382 to +10.196; positive in every target). On four EEGPT-clean targets, the descriptive means were 61.520% and 59.057%. In four post-hoc exact same-parent tests, FULL exceeded coordinate-basis, matched-spectrum, row-shuffled, and wrong-anatomy controls by 9.959, 9.698, 11.241, and 3.985 points, respectively (all 95% CIs excluded zero; Holm-adjusted P<0.001). A separate 60-participant same-paradigm evaluation retained a positive physical-operator contrast (+4.029 points; +2.338 to +5.773), whereas dynamic--static was inconclusive; its preregistered status is partial confirmation rather than unrestricted external validation. The SSM added +1.059 points (+0.013 to +1.892). Claims remain bounded to five binary motor-imagery domains and the tested operators.

articles.title: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages. We propose TriRouter, an electrode-space routing framework with discriminative-preservation, mask-robustness, and latent-compensation paths. A validation-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness. In BNCI2014-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic-spatial-filtering corrupted-EEG baseline. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68, 4.02, and 6.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low-channel dataset evaluation.

articles.title: Tool Recommendation for Multi-Step Agents: Finding Every Tool a Task Needs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multi-step agent task fails when a single tool it needs is missing, yet the tools an agent may need are too many to list: the roughly 8,200 tools on the platform we study have definitions that together exceed the context window of any model we evaluate. We present Tool Recommendation, a deployed system that gives an agent all of them, hundreds of times more than a typical MCP server exposes, through a fixed interface of three tools. It runs at the gateway between agent and tools, executing every call under the end user's own credentials and checking it against the user's consent for each service and the tools the agent may use. We evaluate it on both a public retrieval benchmark and billed end-to-end session cost. On ToolRet, Tool Recommendation places every tool a query needs in the top ten 57% more often than BM25, a lexical ranking that commercial tool search offers, and compares favorably with published systems up to nine times its size. In paired multi-step workflows, its first recommendation covered every required tool in 93% of Codex sessions, and against a fixed list of 100 tools it cut input tokens by 17% with Codex and 40% with Claude Code and the total bill in all 14 runs, by up to 40%, with no change in task completion.

articles.title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions on short-answer question answering in four MoE families. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly. In Qwen3-30B-A3B this loss is made at the two chat-template tokens before the answer, and in DeepSeek-V2-Lite at the first 8-32 prompt tokens, where its instruction sits; by answer likelihood these positions account for about half and a fifth of the damage. Reduction changes the first token's attention mass, norm and largest activation by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most about a quarter of the loss, well below keeping the sensitive positions full. On real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts, placing them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while placing them at random in the documents is about 3 points worse (two of five prespecified primary comparisons; the others were undecided or not run). Because the answer boundary always ends a single-turn prompt, and DeepSeek's loss was no longer detectable once its instruction moved away from the start, the sensitive tokens lay at the prompt ends in every sensitive layout we found, so rules that keep the ends are not distinguished from rules that read application marks. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts and not at 2K tokens.

articles.title: Explaining Chess and Go in Natural Language
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern chess engines play far beyond human ability, often choosing moves whose underlying ideas are difficult for humans to understand. We propose an automatic metric for evaluating chess explanations, grounded in chess-engine evaluations. Evaluating state-of-the-art language models using this metric, we find that they perform surprisingly poorly, often relying on surface-level board observations rather than robust, transferable chess concepts. We then introduce BinProp, a training-free method that enables these same models to discover reusable chess concepts and use them to explain moves in natural language. BinProp improves explainability for every model tested, nearly tripling the average score compared with direct prompting. Beyond chess, the same method discovers useful concepts in Go, draughts, and shogi without additional tuning.

articles.title: Managed stratospheric aerosol injection phaseout under deep carbon removal: cross-model and aerosol-lifetime sensitivity
articles.abstract: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) has been proposed as a temporary complement to mitigation and carbon dioxide removal (CDR), but safe withdrawal depends on how rapidly greenhouse forcing falls and on the dynamics of the aerosol actuator. We execute one prespecified annual feedback controller separately in FaIR 2.2.4 and Hector 3.5.0 under matched future non-CO₂ forcing and a deliberately deep CDR stress-test pathway. In a two-layer energy-balance emulator of the SAI response, we then add a first-order aerosol-forcing reservoir with 0.67, 1.0 and 1.5 year e-folding times, spanning the approximately 8-month to 1.5-year sulfur lifetimes reported across four G6-1.5K-SAI Earth system models. Across 1,500 aerosol-lifetime-by-plant tests, median 2060 temperature is 1.200–1.206°C, no trajectory reaches the 3.5 W m⁻² command ceiling, and none of 1,192 trajectories with complete 20-year post-phaseout windows has a positive temperature trend. Phaseout emerges from the feedback law; a CO₂-indexed command ceiling never binds. FaIR and Hector temperature trajectories remain close while their long-horizon CO₂ endpoints diverge. These results show that, conditional on sustained deep CDR, no complete experiment in the tested reduced-complexity models and forcing-persistence assumptions produced a positive 20-year post-phaseout temperature trend. Regional hydrology, aerosol microphysics, ozone chemistry and governance remain outside the validated scope.

articles.title: Calibration-Free, Nanometer-Scale Single-Molecule Localization with MINFLUX and RASTMIN via Direct Minimum Fitting
articles.abstract: Ultraprecise super-resolution fluorescence microscopy techniques such as MINFLUX and RASTMIN achieve single-digit nanometer-scale localization precision of single molecules by probing them with a minimum of light. Their standard analysis pipelines rely on maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) combined with prior calibration of the excitation profile, imposing significant experimental complexity and sensitivity to imperfections. Here, we introduce a calibration-free localization framework for these methods based on direct fitting of photon-position arrays using physically motivated point spread function models. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we show that direct fitting—particularly with a donut-based model—achieves localization precision approaching the Cramér–Rao lower bound and closely matches MLE performance over a wide range of photon counts. Experimental validation using RASTMIN measurements on single emitters confirms that, at ≥ 1000 detected photons, calibration-free fitting yields localization precision indistinguishable from MLE while maintaining nanometer-scale accuracy. We further demonstrate that incorporating modest model flexibility enables robustness against realistic optical aberrations and accurate reconstruction of spatial patterns. These results establish direct fitting as a simple and robust alternative to calibration-dependent approaches, providing a more practical route toward high-precision photon-efficient single-molecule localization using minima of light.

articles.title: Indoor Air Quality and Thermal Environment Across Three Leather Footwear Facilities in Agra India
articles.abstract: Field evidence on indoor air quality and thermal environment from small-scale Indian manufacturing remains scarce, particularly for leather footwear. We monitored particulate matter, carbon dioxide (CO2), formaldehyde, volatile organic compounds, temperature, humidity, and air velocity across three leather footwear facilities of differing scale and ventilation in Agra, India, over 27 months (608 sessions). Two-way ANOVA (facility by season) showed between-facility differences dominated variance for every parameter (partial eta-squared 0.10–0.87); mean PM2.5, CO2, formaldehyde and volatile organics were 2.0-, 1.9-, 3.0- and 3.5-fold higher in the cottage than organized facility. Season dominated particulate matter and thermal variables but not gas-phase pollutants, tracking ventilation rather than climate. Indoor/outdoor PM2.5 ratios rose from 0.48 to 1.00 across facilities, and CO2 exceeded the ASHRAE ventilation threshold in 99.5% of cottage sessions versus 0% in the organized facility. As one facility represents each tier, these associations are hypothesis-generating, not evidence of a general scale effect.

articles.title: Plasma-Activated Water and Oregano Essential Oil Nanoliposomes Integrated into a Hydroxyethyl Cellulose Coating for Microbial Control of Seafood
articles.abstract: Plasma-activated water (PAW) is a promising non-thermal antimicrobial system for food preservation, but the limited persistence of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) can restrict its prolonged activity on food surfaces. This study developed a hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC)-based active coating integrating PAW-derived RONS with oregano essential oil nanoliposomes (OEONL) for microbial control of seafood. Among the tested HEC concentrations, 3% (w/v) provided the most favorable balance of water uptake, water retention, and RONS persistence. OEONL exhibited a mean particle size of 102.31 ± 1.46 nm and an encapsulation efficiency of 79.31 ± 2.86%. Nanoliposomal incorporation produced a more homogeneous coating microstructure while largely preserving the principal chemical features of HEC. Incorporation of OEONL also enhanced DPPH radical-scavenging activity in a sample-mass- and extraction-time-dependent manner. In seafood challenge tests, the PAH-OEONL coating suppressed total viable counts (TVC), Vibrio parahaemolyticus, and Salmonella in shrimp meat and golden pompano fillets at both 4 and 25°C. At 4°C, it delayed TVC from reaching 7 log CFU/g from approximately day 6 to day 16 in shrimp meat and from day 4 to day 14 in golden pompano fillets, representing a delay of approximately 10 days relative to uncoated controls. Antimicrobial activity also remained evident at 25°C. These findings demonstrate that combining PAW-derived reactive species with nanoliposome-delivered OEO provides a promising active-coating strategy for microbial control of seafood under different storage temperatures.

articles.title: Baseline radiological assessment of soils in an active limestone mining environment in Ibese southwestern Nigeria
articles.abstract: Industrial limestone mining can alter the natural distribution of naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM) through excavation, blasting, crushing, and dust generation, making baseline radiological characterization essential for environmental surveillance and occupational radiation protection. However, baseline radiological data for active limestone mining environments in Nigeria remain limited. This study established the baseline radiological characteristics of surface soils from the Ibese limestone mining area, Ogun State, southwestern Nigeria. Thirty surface soil samples were systematically collected from active quarry sites, transition zones, and neighbouring residential areas. Samples were prepared following International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) protocols and analysed for ⁴⁰K, ²³⁸U, and ²³²Th activity concentrations using NaI(Tl) gamma-ray spectrometry. Radiological hazard parameters, including Raeq, Hex, Hin, absorbed dose rate, AEDE, ELCR, AGED, and Iγ, were evaluated. Mean activity concentrations of ⁴⁰K, ²³⁸U, and ²³²Th were 485.47 ± 195.75, 11.07 ± 8.11, and 19.37 ± 9.85 Bq kg⁻¹, respectively. While ⁴⁰K exceeded the global average reported by UNSCEAR, ²³⁸U and ²³²Th were below worldwide reference values. The mean values of Raeq (76.14 Bq kg⁻¹), Hex (0.206), Hin (0.236), absorbed dose rate (37.05 nGy h⁻¹), AEDE (0.045 mSv y⁻¹), and Iγ (0.591) were all below internationally recommended limits, indicating negligible radiological risk. Correlation analysis identified ²³²Th as the principal contributor to absorbed dose rate and most radiological hazard indices, whereas ⁴⁰K predominantly influenced AGED variability. Overall, the Ibese limestone mining environment presents no immediate radiological concern for quarry workers or nearby residents. This study provides one of the first baseline radiological datasets for an active industrial limestone mining environment in Nigeria, supporting future environmental monitoring, occupational radiation protection, and NORM management.

articles.title: Heme-oxygenase-1 (HO-1) in CCR2/CCL2/CD200 brain mononuclear cells contribute to neuroinflammation in young adulthood after chorioamnionitis
articles.abstract: Chemokine receptor 2+ (CCR2+) mediates peripheral mononuclear cell infiltration into the brain via its ligand C motif ligand 2 (CCL2), whereas Immune inhibitory ligand CD200, suppresses mononuclear cell activation. Whether sustained alterations in CCR2/CCL2/CD200-expressing mononuclear cell populations and their Heme-oxygenase-1 (HO-1) expression contribute to persistent neuroinflammation following perinatal chorioamnionitis (CHORIO) remains unknown. We hypothesized that HO-1 expression within CCR2/CCL2/CD200 mononuclear cell subsets is altered in adulthood following perinatal CHORIO compared with sham controls. Brains were collected at postnatal day (P) 21 and P60 (n = 6–8/group), dissociated and surface and intracellular markers used to identify inflammatory and oxidative mononuclear cell subsets with flow cytometry. At P60, CHORIO brains exhibited fewer CCR2+CD11bcL/INT cells (p = 0.008), increased intracellular HO-1 expression, (p = 0.01) and a reciprocal increase in CCR2-CD11bcL/INT cells (p = 0.008). In addition, CCL2+/CCR2+CD11bcL/INT (p = 0.04) and CD200+/CCR2+CD11bcL/INT (p = 0.005) ratios were also increased in CHORIO. HO-1 expression in CCR2+CD11bcL/INT cells was lower at P21 than at P60, suggesting an age-dependent phenotypic shift after CHORIO. Here we demonstrate that alterations in CCR2/CCL2/CD200 signaling and HO-1 expression in adult brain mononuclear cells following perinatal CHORIO are sustained, suggesting long-term inflammatory and oxidative immune signaling that may contribute to chronic neuroinflammation.

articles.title: Estimating Evapotranspiration Using the SEBAL Model and Remote Sensing: Spatiotemporal Dynamics in Quara District, Northwest Ethiopia
articles.abstract: Evapotranspiration (ET) is a fundamental component of the hydrological cycle that simultaneously integrates interactions between land surface, vegetation, and atmospheric systems through the combined processes of evaporation and transpiration. This is especially critical in arid and semi-arid regions such as Quara District in northwest Ethiopia, where water resources are scarce and precise quantification of actual water consumption is essential for sustainable water management. This study applies the Surface Energy Balance Algorithm for Land (SEBAL) model using Landsat-8 OLI/TIRS remote sensing imagery acquired during the dry season of 2020 (January, February, March, and April) to estimate actual evapotranspiration (ET) across the Quara District. The SEBAL model computes ET as a residual of the surface energy balance equation, requiring estimation of net radiation (Rₙ), soil heat flux (G₀), and sensible heat flux (H). The results reveal ET₂₄ values ranging from 0.68 mm/day to 9.63 mm/day across the four acquisition dates, with pronounced spatial and temporal variability driven by differences in land cover type, soil moisture, and vegetation density. The methodology demonstrates that satellite-based energy balance models offer a robust, spatially explicit alternative to traditional ground-based methods for ET estimation in data-scarce environments. The findings underscore the value of integrating remote sensing and GIS techniques for operational water resources management in semi-arid landscapes.

articles.title: A receptor and chaperone that influences lung MAIT cell number, function, and lung inflammation
articles.abstract: Innate-like T cells are tissue-resident lymphocytes, but the factors that govern their localization to specific tissues, at steady state or after infections, are not well defined.  Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are an innate-like T cell population that is relatively frequent in the lungs of mice and humans.  Receptor activity-modifying protein 3 (RAMP3) is a member of a family of three proteins that modulate the expression and function of several GPCRs, including those involved in immune responses.  Despite this, the role of RAMP3 in T cell immunity has not been widely explored. We found that Ramp3–/– mice had increased lung MAIT cells at steady-state or after infection, while other T cell populations were less affected. Ramp3–/– mice had increased surface CXCR6 expression, and RAMP3 overexpression reduced CXCR6. CXCR6 was required for the dramatic increase in lung MAIT cells after infection. These data suggest that RAMP3 negatively regulated CXCR6 and limited lung MAIT cell numbers. This has important consequences, because infected Ramp3–/– mice had increased IL-17A-secreting lung MAIT cells, but were more susceptible to pulmonary infection, with reduced bacterial clearance, increased cellular infiltration, and immunopathology.  The increase in lung MAIT cells after infection occurred predominantly from cells located in the tissue, but in Ramp3–/– mice there was evidence for some recruitment to the lung. We have established that RAMP3 is a negative regulator of excessive lung MAIT cell responses, acting in part through CXCR6.

articles.title: Engine Emission and Noise Reduction Using Organic Waste-based Activated Carbon Filters: A Case Study on Motorcycles
articles.abstract: The increasing number of motorcycles in developing countries such as Indonesia has intensified air and noise pollution, while large quantities of agricultural waste remain underutilized. This study investigates the feasibility of converting agricultural residues into activated carbon filters for simultaneous reduction of motorcycle exhaust emissions and noise. Activated carbon filters were fabricated from three abundant biomass wastes, namely peanut shells, palm fiber, and durian peels, and installed on a 110 cc motorcycle exhaust system. The effects of biomass precursor and chemical activating agents (H₃PO₄, KOH, and NaCl) on carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (CO₂), hydrocarbon (HC), and exhaust noise were experimentally evaluated under idle operating conditions. The results demonstrate that all biomass-derived activated carbon filters reduced exhaust emissions and noise compared with the unfiltered exhaust. Peanut shell-based activated carbon exhibited the highest performance for reducing CO and HC emissions, whereas durian peel-derived activated carbon achieved the greatest reduction in CO₂ emissions. Among the investigated activating agents, KOH produced the highest adsorption performance owing to its ability to generate a more developed porous carbon structure. In addition, palm fiber-based activated carbon provided the greatest reduction in exhaust noise due to its porous acoustic-damping properties. These findings demonstrate that agricultural waste-derived activated carbon can serve as a low-cost and environmentally sustainable alternative for simultaneous exhaust emission control and noise attenuation, while promoting the valorization of agricultural residues within a circular economy framework.

articles.title: Recovering What Breaks in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulation of a Lattice Gauge Theory
articles.abstract: A recent trapped-ion experiment realised a lattice gauge theory with the gauge field in the internal states of the ions and bosonic matter in their vibrations. We showed earlier that its noise damage can be predicted. Here, we show that most of it can be undone. The conservation law of the theory is a parity of each vibrational mode, which heating flips, so a heating event leaves a mark that can be read without disturbing the physics. We keep only the runs in which this mark never changed. With equal heating rates and continuous monitoring, the kept runs reproduce the heating-free dynamics exactly, with a closed-form yield. Reading the mark at finite intervals introduces a small bias linear in the interval, which we derive and bound. At the reported rates, a single final check removes most of the heating and preparation damage while accepting eight runs out of ten.

articles.title: Experimental and Regression Analysis of Prism and Reflector- Less Edm Measurements Under Variable Field Conditions Using Leica TS16p1R500 Total Station
articles.abstract: Electronic Distance Measurement (EDM) is widely applied to carry out topographic surveys and study landforms, land use, river geomorphic change detection, construction layout, dynamic bridge deformations, and documenting the culture heritage. In order to ensure the results of surveying according to the requirements of a particular project, it is important to know the reliability and accuracy of surveying instruments. The achievable accuracy will depend on the instrument used, atmospheric conditions in the line of measurement, and the target employed. In this study, an analysis of prism and reflector-less EDM measurement data based on statistics through a regression approach has been conducted using a Leica TS16 robotic total station. The experimental investigation considered multiple influencing parameters, including prism type, target material, target color, incidence angle, and weather conditions. Statistical analysis was performed using mean error, root mean square error, and regression-based error modeling to examine the relationship between measurement error and observation distance. The results demonstrate that prism-based measurements provide superior accuracy, exceeding reflector-less measurements by approximately 21.77%, particularly at longer distances. Circular prisms exhibited the highest precision, with errors remaining within the millimeter level, while reflector-less measurements showed increased sensitivity to surface properties, incidence angle, and atmospheric variations. Results from regression analysis indicated that prism readings showed consistency with the specified accuracy from the manufacturer across the range of interest, while the reflector-less method displayed increasing discrepancies, especially when atmospheric and geometrical conditions were poor.

articles.title: Ca-Doped BaCeO₃ Nanoperovskites for Enhanced Photocatalytic Degradation and Electrochemical Detection of Trimethoprim
articles.abstract: Calcium-doped barium cerate (Ca–BaCeO₃) nanoperovskites were synthesized via a facile sol–gel method and investigated as dual-functional materials for environmental and electrochemical applications. The synthesized nanoparticles exhibited a direct optical band-gap of 2.1 eV, indicating their suitability for visible-light-driven applications. Photocatalytic activity was evaluated for the degradation of trimethoprim (TMP) under sunlight irradiation, achieving approximately 96% degradation under optimized conditions of 0.7 g L⁻¹ catalyst dosage, 35 ppm TMP concentration, pH 7, and 40 °C. The enhanced photocatalytic performance was attributed to improved charge separation and reduced electron–hole recombination resulting from Ca doping. Electrochemical sensing of TMP was investigated using cyclic voltammetry, where the modified electrode exhibited a linear response with a sensitivity of 0.5 mA µM⁻¹ cm⁻². The limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) were determined to be 0.03 µM and 0.09 µM, respectively, demonstrating reliable sensing performance.
