We test this prediction using resistive-GRMHD simulations at several spins and resistivities and find a regime in which the measured late-time secular decay agrees quantitatively with the analytic prediction.

articles.title: Magnetic connectivity from the Sun to the Earth with MHD models II. Impact of input magnetic maps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Connectivity estimation needs to be fast and thus usually relies on semi-empirical models. We previously established that optimised magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) models can also be used to derive magnetic connectivity, yielding good results, especially for complex configurations. However, the modelling is not the only factor that can impact the connectivity estimation. Models' results, both semi-empirical and MHD, depend heavily on the input data used to drive the simulation. In order to quantify this impact on our connectivity estimation, we used 20 different maps by four providers. We selected the period of July 2019, which corresponds to Carrington rotation (CR) number 2219, because it had already been studied in a previous paper. It corresponds to a period of minimum activity, meaning minimal interference from transient structures, but with a high-speed stream and several polarity switches. We have compared our results with in situ data from ACE and developed several visualisation techniques to validate connectivity not only for a specific date but also for a full CR. The choice of the input magnetic map drastically affects the connectivity estimates, with global scores going from 28% global agreement to 63% in the most extreme case. The HMI and GONG maps consistently gave the best connectivity estimations, with more than 50% correct results of the full CR. For this specific period, the GONG-ADAPT maps yielded the least reliable results, with a score below 35%. This is not surprising, as we have shown before that COCONUT required parameter adjustments for these maps. However, WSO maps which showed poor coronal agreement actually provided good connectivity estimates, showing that the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) location is in the end the most crucial parameter for connectivity. Consistent data over a full Carrington rotation are to be favored compared to daily.

articles.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at sqrts = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb⁻¹. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high p_T. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

articles.title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space S² cong SO(3)/SO(2), we lift a spin s field to the rotation group, convolve on SO(3), and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin s'. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.

articles.title: Physics-guided surrogate learning enables zero-shot control of turbulent wings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.09434v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Turbulent boundary layers over aerodynamic surfaces are a major source of aircraft drag, yet their control remains challenging due to multiscale dynamics and spatial variability, particularly under adverse pressure gradients. Reinforcement learning has outperformed state-of-the-art strategies in canonical flows, but its application to realistic geometries is limited by computational cost and transferability. Here we show that these limitations can be overcome by exploiting local structures of wall-bounded turbulence. Policies are trained in turbulent channel flows matched to wing boundary-layer statistics and deployed directly onto a NACA4412 wing section at Re_c=2×10⁵ without additional training on the wing, constituting zero-shot deployment. The transferred policies reduce total drag by 11.1%, while state-of-the-art opposition control reduces it by 8.9%. With the actuation cost taken into account, the corresponding net-energy savings are 10.9% and 8.8%, respectively. Surrogate training provides an estimated improvement of four orders of magnitude in exploration efficiency over direct on-wing training, enabling scalable flow control.

articles.title: Dynamics of fast magnetosonic wave turbulence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.22710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fast magnetosonic waves are among the fundamental oscillation modes of astrophysical plasmas. To study their dynamics, we carry out numerical simulations of the wave turbulence kinetic equation, which describes the evolution of the energy spectrum of a set of weakly nonlinear fast magnetosonic waves. This kinetic equation, which involves three-wave interactions, has recently been derived from compressible magnetohydrodynamics in the low-β limit (Galtier 2023). It has an exact stationary solution, the Kolmogorov-Zakharov spectrum, corresponding to a direct energy cascade. Here we perform free decay simulations of the kinetic equation for which we propose a Kolmogorov-type phenomenology to explain the temporal decay laws of energy and integral length scale. In the forced simulations, we show that the cascade is in fact composed of a mixture of a forward cascade for counter-propagating waves, and a backward cascade for co-propagating waves, with the former being stronger than the latter. The Kolmogorov-Zakharov energy spectrum in k⁻³/² is found in the radial direction with an anisotropy due to the amplitude that depends on the angle relative to the strong mean magnetic field. We give the analytical expression of the Kolmogorov-Zakharov constant, which is numerically verified in the high Reynolds number limit. Our study provides a theoretical explanation for certain observations in the solar wind plasma (Zhao et al. 2022), where a regime of weak turbulence has been identified for fast magnetosonic waves, alongside a critical balance regime for strong Alfvén wave turbulence.

articles.title: Automatic-Differentiation-Enabled Finite Element Model Updating: Learning Constitutive Neural Networks from Structural Deformation Data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.05199v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The identification of constitutive neural network models from heterogeneous full-field deformation data provides a robust alternative to traditional calibration methods based on homogeneous stress-strain experiments, particularly given the high dimensionality of trainable parameters. This work presents ADE-FEMU (Automatic-Differentiation-Enabled Finite Element Model Updating), an end-to-end differentiable framework that integrates a constitutive neural network model within a JAX-FEM nonlinear solver and identifies its parameters through gradient-based minimization of a measurement-mismatch loss, allowing for training on structural data with limited kinetic information. Thus, it can be considered as an extension of finite element model updating (FEMU) for hyperelastic materials, implemented within a GPU-accelerated, fully automatically differentiable finite element framework Newton tangent stiffness and loss gradients are computed automatically using forward- and reverse-mode automatic differentiation throughout the entire pipeline, thereby removing the need for analytic adjoints or offline surrogate models. ADE-FEMU is demonstrated for two architectures: a grey-box Constitutive Artificial Neural Network (CANN), a polyconvex, fully connected model with high flexibility, and a white-box CANN, an expert-system network with phenomenologically interpretable strain-energy terms. Focusing on incompressible isotropic hyperelasticity, ADE-FEMU is evaluated on three open experimental datasets: (1) full digital image correlation (DIC) of a perforated tensile specimen, (2) a reduced-data scenario with a one-dimensional stretch profile and global force-displacement curve, and (3) a heterogeneous matrix-inclusion system in which both phases constitutive laws are identified and generalized to twenty-two previously unseen samples.

articles.title: Detector Performance and Dark Matter Sensitivity of CYGNO with HFO-1234ze Gas Admixtures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.20370v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The CYGNO project develops optical time projection chambers for directional dark matter searches, using a He:CF4 (60:40) gas mixture at atmospheric pressure and a triple-GEM amplification stage. We investigate the addition of 1-10% HFO-1234ze as a hydrogen-containing additive with low global warming potential. The charge response and scintillation light yield are studied with the MANGO prototype, complemented by secondary-scintillation spectroscopy of the baseline mixture and mixtures containing 1% and 2.5% HFO. Increasing the HFO concentration shifts the charge-response curves towards higher GEM voltages and strongly suppresses the scintillation emission in both the ultraviolet and visible bands. We use the measured optical response to estimate the impact on projected spin-independent WIMP-nucleon and spin-dependent WIMP-proton exclusion limits for a CYGNO-like directional detector. Under the assumed detector-response model, the higher optical energy threshold largely outweighs the benefit of the additional light target, although a 1% HFO admixture retains a limited advantage for low-mass spin-dependent interactions. An idealized fixed-threshold benchmark is also considered to illustrate the potential of the modified target composition without the optical threshold penalty.

articles.title: Cosmic rays density fluctuations with turbulence universal spectrum -8/3
articles.abstract: arXiv:2202.04642v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An exact turbulence universal scaling law-8/3 for the density fluctuations of cosmic ray (CR) is obtained on the basis of a new analytical compressible turbulence theory and known two-fluid model of the CR dynamics. It is shown that the origin of this scaling law may be due to the breaking of the nonlinear simple waves in CR medium near the scale of their Larmor radii as for the space plasma of solar wind and magnetosheath.

articles.title: Enhancing Event Reconstruction in Hyper-Kamiokande with Machine Learning: A ResNet Implementation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.13503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The forthcoming Hyper-Kamiokande experiment is expected to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to neutrino oscillations. Meeting these precision goals requires substantially larger Monte Carlo datasets than previous experiments to satisfy stringent systematic-uncertainty requirements. While traditional maximum-likelihood reconstruction provides high-quality event reconstruction, its per-event computational cost makes reconstruction of large, systematically varied Monte Carlo samples increasingly impractical. We demonstrate a neural-network-based reconstruction approach for the Hyper-Kamiokande far detector using simulated data with the experiment's detector geometry. Single-particle events are generated with kinetic energies from the Cherenkov threshold up to 2 GeV above threshold. The resulting PMT charge and timing information are mapped to 274×144 five-channel images that serve as inputs to ResNet models in the WatChMaL framework. These models (i) classify events into four particle hypotheses (e, μ, γ, π⁰) and (ii) regress the interaction vertex, direction, and momentum of electrons and muons. The regression models achieve momentum resolutions of 1.27% for muons and 2.21% for electrons, angular resolutions of 0.91^circ and 1.60^circ, and vertex resolutions of 13.6,cm and 17.0,cm, better than those reported for traditional methods. The classifier improves e-μ, e-γ, and e-π⁰ separation relative to the traditional baseline, with ROC AUC values of 0.9999995, 0.642, and 0.9659. Our networks achieve inference times of 1-2 ms per event on a single GPU, yielding speed-ups of 3.2×10⁴-5.2×10⁴ relative to likelihood-based reconstruction.

articles.title: Certified Bounds on the Measurement Cost of Molecular Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.16866v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum estimates of molecular energy require repeated state preparation and measurement. We bound the minimum repetition count for given measurements and processing rules from above with a practical schedule and from below with independently verified inequalities. For an H₄ chain at H-H distances of 0.90 and 1.80 Å with 2 per cent uniform noise in the ground state, entangling Clifford measurements, which map Pauli products onto one another, cut leading-order repetitions by at least 65.9 and 61.0 per cent, respectively, relative to any schedule using only single-qubit Pauli measurements and Hamiltonian terms. With 69 unaltered measurement settings, each a basis change followed by qubit readout, processing further observables saves at least 12.04 and 6.70 per cent. For four lanthanide and actinide Hamiltonians with depolarized Hartree-Fock covariances, reducing the sum of absolute Hamiltonian coefficients does not proportionally reduce sampling. The bounds cover linear unbiased estimates from independent batches at small error.

articles.title: Beyond Orbital Rotations: Correlation-Rank Limits and Clifford-Accessible Measurement, from Algebra and Global Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.16869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One should not assume that reconstructing an electronic observable with a smaller set of measurement settings will cut the number of repetitions in proportion. Each setting is simply a basis change and qubit readout, but the savings are not guaranteed to be commensurate. Take two electrons of opposite spin in two spatial orbitals: the orbital degree of freedom of each electron acts as a logical qubit and rotations are independent in the spin sectors. From the observable's one- and two-qubit coefficients we derive an exact floor for the setting count and a decomposition to meet it in no more than three settings. With fewer settings, the minimum error in the two-qubit correlation coefficients is set by the singular values left out. A case in point is an exchange with equal nonzero couplings on the three Pauli axes. This demands three orbital settings yet only one joint measurement. We offer a Clifford circuit for four physical qubits to effect the necessary mapping of Pauli products under conjugation. In the case of a one-parameter family of logical singlet-triplet mixtures, the orbital-to-Clifford shot cost ratio is three at maximum mixing and trends toward 3/2 near the logical singlet. Where spin sectors may be mixed, isotropic exchange needs one orbital setting. For spin-conserving Hamiltonians with N spatial orbitals encoded via Jordan-Wigner, the X-rank, the binary rank of the X parts of its strings, of any commuting Pauli string family is no more than 2(N-1). Searches with the Robust Adaptive Nature-inspired Global Explorer (RANGE) reach this limit for CH₄, with the rank of the Hamiltonian support vouching for the maximality of the search values. And for all nonidentity Pauli strings on n qubits, semidefinite witnesses from the Lovász theta number give a lower bound on the Clifford setting count that agrees with the integer cover and counting bounds at 2ⁿ+1.

articles.title: Optimal Calibration-Free Observable for the Nucleon-Coupling Ratio in a Dual-Alkali Comagnetometer for Dark Matter Searches
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.07456v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A dual-alkali single-cell ⁸⁷Rb-³⁹K-³He comagnetometer can read an axion-like dark matter signal through two optical rotation channels, encoding the ratio R=ξₙ/ξₚ of the field's neutron and proton spin couplings in their relative response. The inter-species phase difference Δϕ has been proposed as a calibration-free readout that is sensitive to R. Treating the extraction of R as a statistical estimation problem, we show that the estimate of R depends on the two channels only through their complex ratio, which splits into Δϕ and an amplitude ratio, of which only Δϕ is insensitive to the relative gain and hence calibration free. For our choice of comagnetometer parameters, above sim!100 Hz the phase difference alone captures most of the coupling-ratio information. At lower frequencies Δϕ is no longer near-sufficient. Below sim!40 Hz, the amplitude ratio would improve the precision on R by a factor of gtrsim2. Recovering that information, however, requires the relative gain to be known sufficiently accurately, so Δϕ remains the robust observable even where it is not the most informative one.

articles.title: Efficient Quantum Simulation of Linearized Vlasov--Poisson Dynamics Using Trotter and THRIFT Hamiltonian Simulation Methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.23127v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Vlasov--Poisson system provides the fundamental kinetic description of plasma and plays a central role in understanding collective phenomena such as Landau damping and wave--particle interactions. Efficient numerical simulation of these dynamics remains challenging because of the high dimensionality of phase space. In this work, we studied magnetized and non-magnetized plasma using a quantum simulation framework for the linearized Vlasov-Poisson equation by reformulating the discretized system as a Hermitian Hamiltonian suitable for gate-based quantum computation. The time evolution is implemented using first, second and fourth-order Trotter--Suzuki product formulas and the recently proposed Time-Resolved Interaction Framework (THRIFT). The performance of the different simulation methods is systematically evaluated through electric field evolution, state fidelity, convergence behavior, energy conservation, entanglement entropy and quantum resource requirements, including circuit depth and two-qubit gate complexity, for both magnetized and non-magnetized plasma models. To further reduce finite time step errors without increasing circuit depth, Richardson extrapolation is incorporated as a error-mitigation technique. The results provide a comprehensive comparison of Trotter and THRIFT approaches and establish practical guidelines for accurate and resource-efficient quantum simulation of plasma dynamics on gate-based quantum computers.

articles.title: Behind-the-Meter Photovoltaic Visibility from Net Smart Meters: Deployment Regimes and Operational Insights
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distribution operators need visibility of behind-the-meter photovoltaic (PV) generation, yet most residential customers are observed only through net smart meters. Deep-learning-based PV disaggregation can restore this visibility, but its operational value depends on whether the model serves known customers, new customers, future periods, or new regions. We quantify this dependence using four deployment regimes that separate household transfer from temporal extrapolation, applied to Ausgrid smart-meter data with cross-dataset adaptation to the Pecan Street data. Using a fixed training protocol, we benchmark representative deep sequence architectures for PV disaggregation under regime-matched evaluation. At a fixed 48-hour context length, daylight mean absolute error (MAE) of the best model rises from 0.104~kW on seen households in the future test period to 0.185~kW on unseen households over the same period, and under a fixed training contract the deployment regime explains far more of the error variation than model choice. Under target-domain normalization, fine-tuning on five target-region households reduces source-model transfer error by 28%--36%. Long input windows help known-customer extrapolation, while their new-customer benefits vary by model. These findings suggest regime-matched error budgets, limited target supervision for model adaptation in new regions, and use-case-dependent context selection for energy data analytics.

articles.title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.

articles.title: Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning has become the foundational paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Yet the dominant approach, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), relies on a geometrically degenerate clipping proxy that cannot adapt its resistance to policy shifts, leading to premature clipping and degraded exploration. Subsequent variants alleviate these issues through fragmented and heuristic modifications. We propose Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization (GPPO), a principled and unified framework for understanding and designing LLM RL algorithms through the lens of divergence. We establish a generalized f-divergence trust-region theory with a monotonic performance improvement guarantee, and show that different f-divergences induce distinct geometries and policy update dynamics. We further introduce novel estimator topologies that provide more faithful divergence estimates than the conventional single-sample Monte Carlo estimation. Under this framework, PPO and recent variants such as DAPO, DPPO, and RIPO emerge as special cases, establishing a principled two-dimensional design space of Divergence × Estimator. Extensive experiments on eight competition-level math and coding benchmarks show that both dimensions are critical. The best-performing GPPO instantiation surpasses standard GRPO by up to 50% and 14% on math and coding, delivering SOTA performance.

articles.title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continual post-training faces a dual challenge of acquisition and retention: models must learn new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge. While Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) mitigates this using self-supervision with in-context demonstrations, it relies on strong in-context learning and instruction-following abilities. Consequently, SDFT fails on smaller models critical for low-latency, on-device use. To enable continual learning at smaller scales, we first identify the root cause of failure. We show that poor acquisition and forgetting correlate linearly with the post-trained model's distribution shift, revealing the necessity of in-distribution learning. We thus introduce Synthetic Self-Distillation (SynthSelf), imitating SDFT's in-distribution rewrite by outsourcing the task to a minimally larger, same-family aligner. Coupled with off-policy supervision and rejection sampling, this provides the high-quality supervision small models require without breaking their original distribution. Evaluations spanning 4 acquisition datasets (including a mixture) and 14 retention benchmarks show SynthSelf consistently outperforms 6 methods (including off- and on-policy distillation) across 3 small model scales. Extensive further analyses confirm SynthSelf paves the way toward effective small-model continual learning.

articles.title: PDE-PFN: Prior-Data Fitted Neural PDE Solver
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the success of large language models (LLMs) with broad generalizability and robustness to noisy or unreliable pre-training data, we explore in-context prediction of PDE solution fields using approximate pre-training data. In addition, inspired by the posterior predictive mean-based inference mechanism of the in-context learning in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), we propose PDE-PFN, a prior-data fitted neural solver that approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via in-context learning. PDE-PFN builds on a PFN architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms of Transformer and is pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions generated by physics-informed neural networks, serving as diverse but not necessarily exact priors. Through experiments on a range of two-dimensional PDEs, we demonstrate that PDE-PFN achieves empirical generalization across heterogeneous equations, robustness under noisy priors, and zero-gradient-update in-context inference capability. PDE-PFN achieves competitive or improved predictive accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines while supporting flexible context and query representations.

articles.title: AgentTune: A Unified Training Lifecycle for Tool-Using LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using agents increasingly require a common substrate for building, training, evaluating, distilling, and maintaining agentic systems, yet existing tooling typically addresses these stages in isolation. We present AgentTune, a source-available Python library that provides a unified framework for developing and optimizing tool-using agents. At its core, AgentTune introduces a two-tier EventLog representation that preserves agent trajectories while supporting consistent projections for training, evaluation, and auditing. Building on this substrate, the library provides a shared agent runtime, tool-calling reinforcement learning, agentic distillation, retrieval-augmented generation, decision workflows, evaluation utilities, and a designed path toward self-healing agents. These components are exposed through composable interfaces so that agent strategies, training methods, evaluation procedures, and recovery mechanisms can be combined without requiring separate representations or pipelines. We demonstrate the framework across agentic tasks including legal contract search and domain-specific applications, illustrating its use for trajectory-based optimization, tool-use evaluation, and cross-task agent development. AgentTune is released as a source-available library at https://github.com/Lexsi-Labs/AgentTune

articles.title: Probabilistic Ship Trajectory Forecasting using Transformer Models on AIS Data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time. This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated. Historical information on how other vessels have moved in the local area surrounding each agent is conveyed using positional heat maps. The heat maps are generated using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and encoded with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) before entering the Transformer models. The models are trained with quantile loss to efficiently obtain a model-aware prediction interval, as this is crucial for timely collision avoidance. The proposed model architectures are shown to greatly outperform previous work while the inclusion of local heat maps enables the prediction of vessel movement that is not otherwise indicated from the previous positions.

articles.title: L₀ Feature Selection via Monte Carlo Tree Search in High-Dimensional Financial Regression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feature selection is a central problem in high-dimensional financial regression, where large numbers of engineered variables and strong correlations among predictors reduce model stability and interpretability. L₁ regularization (Lasso) is widely used for sparse regression, but its shrinkage can be restrictive when informative signals are spread across correlated variables. Exact sparse regression avoids this shrinkage but requires solving a combinatorial optimization problem that is computationally difficult and is typically fit to minimize in-sample rather than out-of-sample error. This paper presents a feature selection framework based on Monte Carlo Tree Search with Generalized Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation (GNRPA). Feature selection is formulated as a sequential decision process, and candidate subsets are scored by their out-of-sample validation performance rather than training error. The method also supports a lexicographic objective accounting for subset size and multicollinearity. We study this approach on a contemporaneous explanatory regression task: explaining the weekly return of the NASDAQ-100 index from 1,072 engineered features spanning market, macroeconomic, and factor data. This isolates the value of subset selection under multicollinearity from the separate problem of predictive forecasting. On this task, the proposed method identifies sparse feature subsets with higher out-of-sample explanatory power than an optimized Lasso baseline, reaching an out-of-sample R² of 0.6961 versus 0.6313 for Lasso. These results suggest that Monte Carlo Tree Search is a practical alternative to convex regularization for sparse explanatory feature selection in financial regression, with potential value for factor attribution and risk decomposition where transparency matters as much as out-of-sample fit.

articles.title: VQIL: Visible Quantum Interference Learning for Perturbation Response Ranking on Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning how local perturbations affect a network is important for identifying which components drive or absorb a system's response. We formulate this as seed-conditioned response ranking: given a perturbation at one seed node, ranking all other nodes by response strength. This is challenging when the model is given only the interaction topology, while the mechanism governing how perturbations propagate must be learned from data. We present VQIL (Visible Quantum Interference Learning), a trainable Szegedy quantum walk for seed-conditioned ranking. Edge weights, link phases, and per-node phase rotations are optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while the walk operator remains unitary throughout training. Node scores are obtained from a geometrically discounted coherent sum of quantum-walk amplitudes, enabling quantum interference before the final squared-norm readout. Because each learned parameter is attached to a named edge or node, the trained model provides directly inspectable hypotheses about the roles of individual graph components in the propagation mechanism. On AC power-flow perturbations over six transmission grids, with electrical parameters withheld from the model, VQIL improves Spearman rank correlation from 0.147 for the untrained walk to 0.831 and outperforms an identically trained random-walk model. On gene perturbation over five protein-protein interaction networks with Perturb-seq supervision, VQIL improves rank correlation from 0.171 to 0.620, outperforming the strongest learned classical and neural baselines. These results show that trainable quantum-walk interference provides a scalable and interpretable inductive bias for learning seed-conditioned response rankings on graphs.

articles.title: Specialists Learn Faster: Knowledge Organization in Pre-training Shapes Knowledge Update Efficiency
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An ideal (language) model must continually update its knowledge. Existing work largely focuses on making these updates efficient after training. We investigate how the organization of time-varying knowledge during pre-training shapes the efficiency of subsequent updates. Models trained on chronologically ordered knowledge specialize in the most recently encountered knowledge; we call them specialists. In contrast, models trained on the same knowledge in randomly shuffled order perform well across all represented time periods; we call them generalists. Surprisingly, specialists require far fewer update steps than generalists to acquire new knowledge. To explain this advantage, we derive a law from first principles that relates update cost to the model's optimization dynamics and that closely predicts empirical results. Guided by these findings, we design a strategy for organizing pre-training data that preserves stable historical knowledge while enabling efficient updates to current knowledge. We also show that the benefits of temporal knowledge organization extend to real-world pre-trained models and existing knowledge update tools, and generalize to other knowledge orderings. Project page: https://horizon-lab.org/specialist/

articles.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training on a small chemical reaction prediction task - a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

articles.title: Neuromorphic Satellite Intelligence: A Formal Framework for Event-Driven Architectures, Spike-Based Algorithms, and Quantitative Energy-Accuracy Trade-offs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Satellite onboard computing faces an irreducible tension: mission intelligence requirements grow monotonically while power, mass, and radiation budgets remain fixed. This paper advances the state of the art on three fronts. First, we develop a formal mathematical model of spiking neural computation for satellite workloads, deriving closed-form expressions for energy consumption as a function of network sparsity, firing rate, and synaptic fan-out. Second, we propose three original algorithms -- a Spiking Kalman-Complementary Filter (SKCF) for attitude estimation, a Temporal Contrast Anomaly Detector (TCAD) for spacecraft health monitoring, and a Spike-Based Adaptive Modulation and Coding (SAMC) scheme for cognitive satellite links -- each with pseudocode and analytical complexity bounds. Third, we introduce a quantitative Energy-Accuracy-Latency (EAL) trade-off surface and populate it with numerical estimates derived from published silicon measurements of Loihi and SpiNNaker, enabling direct comparison with FPGA and GPU baselines. A taxonomy of four radiation-aware neuromorphic architecture classes is refined with fault-rate models. Continual on-orbit learning is formalized through a constrained Spike-Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP) rule that provably bounds weight drift. Case studies for a 12U CubeSat Earth observation mission, a GEO communications payload, and an autonomous deep-space probe provide concrete, quantified design points. Our analysis shows that neuromorphic implementations can achieve 8 to 47 times energy reduction over GPU baselines while maintaining inference accuracy within 2.1% for representative satellite workloads.

articles.title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities. We propose Product Monte Carlo (PMC), an algorithm for computing arbitrary expectations under a product of densities using only Monte Carlo draws from individual densities. We turn the intractable product expectation into a regression problem by expressing it through a family of computable conditional expectations. Besides the point estimate, our fully Bayesian regression formulation provides coherent uncertainty quantification and principled diagnostics. We establish theoretical guarantees on consistency and characterize convergence rates for the PMC estimator. Across simulated and real-data experiments varying the number, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of the component distributions, PMC achieves higher estimation accuracy, better-calibrated uncertainty coverage, and improved scalability at a lower computational cost than existing methods. In addition, PMC requires no density evaluation, making it applicable to simulation-based inference, as we demonstrate in an application with protein images.

articles.title: Trainable Quantum-Native Language Models: Dissipative Memory, Capacity Limits, and Hardware Validation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study byte-level autoregressive language models whose hidden state is a small quantum register, whose transitions are learned token-conditioned quantum channels, and whose next-byte probabilities come directly from Born-rule measurements without a learned classical vocabulary projection or softmax. In the fixed-width recurrent setting, unitary dynamics cannot contract or reset stored distinctions; experimentally, unitary recurrence loses to its retrained one-token control in every tested variant. Introducing learned dissipation, then token-conditioned dissipative gating, yields useful memory beyond one token. The gated model improves test negative log-likelihood by 0.20 +/- 0.03 nats/byte over retrained parameter-matched one-token controls at context length 12, and by 0.29-0.33 at longer contexts, but never beats retrained two-token controls. A key-value recall benchmark shows a width-dependent threshold: one stored pair meets the pre-registered accuracy bar at 4-5 memory qubits, two pairs at 6-7, and three pairs remain unsolved. This is consistent with, but does not establish, a capacity explanation for the short effective memory horizon. As a secondary result, one-qubit models reach lower stationary memory entropy than a heuristically optimized classical predictive frontier at matched error in 9/9 seeds. On IBM Heron hardware, computational-basis memory-register distributions show signal against a uniform null in 12/12 circuits across prefixes of up to 12 tokens, next-bit probabilities pass pre-registered accuracy bars at four-token prefixes, and bytes are generated autoregressively by sampling physically measured bit probabilities. The tested models are classically simulable and substantially worse than classical n-gram baselines. We claim no computational quantum advantage.

articles.title: Fast Gradient-Based Approximation of Continuous Dynamic Time Warping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is a common choice for measuring the discrepancy between time series. It proceeds by finding an optimal warping between timestamps through dynamic programming, which can be slow and is not differentiable. Consequently, several variants have been proposed. Among them, Soft-DTW proposes a smooth formulation of DTW, amenable to gradient computation, while Continuous-DTW (CDTW) introduces a continuous formulation through parametrizable warping functions. Yet, computational costs remain high for both methods and impractical for large datasets in modern machine learning pipelines. This paper revisits CDTW in several ways. After establishing its differentiability under mild conditions, we introduce FastCDTW, which is an efficient approximate solver with two different computational strategies: an exact closed-form scheme for piecewise-linear warping functions, and an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator for smooth ones, such as implicit neural networks. Both strategies provide gradients with respect to the warping function and the input time series, and the resulting algorithm is GPU-friendly. We demonstrate its benefits through its integration into more complex learning problems, including time series averaging, classification and deep domain adaptation.

articles.title: A Critical Look at Power Sampling when Test Time Sharpening LLMs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved LLM reasoning, yet growing evidence suggests it mainly performs distribution sharpening: concentrating probability mass on reasoning paths the base model already produces. Recent work therefore seeks RLVR's gains without needing reward signals, by sampling from the power distribution π_α propto πbₐₛₑ^α via Markov chain Monte Carlo or sequential Monte Carlo. We show that these samplers fail to converge to π_α under realistic compute budgets, and that their gains are largely recreated via simple Best-of-N with appropriate grading . This suggests they succeed by selecting high-probability sequences, not by approximating π_α, raising a natural question: is the power distribution itself a worthwhile target? We test this hypothesis directly by fine-tuning the base model to match π_α, sidestepping sampler convergence issues entirely. Despite approximating the target far more faithfully than existing samplers, this strategy yields gains that are noisy and specific to certain models and sampling tasks. Together, our results suggest that the value of power sampling lies not in faithfully targeting π_α, but in the simpler goal of extracting sequences the base model already deems likely.

articles.title: Teaching neural decoders with language
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brain-computer interfaces decode neural activity, yet class-label supervision (CLS) leaves relationships among classes implicit. We propose Language as Supervision (LaS), which aligns neural features with natural-language class descriptions through learned projections and predicts classes using candidate text prototypes. We evaluate seven encoder architectures with independently trained models for visual, motor, and speech decoding from scalp and intracranial recordings. LaS improves speech-decoding accuracy by up to 17.15~pp over matched CLS baselines. Its representations support candidate-set reuse and label-supervised subject and session adaptation, while LaS enables conditional unseen-frequency decoding in steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) responses. Correct class-description correspondence supports this generalization, and dual-sided attribution visualization shows neural and textual contributions to the same class-matching score. These findings suggest that text descriptions can serve as general-purpose references for learning and interpretation in neural decoding.

articles.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

articles.title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Actions specify what a robot should execute, but do not describe what those commands will achieve. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies nevertheless learn primarily by predicting action chunks from images, language, and state. We introduce Action--Future Coupled Effect Learning (AFCE), which makes a future-grounded physical Effect the policy's primary prediction target. An offline tokenizer constructs temporally ordered Effect tokens from demonstrated actions, realized robot responses, and sparse visual transitions. Reconstruction objectives encourage the representation to retain executable detail and observed physical change. A flow-matching VLA predicts Effects from current images, instruction, and robot state, while a state-conditioned decoder converts them into action chunks. Embodiment-specific interfaces allow single- and dual-arm tasks to share the Effect model. On DexJoCo, AFCE achieves 50.97% overall success, improving over π₀.₅ and UVT by 11.82 and 15.21 percentage points, respectively. It leads on all five bimanual tasks, highlighting the value of Effect supervision for coordinated dexterous manipulation. The project page is available at https://afceproject.github.io/AFCE-Web/.

articles.title: Conversational versus Dashboard Explainable AI for UAV Intrusion Detection: An Empirical Study of Operator Trust and Reliance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.10434v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have demonstrated superior performance in securing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. However, the 'black-box' nature of these models, combined with the high dimensionality of multimodal cyber-physical data, poses significant interpretability challenges. Static visualization dashboards may struggle to present complex relationships among multimodal cyber-physical features in a form that is easy for operators to inspect and interpret. To address this, we propose a Conversational XAI interface powered by Large Language Models (LLM) to facilitate on-demand investigation. In a controlled experiment with participants, we systematically evaluated the impact of this conversational interface versus a traditional XAI Dashboard on operator understanding, trust, and reliance during post-incident auditing tasks. Our results suggest that the conversational interface was perceived as more useful than the dashboard, potentially because it helped participants access and synthesize relevant information more easily. However, this benefit was accompanied by a lower level of appropriate self-reliance, indicating a potential risk of over-reliance. One possible interpretation is that the natural-language responses made the AI advice easier to accept, which may have reduced participants' tendency to verify the underlying evidence when the IDS was incorrect. These findings point to a potential trade-off in human-AI collaboration for UAV intrusion auditing: interaction mechanisms that improve perceived usability may also increase the risk of inappropriate reliance. We conclude by discussing design implications for future XAI systems that balance seamless interaction with cognitive forcing functions to foster appropriate reliance.

articles.title: Multi-Harness Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents: Training Gains and Harness Dependence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.04518v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent systems train coding agents with reinforcement learning (RL) on trajectories collected through multiple execution harnesses. However, gains under the training harnesses leave open whether the improvements transfer to unseen interfaces and how they depend on reward normalization. We present a controlled study that measures RL gains under fixed harnesses and compares the same models across harnesses. We train two Qwen3-8B RL variants from the same supervised fine-tuning (SFT) checkpoint using identical replay data. They differ only in whether rewards for each task are normalized within each harness (Within) or across harnesses (Cross). On SWE-bench Verified, we identify three main findings: (i) Multi-harness RL yields modest gains over the SFT baseline under both normalization rules. Across the four training harnesses, the estimated mean improvements are +0.48 and +0.77 percentage points for Within and Cross, respectively. (ii) Cross increases the fraction of trajectories with nonzero advantage but provides no consistent advantage over Within on an unseen harness across training seeds and evaluation budgets; neither rule significantly improves over SFT on this harness. (iii) Performance varies substantially more across harnesses than with RL training. After averaging over model variants, the highest and lowest source-harness solve rates differ by 7.13 percentage points, far exceeding the estimated training gains. Even after multi-harness RL, the observed performance differences across execution interfaces remain substantially larger than either the gains from training or the differences between normalization rules.

articles.title: Southward range expansion of Siderastrea spp. into Ilha Grande Bay: evidence of tropicalization in the Southwestern Atlantic
articles.abstract: Climate-driven shifts in marine species distributions are increasingly reshaping coastal ecosystems, yet evidence for the widespread occurrence of tropicalization remains geographically uneven. Tropicalization, characterized by the poleward expansion of tropical species under warming conditions, has been increasingly documented, but its extent and generality across the Atlantic remain poorly understood. Here, we report a contemporary population of Siderastrea spp. in Ilha Grande Bay, Southwestern Atlantic, approximately 230 km south of the previously recognized southern distributional limit of the genus Siderastrea at Arraial do Cabo, Brazil. The occurrence of this population beyond the known southern limit of the genus, within a transitional biogeographic zone between the Tropical and Temperate Atlantic realms, provides an opportunity to examine a contemporary range shift in the context of long-term environmental change. We characterized population occurrence, structure, and associated benthic habitat and evaluated regional sea surface temperature (SST) trends using a 45-year time series. A total of 295 colonies were recorded at Sítio Forte Cove, with a mean density of 11.80 ± 20.24 colonies m⁻². Annual mean SST increased significantly from 1982 to 2025 at a rate of 0.149°C decade⁻¹ (R² = 0.192, p = 0.0029). The contemporary southward occurrence of Siderastrea spp., together with persistent regional warming, is consistent with ongoing tropicalization of the Southwestern Atlantic. This range expansion provides empirical evidence consistent with ongoing tropicalization in a transitional marine region and highlights the potential for continued ocean warming to facilitate the southward redistribution of tropical reef organisms and reshape coastal communities.

articles.title: Distributed Composite Control for Connected Automated Vehicle Platoons: Car- Following Dynamics Based Stability and Robustness Analysis
articles.abstract: Connected automated vehicle (CAV) platoons face two critical engineering challenges: uncertain V2V communication degrades string stability of traffic flow, and unknown external disturbances deteriorate tracking robustness. Single-structured controllers can hardly satisfy both requirements simultaneously. To address this issue, this paper proposes a distributed composite control framework based on car-following dynamics that integrates traffic flow characteristics into platoon control. First, an optimal velocity (OV) based car-following model is established, which incorporates multi-predecessor communication weighting to capture realistic information interaction features in platoon operations. On this basis, a composite controller consisting of a linear compensator and an adaptive integral sliding mode controller (ISMC) is developed. The linear compensator is designed via classical control theory to ensure string stability of the platoon, while the adaptive ISMC is proposed to suppress external disturbances and reduce control chattering. The string stability condition is derived using the long-wavelength approximation method and further verified by the frequency-domain (:Hᵢₙfₜy:) criterion. The finite-time convergence of the sliding mode surface is proved via Lyapunov theory. Both discrete and continuous analyses demonstrate that the proposed adaptive ISMC effectively reduces chattering amplitude and shortens convergence time compared with conventional ISMC. Finally, numerical simulations and intelligent small robot vehicles experiments validate the theoretical analysis, demonstrating the system's effectiveness in maintaining platoon dynamics and its potential application in intelligent transportation systems.

articles.title: Mechanism and Application of Electrical Resistivity Responses in Annular Adsorbed Water Films: Insights From Capillary Theory
articles.abstract: In strongly water-wet low-resistivity oil reservoirs, hydrocarbons can displace most free water, but residual water may still remain as continuous or semi-continuous films on pore walls. These adsorbed water films, together with electrical double-layer and surface-conduction effects, may form effective conductive pathways and cause conventional Archie models to overestimate water saturation. However, the quantitative contribution of adsorbed film water to the resistivity response remains difficult to characterize. This study investigates low-resistivity oil reservoirs in the Lunnan area and develops a pore-scale constrained rock-electrical model for water-saturation evaluation. Lithological, clay-mineral, conductive-mineral, and wettability analyses show that the low-resistivity response is not mainly controlled by clay minerals or conductive minerals. Instead, the evidence points to connected bound-water films developed under strongly water-wet conditions as a major contributor to the anomalous conductivity. On this basis, a thermodynamic relationship between water-film thickness and pore-throat radius is established by balancing Young–Laplace capillary pressure with thin-film disjoining pressure. A coupled high-pressure mercury intrusion and nuclear magnetic resonance method is developed to separate capillary-bound water in fine pore throats from adsorbed film water retained on the walls of larger pores. High-pressure mercury intrusion constrains the pore-throat structure and the capillary-controlled immobile-water volume, whereas nuclear magnetic resonance provides the total bound-water saturation after centrifugation. The difference between the NMR-derived total bound water and the HPMI-constrained capillary-bound water is then used to quantify the adsorbed film-water content and invert an interfacial thermodynamic constant. Dynamic resistivity experiments are further incorporated to establish an electrical-double-layer-enhanced dual-network conductivity model and determine the conductivity enhancement ratio and cutoff exponent. The proposed model explains the persistently low resistivity index observed at low water saturation and shows good agreement with oil-test interpretations when applied to logging data. This study provides a physically constrained approach for water-saturation evaluation in strongly water-wet low-resistivity reservoirs.

articles.title: Screening, Identification and Statistical Optimization of Peroxidase from Bacillus rugosus JBP20: A Microbial Biocatalyst Approach
articles.abstract: Background: Peroxidases are oxidoreductase enzymes. They have an important role in bioremediation and environmental biotechnology due to their ability to degrade a broad range of pollutants. This study aimed to isolate, identify, and optimize a peroxidase-producing bacterium from industrially contaminated samples collected from Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC), Vatva, Ahmedabad. Results: Out of all the isolates screened, strain JBP20 had the highest extracellular peroxidase activity (0.21 U/mL). The isolate was identified as Bacillus rugosus by molecular identification done by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. It is phylogenetically similar to Bacillus rugosus SPB7. The effect of different physical and nutritional parameters on the enzyme production was investigated in a systematic manner. Enzyme activity was optimum at 24 h old (8%), pH 8.0, and an incubation temperature of 37°C using dextrose and peptone as the choice of carbon and nitrogen sources, respectively. Additional optimization with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) indicated high interrelationships among the chosen variables, and the quadratic model created demonstrated the high predictive capabilities (Adj. R2 = 0.9336; Pred. R2 = 0.8204). Reaction conditions were optimized and giving a maximum peroxidase activity with OPD (0.5%), H2O2 (0.7 mL), enzyme volume (0.2 mL), and the presence of Fe2+ ions was observed to significantly increase enzyme activity. In optimized conditions, the production of peroxidase has improved, and the highest activity was 0.38 U/mL. Conclusion: The results suggest that Bacillus rugosus JBP20 is a promising microbial source for peroxidase production. This finding supports the potential application of Bacillus rugosus JBP20 in bioremediation and environmental biotechnology.

articles.title: Quantum Bayesian Neural Network for Uncertainty-Aware ECG Anomaly Detection
articles.abstract: This study develops a Quantum Bayesian Neural Network for electrocardiogram anomaly detection by integrating multi-scale feature engineering, variational quantum learning, Bayesian parameter modelling, and physical quantum hardware evaluation. Using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the proposed pipeline applies leakage-safe preprocessing, record-adaptive multi-window analysis, dependency-aware feature construction, and robust feature selection before quantum encoding. Angle and Dense-Angle encoding are systematically evaluated across four- and six-qubit circuits, two and four variational layers, and configurations with and without data re-uploading. Bayesian inference is incorporated by representing quantum parameters probabilistically and estimating posterior predictive anomaly probabilities through repeated parameter sampling. Among the evaluated configurations, Dense-Angle encoding with six qubits, four layers, and data re-uploading provides the strongest overall probabilistic perfor- mance, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.91, an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.90, recall of 0.88, and a Brier score of 0.13. A compact four-qubit Dense-Angle model is additionally executed on the IBM Marrakesh quantum processor to investigate predictive consistency under physical quantum noise. These results demonstrate that quantum encoding density, circuit architecture, data re-uploading, and Bayesian inference jointly influence anomaly-detection performance and provide a practical foundation for uncertainty-aware quantum learning for electrocardiogram analysis.

articles.title: Practical implementation of a Safe-by-Design framework: a proof of concept for early-phase hazard assessment of PFAS-free formulations
articles.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in various industrial sectors for their thermal stability, chemical resistance and surface-active properties. However, these same characteristics also contribute to their environmental persistence, potential for accumulation and adverse health effects, triggering increasing scrutiny across product life cycles. Within the EU-funded project PROPLANET, a tiered and iterative Safe-by-Design methodology was applied to PFAS-free coatings being developed for technical textiles, metal elements of food-packaging machinery and low-maintenance glass applications, at technology readiness levels (TRL) 3–5. The approach combined regulatory data mining, in silico screening and in vitro testing to identify potential hazard concerns and inform formulation-development decisions, while accounting for technical-performance requirements. Data mining from Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and the ECHA CHEM database were used to identify and exclude known harmful substances, including carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic (CMR) compounds and substances of very high concern (SVHCs), during the early stages of formulation development. Data-gap analysis indicated that the existing in silico models applied had insufficient coverage of the chemical space relevant to the substances under investigation, encouraging the development of custom-trained models. Two-tiered in vitro testing further characterized the toxicity profiles of several formulations throughout the project. One formulation intended for textile applications showed no hazard alerts under the tested conditions, whereas the formulations intended for glass and metal applications raised potential hazard concerns, requiring further investigation before progression to higher TRLs. This study presents the practical implementation of the Safe-by-Design methodology and the main results and inputs for decision making. At the same time, the practical challenges encountered during the implementation of the approach are discussed, together with the methodological gaps and grey areas. In conclusion, the structured, tiered and iterative approach implemented in this study supports the screening and prioritization of candidate chemicals and formulations in the early stage of their development, guiding the selection of PFAS-free chemicals and materials for further development in a SSbD context. In future work, analysing leachates, abraded particles, and chemicals released from coated products could provide an additional approach to assessing consumers and environmental safety during the use phase.

articles.title: A Sensor-Integrated, Explainable Machine-Learning Digital-Twin Framework for Field-Validated Service-Life Prediction of Cementitious Materials under Coupled Chloride–Sulfate Carbonation Degradation
articles.abstract: Reinforced cementitious infrastructure is subjected to all of these mechanisms – chloride ingress, sulfate attack, carbonation, and freeze-thaw or alkali silica cycling – during its service life, but most of the available service-life models treat these mechanisms separately. There are a number of coupled mechanisms that are not currently covered by the industry standard approaches such as classical deterministic Fick’s second law, or semi-probabilistic approaches such as Life-365, DuraCrete and the fib Model Code for Service Life Design, for which it is not yet possible to find broadly accepted models. At the same time, a large number of machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) studies have developed to be able to predict short-term performance with higher accuracy, but as recently summarized in the RILEM Technical Committee 315-DCS and related reviews, most of the studies are based on laboratory generated data, with only limited field validation, few open datasets and very poor model interpretability. After synthesising available evidence on degradation mechanisms, microstructural characterisation, supplementary cementitious materials, self-healing technologies, classical service-life models, and ML/digital-twin structural health monitoring, the present authors conclude that a specific research gap, identified in the literature, lies in the absence of an explainable, sensor-integrated, digital-twin framework that couples multi-hazard mechanistic degradation models with field-updatable machine learning for cementitious materials. This updated version clearly aligns the proposed contribution with six more recent digital-twin and ML-durability frameworks (Section 3.1); develops the governing mathematical formulations for each layer (Section 5); develops a computational workflow and synchronisation algorithm (Section 5.1); expands the explainable-AI and machine-learning methodology (Sections 5.5–5.6); adds a practical implementation and uncertainty-propagation treatment (Section 5.7 and Section 8). A five-layer conceptual framework is suggested that merges embedded electrochemical and optical sensing with a coupled chloride-sulfate-carbonation reactive-transport core, a physics-informed explainable ML layer, Bayesian updating of the digital twin, and a decision support output that is interpretable. A validation strategy, based on existing accelerated-exposure and field-monitoring datasets, is outlined and the framework is illustrated with literature-derived parameter ranges. The paper is written in a concept and method-oriented manner and not to report new laboratory results.

articles.title: Improving water quantity and quality in a mountain hard-rock watershed (La Vera, Spain) through Ancestral Nature-Based Solution for Managed Aquifer Recharge
articles.abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NbS), applied to water resources management, are increasingly promoted as sustainable strategies to address water scarcity and climate-change impacts. The restoration of ancestral aquifer recharge channel systems could be one of the most powerful and low-cost water-management tools. Recent studies have demonstrated that infiltration channels known as pesqueras contribute substantially to groundwater resources in Sierra de Gredos (western Spain). However, their role on groundwater quality and chemistry within the weathered granitic hillslope aquifer have yet remained unexplored. This study aims to characterize how the restored pesqueras network functions as hydrogeological and hydrochemical NbS, based on hydrochemical and isotopic monitoring. Two sampling campaigns were conducted in spring and autumn under contrasting hydrological conditions and included groundwater, stream-water, and recharge-channel samples. Major ions, dissolved silica, electrical conductivity, pH, δ¹⁸O and δ²H were used to identify recharge pathways, groundwater evolution and water-rock interaction processes. The results demonstrate that restored pesqueras not only increase groundwater recharge but also promote natural hydrogeochemical conditioning of infiltrated waters during subsurface transit. Water-rock interactions within the weathered granitic aquifer increase groundwater mineralization from extremely dilute surface-water conditions, producing water of improved suitability for human consumption while preserving high-elevation recharge isotopic signatures that confirm recharge transfer through the aquifer to the discharge zones. Groundwater hydrochemical and isotopic signatures independently support and validate previous conceptual and hydrological models of recharge. These findings show that ancestral recharge channels function as a multi-benefit NbS, simultaneously increasing groundwater storage, improving water quality and sustaining water supplies for mountain communities. The study highlights how the restoration of hydrological infraestructures based on traditional ecological knowledge can provide scientifically validated, low-energy and climate-resilient water-management solutions.

articles.title: Tribocorrosion Performance of TiAlN and AlTiN Coatings on Ti6Al4V in Artificial Saliva: Influence of Mechanical and Electrochemical Responses
articles.abstract: The tribocorrosion performance of TiAlN and AlTiN coatings on Ti6Al4V was investigated in a near-neutral, chloride-containing artificial saliva electrolyte to assess the relationship between mechanical properties, tribological behavior, and electrochemical response. The coatings were deposited by cathodic arc evaporation and characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive spectroscopy, nanoindentation, scratch testing, friction measurements, open-circuit potential (OCP) monitoring, and wear-track analysis. Nanoindentation and scratch testing revealed superior mechanical performance for AlTiN, which exhibited higher hardness, H/E and H³/E² ratios, and critical loads than TiAlN. Under tribocorrosion conditions, however, TiAlN exhibited the lowest measured wear rate despite its lower mechanical performance. Both coatings reduced the coefficient of friction (COF) relative to uncoated Ti6Al4V, with AlTiN showing the lowest average COF against alumina ball, and TiAlN exhibiting a more stable friction coefficient response. The OCP transients revealed a smaller potential perturbation during sliding for TiAlN, indicating a lower degree of electrochemical activation under the investigated conditions. SEM/EDS analysis of the wear tracks also revealed differences in the distribution and retention of oxygen- and electrolyte-derived species on the coating surfaces. These observations suggest that the higher mechanical properties of AlTiN did not directly translate into improved resistance to tribocorrosion. The contrasting OCP responses and wear-track chemistry are consistent with differences in surface-film retention and electrochemical activation, although the specific chemical nature of the films was not established. Under the investigated artificial-saliva conditions, TiAlN provided the highest resistance to tribocorrosion-induced material loss among the tested systems.

articles.title: Synthesis and cooling performance evaluation of novel nanofluid containing n- hexadecane-based nano-encapsulated phase change materials (NEPCMs) in minichannel heat sinks
articles.abstract: This study focuses on nano-encapsulation of n-hexadecane as phase change material (PCM) to produce nanofluid PCM (NPCM) as a potential cooling fluid in minichannel heat sinks. Such new nanofluids exhibit higher heat capacity during phase change than conventional ones, leading to enhanced heat transfer rates. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirms the successful synthesis of nanocapsules via emulsion polymerization. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show spherical nanocapsules with compact walls and smooth, impermeable surfaces. To evaluate the cooling efficiency of the employed working fluid, the nano-encapsulated phase change materials (NEPCMs) are suspended in deionized water at a mass fraction of 0.3% to be used in both wavy and straight minichannel heat sinks. The study compares the performance of NPCM with pure water at different flow rates. The results demonstrate that NPCM exhibits superior heat transfer coefficients and higher pressure drops than pure water. In wavy minichannels, the convective heat transfer coefficient increases by 45% at the highest Reynolds number. However, in straight minichannel heat sinks, the heat transfer coefficient decreases for Reynolds numbers above 500. The cooling performance of the wavy minichannel heat sink is higher than that of the straight minichannel heat sink. Despite a pressure drop penalty in the wavy minichannel heat sink, enhanced heat transfer compensates, resulting in a thermal performance factor greater than 1 for the NPCM. The optimal thermal performance of NPCM occurs at a Reynolds number of 500, where the Nusselt number improves by up to 62% and 57% in wavy and straight minichannels, respectively.

articles.title: An Intelligent Regime-Aware, Arbitrage-Consistent, and Explainable Semi-Parametric Framework for High-Frequency Derivatives Pricing and Algorithmic Trading
articles.abstract: The emerging nature of the high-frequency electronic derivatives markets has exposed important issues with existing pricing and trading intelligence systems: deep learning models have struggled to effectively combine multiple types of volatility indicators across time scales, and the extension of these systems to complex payoff structures has violated key no-arbitrage constraints, especially during intraday regime changes. Meanwhile, traditional algorithmic trading agents cannot provide a financially interpretable account of their uncertainty and lack statistical guarantees for that uncertainty quantification. This paper introduces a coherent semi-parametric architecture of five closely coupled modules. M 3 V-FuseNet combines microstructure signals with families of realised and implied volatilities, transforming surface geometry across multiple temporal scales (τ = 5, 25, 120 ticks) into a regime-sensitive latent volatility state. Arb-Guard enforces monotonicity, convexity, and calendar-spread consistency via projected-gradient operators, forming an arbitrage-consistent European pricing surface. ExoX-SDE calibrates a risk-neutral Neural SDE [1, 2] to the Arb-Guard surface, pricing barrier, Asian, and other exotic payoffs through a differen-tiable payoff library and 50,000 Monte Carlo simulations. A-XAI TraceStack provides Fréchet-based attribution, counterfactual perturbation analysis, and formal arbitrage-compliance certificates. TheoMix-CP combines a theory-guided residual learner with conformal prediction for distribution-free coverage guarantees (≥ 95%). Evaluation on 18 months of high-frequency equity-index and 1 single-stock option data (420 million ticks; 8,000–10,000 implied-volatility surface points per day) shows European option RMSE reductions of 27–35% relative to Deep Hedging [3]; implied-volatility surface RMSE of 1.28 bps; exotic-pricing RMSE reductions exceeding 35%; a static-arbitrage violation rate of 0.06%; directional accuracy of 78.6/73.9/69.2% (calm/transitional/stressed); a Sharpe ratio of 1.62; and a delta-hedging error of 0.062. Ablation across all five modules confirms statistically significant incremental contributions (paired t-test, Wilcoxon, Diebold–Mariano, Kupiec; all p < 0.005).

articles.title: Temporal robustness hierarchies distinguish structural and quantum-feasible traversals in living networks
articles.abstract: Dynamic quantum networks require two questions to be separated: whether a time window contains a spanning graph-theoretic certificate, and whether that certificate can be executed chronologically while meeting quantum-quality and resource constraints. We formulate a quan tumliving temporalgraphwithatomictimecells, state-dependent transmit, receive, and memory capabilities, and discrete or positive-duration link opportunities. Hamiltonian and Eulerian robustness are classified as Weak, Local, Strong, or Interval-Strong. The hierarchy is strict in gen eral. A channel-composition witness is required for the final quantum Eulerian separation; static identity channels alone do not establish it.
