However, the indexer must still score the entire KV cache at every decoding step. This scoring overhead becomes a major bottleneck as the context length grows. We propose SPIN (Shadow Predictive Indexer) to reduce this indexer overhead. SPIN uses lightweight, history-based prediction to identify important KV blocks, avoiding the need to score the full KV cache at every decoding step. SPIN treats KV blocks and speculative decoding as first-class design and implementation considerations. Across extensive evaluations on long-context and agentic benchmarks, SPIN achieves 30-40% sparsity while preserving task quality. In end-to-end vLLM serving, SPIN improves output throughput by up to 14.9% and reduces median inter-token latency by up to 13.2%.

articles.title: CurveTQ: Rotation-Free Trellis Quantization of LLM Weights via Curvature-Weighted Search
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The best two-bit weight quantizers for large language models, such as QTIP and Proteus, rotate each weight matrix by a random orthogonal transform, which must be undone at every decoding step, then encode it with a trellis or lattice code under a Euclidean search; the layer Hessian enters only through error feedback between coding blocks. We show that this leaves part of the Hessian unused. Error feedback turns the loss into a weighted sum of per-coordinate rounding errors whose weights, the diagonal of the Hessian's LDL factorization, existing quantizers compute but never read. We put these weights into the Viterbi branch metric, so the search follows the curvature within each coding block. This also explains the rotation: it removes this within-block variation, so weighting in the native basis and rotating are substitutes. On three models the weighted native search matches a full-dimension randomized Hadamard to within about one point of downstream accuracy, and weighting after the rotation gains little. Around this search we build CurveTQ, a trellis codec with no rotation, which handles the weights' amplitude and marginal shape with a factored scale field and a closed-form quantile table, and stores a start state per coding block so the trellis can adapt to the residual that error feedback carries into it. At two bits CurveTQ is 1-3 points higher in mean downstream accuracy than QTIP and Proteus on three 4-8B Instruct models, even after both are given our start state, which alone lifts either baseline by 1-3 points. It also leads on a 35B mixture of experts, to our knowledge the first trellis-coded result on such a model. With no rotation to undo, our decoder is the fastest of the three at all tested batch sizes and bit widths.

articles.title: What a Reporting Convention Hides: A Matched-Budget Audit of Quantum Natural Gradient with an Exactly Computed Metric
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several published comparisons of variational quantum optimizers time only runs that reach a target loss, or read the verdict at a single target. Either convention could decide whether an optimizer's costlier steps pay off. We measure how much each convention changes verdicts among Adam, simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) and quantum natural gradient (QNG), on initializations held out from the selection of settings. We compute the exact metric that preconditions QNG, price every step in circuit evaluations and give every method the same budget. In a median pooled over circuit widths, cost families and a sweep of settings with common misses, SPSA needs more than twice Adam's evaluations to reach a loose target. Dropping the censored runs that miss the target hides this gap. On the global-cost family we hold fixed the settings selected for a strict target. QNG then usually reaches the loose target after Adam but the strict target first. QNG's strict-target lead disappears when the metric's simulator price, linear in the number of parameters, is replaced by an assumed hardware count quadratic in that number. We recommend charging every miss the budget and reporting verdicts across targets.

articles.title: UniCSI Towards a Universal Wi-Fi CSI Encoder for Ubiquitous Human Sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wi-Fi sensing promises to turn the everyday wireless signals that already surround us into ubiquitous sensors for human sensing. However, a fundamental obstacle is that CSI is acquired under diverse device-specific configurations, including different subcarrier counts, bandwidths, and carrier bands. Consequently, the resulting CSI tensors vary in both spectral resolution and tensor shape, making heterogeneous modeling challenging. Standard architectures struggle with such heterogeneity, forcing lossy pre-processing which compromises the underlying signal. To bridge this gap, we present UniCSI, a unified foundation architecture that directly operates on heterogeneous CSI while preserving the integrity of the native waveform. UniCSI hinges on two core innovations: (1) a physics-informed RF tokenizer that encodes each frequency channel based on its fractional position within the physical spectrum rather than rigid array indices. It preserves intrinsic spectral coherence and enables seamless, frequency resolution-agnostic processing across arbitrary sensing configurations. (2) a spectral aggregator that distills variable-length channel sequences into a fixed-size spectral signature, effectively decoupling the feature dimensionality from the physical subcarrier spacing. Extensive evaluations on a large-scale corpus of 25 heterogeneous public datasets, spanning 14 to 2048 subcarriers, 20 to 160 MHz bandwidth, and the 2.4 and 5 GHz bands, demonstrate that native heterogeneous ingestion substantially improves cross-domain transfer under both supervised and self-supervised training schemes, particularly in regimes where fixed-grid architectures fail to generalize.

articles.title: ProtocolMatch: Protocol-Dependent Model Selection for Scientific Dynamics Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific dynamics forecasting is often framed as an architecture choice, although deployment is also determined by observed history, rollout feedback, compute budget, physical objective, and test distribution. We formulate protocol-dependent model selection and introduce ProtocolMatch, a compute-matched, validation-selected, and failure-preserving evaluation framework. On driven quantum-spin dynamics, we compare recurrent, patched-attention, causal-attention, and low-rank linear predictors across three independently generated datasets. The causal-attention--recurrence ordering reverses as the training set grows within a fixed two-spin task, while a linear predictor has the lowest mean error in the six-spin local-observable comparison. Restricting observed history worsens every refreshed-history view but improves every closed-loop view in the four-spin study. A latest-state MLP has lower error than persistence on every dataset under state refresh across all five cells, yet its closed-loop rank varies by system and includes finite explosive errors. Physical penalties improve targeted consistency without reliably improving prediction error, and in-distribution intervals lose most coverage after a driving-frequency shift. Thus scientific model selection should return a predictor with its protocol and report accuracy, physical validity, and shifted-distribution reliability separately.

articles.title: Dataset Pruning from First Principles: A Label-Free Linear Programming Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dataset pruning reduces a large training set to a representative subset while preserving model performance. Existing geometry-based methods typically assume that nearby points in embedding space share similar properties. Rather than imposing this assumption, we derive geometric selection criteria by reformulating unbiased subset selection as a variance minimization problem. Unbiasedness ensures that unweighted subset averages recover full-dataset averages in expectation, including losses and gradients at fixed model parameters. Specifically, we characterize a family of unbiased subset selection algorithms as a high-dimensional polytope. In this context, minimizing the expected sampling variance is a linear objective. Differences in sampling variance, averaged over rigid motions, admit closed-form pairwise expressions. Because the polytope has high dimension, directly applying standard linear programming is impractical. We instead use these expressions to construct an efficient vertex walk that optimizes an approximation of the variance objective while preserving unbiasedness, yielding a method that requires neither labels nor model training during selection. Across CIFAR-10, MNIST, and CelebA benchmarks, our method matches or exceeds uniform sampling in mean test accuracy at every evaluated budget and outperforms competing geometric methods in several settings, particularly at small selection budgets. Beyond dataset pruning, the same framework reduces stochastic-gradient variance by increasing diversity within mini-batches while keeping the batch size unchanged.

articles.title: Whose Memory Is It? Scope-Aware Commit Rules for Long-Term LLM Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent memory allows an LLM agent to carry experience across conversations, but it also turns a local reasoning mistake into a durable one. During deliberation, an agent may consider a plan, simulate a tool result, report another speaker's belief, and then reject all of them. If memory retains only the resulting sentences, those once-useful possibilities can later return as facts. The record is neither fabricated nor irrelevant; it has simply been detached from the context in which it was valid. We identify this missing context as emphdiscourse ownership: the world, branch, or speaker that licenses a proposition. Our first finding is counterintuitive. Language models already carry a causally active signal for ownership, yet conventional memory interfaces discard it when they convert reasoning into records. We introduce CASK (Causally Anchored Scoping Keys), a commit rule that preserves this signal so that shared-world facts enter durable memory while provisional content remains available only within its original scope. Our second finding is that the most obvious way to preserve the signal---storing the discovered internal coordinates---is unreliable because equivalent representations need not keep the same coordinates. CASK instead preserves the stable relations that express ownership. Controlled long-conversation conflicts and tool-agent traces show that this design improves memory admission and prevents provisional content from contaminating later answers while complementing runtime provenance. The resulting commit boundary lets agents explore more possibilities without granting every intermediate sentence authority over future behavior.

articles.title: GeoNatureAgent (GNA): A Framework and Benchmark for Pre-Production Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents on Geospatial and Environmental Tasks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Before tool-using LLM agents are deployed in environmental and geospatial workflows, teams need evidence that an agent reliably selects the right operations against real APIs. We introduce GeoNatureAgent (GNA), a framework for pre-production evaluation of tool-using agents: a fixed sixteen-tool geospatial interface published as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, so the agent under test is the only variable, scored against an identical tool layer, task suite, and deterministic scorer. Its flagship instance is a 103-task benchmark (a 93-task main suite across 18 categories plus a ten-task comparison expansion) evaluated against an open, self-hostable geospatial API serving three environmental indicators across Spain and Portugal. We evaluate nine LLMs under three temperature-1.0 seeds, reporting capability and per-case cost as orthogonal axes. (1) Claude Sonnet 4 achieves the highest capability (61.7% +/- 0.7% on all 103 tasks; 60.8% on the main suite), followed closely by DeepSeek V3.2 (57.9%), while no other model exceeds 53%; (2) the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier is mostly open-weight, with DeepSeek V3.2 offering 93% of Claude's capability at 11.3x lower list-price cost; (3) under strict all-checks scoring the best model sits 24-36 points below the 85-97% reported on general-purpose GIS benchmarks, whereas per-check partial credit for the top four models (86-90%) is comparable, so much of that gap reflects scoring strictness rather than task difficulty alone. The MCP server, evaluation harness, benchmark, and API are publicly available; swapping the tool executors and task suite instantiates an equivalent benchmark for any geospatial domain.

articles.title: Which Buildings Are Artificial Intelligence-Ready? A Measurement-Based Assessment Framework for AI Question Answering and Actuation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are becoming the interface to buildings, answering questions and controlling operations, but a building's readiness for them has not been systematically assessed. This study proposes a framework to quantify it. First, a building's knowledge graph sets two ceilings. The answerable-readiness ceiling is the share of operational questions its data could answer, and the actuation-readiness ceiling is the share of control actions it exposes. Second, a reference AI agent's accuracy on a fixed set of these questions shows how much of the ceilings is realized. On a simulated office, the agent realizes 0.62 of a 0.64 answerable ceiling, so missing data, not the AI, limit readiness, except in naming a fault's cause. Across 37 public real-building graphs, the median answerable ceiling is 0.16, and in 15 of 45, unlinked sensors lower it. The framework turns "is this building AI-ready?" into an auditable, ranked retrofit question.

articles.title: NL2Hull: A Natural Language-Driven Constrained Ship Design Decision Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ship-form design combines smooth geometric representation, local shape editing, and constraints on the resulting hull. We present the Natural-Language-to-Hull Framework (NL2Hull Framework), which formulates ship-form editing as a typed discrete decision problem and connects language decisions to numerical geometry. Its Constrained Free-Form Deformation Engine (CFFD Engine) represents hull waterlines with non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS), applies free-form deformation (FFD) to their control points, reconstructs the hull, and checks geometric constraints. We construct the Ship Design Decision Dataset (SDD Dataset) with 134,558 cleaned records and evaluate compared models on its subset Ship Design Decision Benchmark (SDDBench), containing 5,000 records and 43,496 typed questions. We propose Chip, a constrained ship-design decision model for processing natural-language requests. Chip reaches 95.90% question accuracy and 99.32% FFD exact match, with a negative log-likelihood of 0.0951, an expected calibration error of 0.0032, and a Brier score of 0.0551. The NL2Hull Framework provides a reproducible interface for evaluating language-based ship-form decisions while identifying the geometry and continuous-control components that require further development. Our code and dataset is available at https://github.com/wenhuahuo/NL2Hull.

articles.title: Physics-based Sphere Packing for Lagrangian Mesh Morphing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies tetrahedral meshes as the body representation for differentiable simulation and computational design. Fixed-connectivity meshes degrade under large morphs, while remeshing from scratch discards node correspondence. We present JamTet, a physics-based sphere-packing framework for volumetric meshing and morphing. We contribute (i) a GPU-parallel mesher combining octree-hierarchical packing with constrained Delaunay tetrahedralization, producing more uniform element volumes than TetGen and fTetWild; (ii) Lagrangian mesh morphing that preserves interior-node identities by re-equilibrating the same spheres within changing shapes and rebuilding the boundary and connectivity, remaining inversion-free where fixed-connectivity and TetSphere meshes invert; and (iii) a differentiable GPU simulator in JAX, with mass-spring edges and a volumetric Neo-Hookean term, integrated with mesh morphing in a design pipeline. In soft-robot morphology design experiments, interior-node gradients improve swimming fitness by 0.73-1.07 over a matched surface-only variant, while voxelized versions of the same designs yield 32-63% lower fitness. These results establish sphere packing as a practical volumetric mesh representation for gradient-based shape optimization. Code and media: under review.

articles.title: Multi-Aspect Runtime Verification for Simulation-Based V&V of LLM-Enabled Autonomous Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08928v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-based agents are entering decision-support roles in defence staff work, where the obligations they must respect are already written down and binding, and where retraining is not available as a control because models arrive as procured components. What can be placed under engineering control is the interface between the agent and the systems it acts on. Those obligations are at once spatial, temporal and text-semantic, and a violation typically lives in the composition of a multi-step interaction, which is why per-event guardrails miss sequential tool-attack chains. We present a multi-aspect runtime-verification framework that decomposes a natural-language policy clause into a typed spatial/temporal/semantic triple over one canonical event stream, checks each aspect with its own monitoring specification, and fuses the verdicts through a four-valued algebra that carries provenance. The spatial aspect is interpreted over a weighted two-sorted location graph in which mission geometry and information-release topology are one object; we show that these spatial obligations are not in general subsumed by a first-order temporal specification. The past-time aspect runs on the unmodified MonPoly engine, which agrees with our reference monitor at every time point. Across two mission domains, casualty evacuation and contested sustainment, and one civil domain, composition under the precautionary blocking policy drives attack success to zero with no observed false positives and microsecond-scale per-event cost, while every single aspect and every pair leaves a substantial share of attacks succeeding. In a closed-loop experiment a policy-naive planner reaches a violating state in most unshielded missions and in none when shielded, and four refused episodes in five still recover to a compliant outcome.

articles.title: Toward Evidence-Driven Human-Agent-Robot Teaming for Earth-Independent Anomaly Triage
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep-space crews cannot rely on real-time ground support for urgent off-nominal events. Initial alerts may underdetermine cause, while discriminating evidence may reside in crew observations or at locations that are unsafe, costly, or unavailable for crew inspection. We present an evidence-driven architecture for human-agent-robot teaming in Earth-independent anomaly triage. Agentic AI is treated as a stateful coordinator over bounded, inspectable services rather than as a fully autonomous vehicle controller. A triage state manager maintains hypotheses, evidence provenance, uncertainty, operational context, and tool status; a crew-facing embodied agent elicits observations and explains assessment changes; and a mobile robot acquires targeted, localized evidence. Typed interfaces separate dialogue and orchestration from monitoring, robot command, context retrieval, and safety-critical control. Two scenarios illustrate the architecture: a crewed deep-space mission based on an actual ISS ammonia false alarm, where suspected contamination restricts crew access, and a power-interface anomaly at a crewed lunar base, where robotic inspection distinguishes a local connector fault from other causes ambiguous in remote telemetry. Our main contribution is an authority-bounded closed evidence-loop architecture, exercised in a hardware-in-the-loop integration prototype using Reachy Mini and an Innate MARS mobile robot.

articles.title: Quad-State Safety Evaluation of Open-Weight Large Language Models on Non-Canonical Inputs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard safety evaluations of large language models assess harmful requests written in canonical plain text, while models in real-world deployment routinely receive inputs containing emojis, altered spellings, encoded strings, and character-level variations. This work introduces the Adversarial Surface-Form Robustness Dataset (ASRD), comprising 2,100 prompts across seven distinct surface-form families. Five open-weight language models are evaluated across these prompts, producing 10,500 responses. The Quad-State Evaluation Rubric classifies each response into one of four outcomes: harmful compliance, safe response, comprehension failure, or indeterminate. Emoji and invisible Unicode variations cause almost no comprehension failure, with pooled harmful compliance of 20.27% and 17.20% against a 22.87% baseline that is driven mainly by Mistral 7B, whereas leetspeak, encoded wrappers, and hybrid transformations score 2.40%, 0.13%, and 2.40% while comprehension failure rises to 36.47%, 65.60%, and 34.47%. Inspection of raw model outputs reveals three response behaviors: hallucinated benignity, structural collapse, and language drift. Project page: www.pavanmaddula.com/quadstate

articles.title: Talking with Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When we interact with large language models (LLMs), are we having a conversation? They are designed to invite us to treat them as intelligent interlocutors who remember, act, and make commitments. But appearances deceive. We introduce the artifactual stance, a framework that reconceives human-AI interaction as artifact-mediated exchanges of candidate texts. LLM outputs are candidate texts optimized for utility, not utterances bearing meaning or force. LLMs are sophisticated text generators, not speakers. Between sessions, nothing runs; between turns, no one remembers. What persists is a configuration and a transcript. The "conversation" is a user's solo performance, interpretive labour disguised by interface and artifact design. This shift dissolves recent philosophical puzzles. Questions about what 'I' and 'you' refer to in AI exchanges, about whether systems can lie or be held to promises, about the identity of our supposed interlocutors all rest on a false presupposition. There is no speaker behind the screen, hence no one to refer to, no one to hold responsible. What feels like dialogue with someone is interaction with an artifact that generates text at unprecedented scale and fit. By abandoning the conversational framing, we see these systems for what they are: immensely sophisticated artifacts that afford varied uses. The philosophical questions that matter are about the normative underpinnings of design, adoption, authorization, and human practices of use.

articles.title: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) perform tasks across applications (such as desktops, mobile apps, and web browsers) by observing graphical interfaces and issuing commands such as clicks and keystrokes. These interfaces combine trusted controls and content with untrusted content needed for legitimate tasks. An adversary controlling this untrusted content can embed instructions or misleading visual cues to change the agent's intended action or redirect its commands to the wrong interface target. We formalize security requirements for both the agent's decisions and their execution through GUI commands. In an ideal execution model, we show that enforcing both requirements at each step protects execution traces. We instantiate this model in Secure-CUA, our system for secure CUA execution. Its key idea is to commit to an explicit per-action program, called an action transaction, before accessing untrusted content. Each transaction fixes its queries to untrusted content and the permitted uses of their responses. The system masks untrusted regions and evaluates each transaction to produce the next action, using an isolated query model to answer its queries. It then locates the intended interface target using the masked interface. Under the model's assumptions, Secure-CUA is secure by design, while generating a new transaction at each step helps maintain high task utility by adapting to changing interfaces. We evaluate Secure-CUA under benign conditions on 400 WebArena tasks using three frontier models across 5 seeds, yielding 6,000 execution traces. Secure-CUA achieves an average task success rate of 53.55%, compared with 55.12% for Vanilla-CUA and 13.17% for CaMeL-CUA.

articles.title: Interfacial Corrosion Protection of ST37 Steel by Borassus flabellifer Husk Extract in 1 M HCl: Effect of Inhibitor Concentration
articles.abstract: In this study, the corrosion inhibition performance of Borassus flabellifer fruit husk extract was evaluated for ST37 steel in 1 M HCl at inhibitor concentrations of 50–250 ppm using weight-loss, potentiodynamic polarization, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), FTIR, SEM–EDX, and atomic force microscopy (AFM). The extract exhibited its highest inhibition efficiency of 88.40% at 100 ppm. At this concentration, the corrosion current density decreased from 479.12 to 121.86 µA cm⁻², the corrosion rate decreased from 5.62 to 1.43 mm year⁻¹, and the charge-transfer resistance increased from 41.72 to 190 Ω cm². Polarization measurements indicated mixed-type inhibition with anodic predominance. Surface characterization showed reduced corrosion-induced degradation and lower surface roughness at 100 ppm, with (:Rₐ) and (:Rq) values of 68.28 and 88.15 nm, respectively. FTIR analysis identified oxygen-containing and aromatic functional groups that may contribute to interfacial adsorption. Overall, the electrochemical and surface-characterization results support a proposed adsorption-assisted inhibition mechanism involving the formation of a protective interfacial layer that reduces corrosion of ST37 steel in acidic media.

articles.title: Impact of End-Capped Modification on tert-Butyl Carbazole Non-Fused Acceptors for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Developing small-molecule-based asymmetric non-fullerene (SM-NFAs) acceptors is highly desirable because they offer significant structural diversity, higher dipole moments, and strong intermolecular interactions. In this study, four new molecules (EE1-EE4) were designed by end-group modification to improve photovoltaic performance. The designed materials show a significant reduction in the energy gap of 1.70–1.88 eV, lower than the reference (2.02 eV). The designed molecules exhibited λmax values (638.21-682.13 nm) in the gaseous phase, higher than the reference (617.51 nm). In addition, λmax values were further redshifted in the solvent phase (696.93-769.18 nm) compared to the reference (660.72 nm). The open-circuit voltage (Voc) values (0.64 eV-0.90 eV) were comparable to R (1.25 eV). The lower reorganization energies for electrons (λe = 0.0078–0.0115 eV) and holes (λh = 0.0047- 0.0069eV) indicate efficient charge transport and reduced energy losses. This study provides valuable insights into structure-property relationships and offers a rational design strategy for high-performance NFAs in next-generation organic solar cells.

articles.title: Effect of the external electric field on the fixed grating in Bi2TeO5 photorefractive crystal
articles.abstract: We describe the effect of an external electric field on a fixed grating in an undoped Bi2TeO5 crystal. The experimental results show an asymmetry in the diffraction efficiency of the fixed grating with respect to the externally applied electric field, and this asymmetry was attributed to the spontaneous polarization of the crystal. A mathematical model was used to analyze the general observations of this experiment, including the photovoltaic effect. This effect was observed in our sample and was characterized through measurements of the photovoltaic current as a function of light intensity and its polarization states at different wavelengths.

articles.title: Removal of Brilliant Green from Wastewater by Heat Activated Persulfate Oxidation : Modeling and Optimization
articles.abstract: The present paper aims to investigate the effect of various operational parameters on the degradation efficiency of the toxic dye “Brilliant Green (BG)” using temperature-activated persulfate (T/SP). The study was carried out by varying the concentration of Brilliant Green (BG) from 5 to 50 mg/L, the concentration of persulfate from 0.42 to 4.2 mM, and the agitation speed from 250 to 350 rpm under a temperature range from 25 to 50°C. Statistical approaches, such as Plackett-Burman Design (PBD) and Response Surface Methodology (RSM), were used in the optimization process. The Plackett-Burman design was carried out using twelve trials, identifying significant parameters such as the Brilliant Green (BG) concentration, the persulfate concentration [SP], and the temperature T. The RSM was used to determine the optimal parameters for degradation. The maximum degradation efficiency (100%) was achieved under the following optimal conditions: T = 25°C, [SP] = 3.7165 mM, and [BG] = 50 mg/L. Despite a strong correlation between theoretical and practical returns (R² = 93.89%). Finally, a confirmatory study using optimized parameter levels showed a good response to the predicted model. The results revealed that the T/SP oxidation system is an effective and promising process for the degradation of BG at room temperature.

articles.title: Architectures and physical limits of fast and sustainable artificial intelligence
articles.abstract: Fast artificial intelligence depends on the coordinated behavior of semiconductor devices, arithmetic units, memory hierarchies, communication fabrics, compilers and data center infrastructure. Peak arithmetic throughput alone cannot predict either response time or environmental performance. This critical integrative review connects these layers through a workload-dependent analysis of computation, data movement, communication, queueing and heat removal. It distinguishes training, prompt processing and autoregressive decoding; compares CPUs, GPUs, domain-specific accelerators, FPGAs and emerging computing paradigms; and examines semiconductor scaling, packaging, memory capacity, bus signaling and distributed execution. The analytical contribution is a decision framework that combines established performance bounds with explicit feasibility constraints and lifecycle accounting. Derived crossover conditions identify when increasing arithmetic throughput cannot improve latency, when batching encounters a memory limit, and when hardware replacement cannot yet recover its embodied carbon. A worked example uses published H100 SXM specifications exclusively as idealized hardware ceilings, not as measured application performance. Normalized sensitivity analyses expose the consequences of bandwidth, utilization and traffic reduction without manufacturing benchmark data. The synthesis indicates that sustainable acceleration requires minimizing useful work and transferred bytes while maintaining task quality, tail-latency limits and feasible power density. This is a literature-based study with transparent analytical derivations; no new device, prototype, experimental benchmark or field measurement is reported.

articles.title: Assessment of PFAS Mobility in Soil–Groundwater Systems Based on Adsorption Characteristics
articles.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in soil–groundwater systems are influenced by molecular structure, soil characteristics, and groundwater chemistry, which determine their mobility and leaching behavior. This study evaluated PFAS adsorption using soils collected from three depth intervals (0–30, 30–60, and 60–90 cm) and groundwater matrices with contrasting ionic compositions. Apparent distribution coefficients and screening-level retardation factors were estimated from batch experiments to assess relative PFAS mobility. Adsorption increased with carbon-chain length and was greater in shallow soils with higher organic matter contents than in deeper soils. Retardation factors decreased with depth, indicating enhanced mobility in subsurface layers. Groundwater matrices reduced adsorption compared with deionized water, particularly for short-chain PFASs, suggesting that dissolved ions limited sorption. Among the tested carbonaceous sorbents, activated carbon exhibited the highest adsorption capacity, although removal efficiencies for short-chain PFASs remained moderate in contaminated groundwater. Overall, PFAS mobility in soil–groundwater systems ware governed by PFAS structure, soil characteristics, and groundwater geochemistry. These findings provide a screening-level framework for evaluating PFAS leaching under groundwater-relevant conditions.

articles.title: Real-world performance of antimicrobial surface coatings differs from laboratory testing
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial coatings are increasingly used on high-touch surfaces to reduce the spread of germs. Most of these coatings are tested under controlled laboratory conditions. However, real-world environments are very different. To investigate how these coatings perform in everyday settings, researchers tested four commercially available antimicrobial surfaces in real-life environments. They measured the number of bacteria, whether the bacteria were alive, and how the microbial communities changed over time. Among all the coatings, copper performed the best: It greatly reduced bacteria and living microbes. Light-activated titanium dioxide coatings provided moderate protection: They reduced bacterial contamination but had little effect on the overall microbial community. In contrast, silver- and quaternary ammonium-based coatings had only limited effects, despite performing well in laboratory tests. Overall, the study shows that laboratory testing alone cannot predict how antimicrobial surfaces will perform in real life. Moreover, microbes commonly associated with humans were more easily reduced, while microbes from the natural environment were more resistant. Future studies will track these surfaces over time to understand how cleaning, wear, and repeated human contact influence their long-term effectiveness. Kaur et al. “Context-dependent effects of antimicrobial coatings on microbial load and bacterial community composition on public high-touch surfaces.” Microbiome (2026)

articles.title: Governance in an Institutional Environment Reconfigured by Artificial Intelligence. A Public Choice Institutionalism Perspective
articles.abstract: This paper argues that polycentricity, conceptualized on public choice institutionalism lines, is the pivotal framework for understanding, evaluating, and steering governance at a moment when artificial intelligence is structurally reconfiguring the institutional environment. It first separates two problems that are routinely conflated: the governance of artificial intelligence as an artifact (its internal configuration and its interface with human judgment) and the broader, deeper problem of governing an institutional world that the diffusion of artificial intelligence is itself transforming. The latter, it contends, is a dynamic problem in collective choice under deep heterogeneity and uncertainty. Applying inframarginal analysis to the division of labor between human and artificial agents, and reading the result through the Ostroms' three-level institutional framework, the paper traces how the reallocation of functions propagates across the architecture, activating, at each order of effect, the canonical public choice effects and problems such as: agency loss, rent-seeking and capture, bureau-maximization, dispersed costs and concentrated benefits, and collective-action failure. The emerging multi-level, multi-criterion, multi-interpretation institutional architecture requires exactly the conceptual structure polycentricity supplies. The case is advanced on analytical, normative, and feasibility grounds, reinforced by the implicit notions of constitutional political economy the framework carries. The paper is explicit that none of these licenses designing a polycentric order into existence; what remains possible is to steer an evolutionary process whose outcomes stay genuinely open.

articles.title: Probabilistic compound flood risk to critical infrastructure in a protected delta: loss concentration, sea-level rise, and tail-risk attribution
articles.abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic compound coastal–fluvial flood risk assessment for 376 critical infrastructure assets of the Fraser River delta, Canada (CAD 55.61 billion replacement value), a census within five pre-declared categories. A 600,000-event stochastic catalog couples goodness-of-fit-tested bi-seasonal copulas to sampled tidal forcing and three sea-level tiers; a reduced-physics hydrodynamic model, evaluated at seven federal gauges with dikes represented explicitly, converts events to water surfaces; a Gaussian-process surrogate (cross-validated depth error 0.053 m) extends the physics to catalog scale; and a custom non-residential damage-function library prices losses. The configuration is Unsatisfactory under a published estuarine validation criterion and adopted under a fitness-for-purpose statement; five bias mechanisms share a conservative sign, so results are a lower bound with respect to them, with two-sided footprint-sampling and valuation uncertainty bracketed. Average annual loss (occurrence basis) rises from CAD 0.374 million today to 119.6, 350.6, and 1,726.2 million at +0.77, +1.00, and +1.50 m relative sea-level rise; the ratio of average annual loss to the 100-year probable maximum loss rises from 0.018 to 0.702; and losses concentrate on two wastewater plants; the regime transition survives within-site sampling at the dominant asset, absolute levels do not. An 1894-class scenario prices the provincial reference flood at CAD 4.8 million today against 2,030 million under the delta-adjusted tier. Statistical dependence between discharge and surge contributes at most ~3 percent of tail losses; hydrodynamic interaction is negligible for the median extreme event yet reaches ~30 percent in surge-driven events; compound tail risk is therefore governed primarily by marginal severities against protection freeboards.

articles.title: Small Modular Reactors in Italy’s Energy Transition: Integrating Long-Term Planning and Hourly Weather Stress Testing
articles.abstract: Energy is increasingly regarded as a strategic national asset. Long-term planning must therefore evaluate environmental sustainability, security of supply, system reliability and the affordability of system costs together. This energy trilemma becomes harder to assess when systems rely more heavily on variable renewable energy. As a result, energy planning requires more robust modelling tools, able to connect long-term system evolution with operational performance under realistic conditions. Energy-system models used for long-term planning often simplify chronology through representative or averaged time slices. This abstraction makes large multi-year optimisation problems tractable, but it may understate the operational consequences of variable renewable energy, prolonged low-resource events and hourly adequacy requirements. This paper develops and applies a soft-linked modelling framework for Italy in which a dynamic multi-carrier energy-system optimisation model, Hypatia, defines long-term pathways across electricity, heat and hydrogen, while an hourly model, Calliope, tests selected target-year configurations under 8760-hour chronology. The coupling transfers Hypatia capacities for 2030, 2040 and 2050 to Calliope, where all non-battery technologies are fixed at their inherited levels, while additional battery capacity can be selected endogenously to meet hourly flexibility requirements.. The hourly stage is run under a Typical Meteorological Year and three critical historical weather years selected from a 45-year solar and wind dataset, including the lowest combined capacity-factor year and one-week and two-week Dunkelflaute events. Four policy-relevant cases are analysed: a conservative reference pathway, a VRES-led net-zero pathway with doubled renewable deployment limits, and two nuclear-plus-CCS sensitivities with high and low nuclear capital costs. Results show that temporal aggregation materially affects scenario interpretation. In the VRES-led net-zero case, Calliope increases 2050 battery requirements from 473 GWh in Hypatia to 26107 GWh, while the corrected system cost rises from 699 to 1866 billion € under the two-week Dunkelflaute case. By contrast, firm low-carbon capacity reduces the adequacy correction: in the low-costs nuclear case, 2050 battery needs remain within 161–183 GWh and the cost correction is within 10 billion €. The results show that operational and weather-year stress testing can fundamentally change the assessment of long-term decarbonisation pathways, highlighting the role of nuclear capacity in achieving carbon neutrality while maintaining system adequacy and limiting the cost and storage requirements associated with prolonged renewable scarcity.

articles.title: Effects of oxide supports and Pt loading on the interfacial structure and catalytic performance of SANIs-inspired catalysts for dry reforming of methane
articles.abstract: Catalysts that simultaneously achieve high catalytic activity and strong resistance to sintering are highly desirable for methane dry reforming (DRM), yet the rational design of such catalysts remains challenging. Inspired by the Single-Atom Nano-Islands (SANIs) concept, a series of SANIs-inspired Pt catalysts with oxide-modified SiO2 supports were rationally designed and synthesized via the liquid-phase electrostatic adsorption method to engineer the metal-support interface. Structural characterization confirmed the successful construction of the SANIs-inspired Pt/NiOx-SiO2 catalyst with highly dispersed Pt species and intimate Pt/NiOx spatial association. Combined X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and hydrogen temperature-programmed reduction analyses revealed strong metal-support interaction (MSI) at the Pt/NiOx interface, which was associated with superior DRM performance among the catalysts studied. Further optimization of Pt loading revealed that an appropriate Pt loading was essential for balancing active site availability and interfacial stability. The 4.2wt% Pt/NiOx-SiO2 catalyst achieved the optimal interfacial structure, delivering a CH4 conversion of 85% and retaining a conversion of 81.3% after 200 h of continuous DRM operation. In contrast, excessive Pt loading promoted Pt aggregation and Ostwald ripening under high-temperature DRM conditions, accompanied by NiOx crystallization and structural redistribution, resulting in Pt/NiOx interface reconstruction and weakened interfacial interaction. These findings demonstrate that the synergistic regulation of MSI and Pt distribution is critical for achieving highly active and stable DRM catalysts and provide an effective strategy for catalyst design through interfacial structure engineering.

articles.title: Elaborate Finite Element Model for Resilient Slip Friction Joints
articles.abstract: Resilient Slip Friction Joints (RSFJs) have emerged as an effective solution for achieving energy dissipation and self-centering capabilities in seismic-resistant structural systems. This study presents the development and validation of a finite element (FE) model for simulating the mechanical behavior of RSFJs. ABAQUS/CAE 2020 was employed to develop the proposed model, which is based on steel plates sliding over each other and connected by pretensioned bolts and elastic springs. The proposed modeling approach enables accurate prediction of key connection parameters, providing a reliable numerical framework for analyzing the performance of RSFJs. The FE model validation was carried out through comparison with both experimental results and, analytical equations. The comparison focused on the hysteresis curve characteristics, with particular emphasis on the force corresponding to maximum allowable relative displacement, stiffness, and the level of damping. In addition, the FE model was employed to perform a comprehensive parametric study aimed at assessing the effects of key design parameters including spring stiffness, bolt pre-tension force, and friction coefficient on the overall performance of the joint.

articles.title: Robust Multi-Sensor Fusion via Memristive Deep Reservoir Computing With Differential-Pair Fault Tolerance
articles.abstract: This paper presents a Deep Reservoir Computing (DeepRC) based multi-sensor fusion framework for autonomous vehicle perception and UAV landing, with a particular focus on hardware-level fault tolerance. Recognizing that practical memristor crossbar arrays(MCAs) suffer from conductance variations and stuck-at faults(SAFs) that severely degrade reservoir dynamics, we first derive a statistical characterization of the fault-induced perturbations on both singlememristor and differential-pair weight encoding schemes. Our theoretical analysis reveals that while both encodings share the same mean scaling factor on the transition matrix, the differential-pair encoding yields a significantly smaller weight variance reducing the SAFs contribution and consequently tightens the spectral radius fluctuation bound to a markedly lower level. Building upon this analysis, we propose a three-level fault-tolerant framework tailored for differential-pair encoding: (i) design-time spectral radius pre-scaling, (ii) system-level calibration via covariance matching, and (iii) runtime adaptive readout via recursive least squares. Comparative evaluations against the state-of-the-art methods show that our approach outperforms both retraining-based and post-compensation baselines. Our methods improve 48.50% and 58.02%, at the 20% of SAFs, variations σ=0.20, with KITTI autonomous driving dataset and a fixed-wing UAV autonomous landing synthetic dataset, respectively. The proposed framework is particularly suitable for real-time edge deployment in autonomous systems where computational resources and power consumption are constrained.

articles.title: Blind prediction and local optical-field validation of a simplified micro-model for unreinforced masonry walls
articles.abstract: This paper tests a simplified micro-model for unreinforced masonry (URM) walls under a deliberately strict protocol, using the EPFL PUP dataset. Models of this class are a standard, practice-oriented assessment tool, but they are usually validated against the global force-displacement curve alone and re-tuned for each wall, so their internal behaviour is rarely checked, and a good fit can come from tuning rather than genuine prediction. To avoid both, the model is built in OpenSeesPy, calibrated on one wall (PUP2), frozen, and used to predict three walls with different boundary conditions (PUP3-PUP5) with no parameter changes. High-resolution optical LED tracking then tests the internal deformation field, not only the global response. Across the three blind walls, the frozen model under-predicts loaded-side capacity by 17-29% and over-degrades reload-side capacity by 27-99%. Both trace to one cause: the interface damage law cannot reproduce the reversible crack closure real masonry shows; once a joint cracks it stays open and degraded. On the three optically validated walls (PUP2, PUP3, PUP5), the model reproduces the rigid base rotation in both direction and magnitude, and distinguishes the shear-dominated wall from the flexural one by mechanism type. But it captures neither how the mechanism evolves with load nor, on the low-axial wall, the direction of the local shear/flexure response, which it inverts. These are not products of fitting but a mechanism-dependent ceiling of the simplified model class, reported here in full and set as a baseline against which a crack-closure re-architecture must be measured. The complete OpenSeesPy codebase, pinned execution environment, and processing scripts are released so the calibration, blind predictions, and optical comparison can be regenerated.

articles.title: Two actinobacterial G protein systems control multicellular mycelial growth and morphology in Streptomyces venezuelae
articles.abstract: Actinobacterial G protein systems (AGPS) are unique regulatory modules among bacteria that combine histidine kinase-like transmembrane receptors with Ras-like GTPase signalling. Filamentous Streptomyces bacteria have about ten AGPSs, encoded by the conservon (cvn) operons. To address their largely unknown biological roles, we systematically mutagenized all conservons in Streptomyces venezuelae. Here we show that two AGPSs encoded by cvn1-cvn2 operons regulate cell shape, hyphal self-avoidance, and multicellular mycelial organization in response to poor nutrition. Mutants lacking cvn1-cvn2 further exhibit hyphal bundling and upregulate genes associated with cell surface properties. Additionally, cvn1 mutants are compromised in multicellular and developmental phenomena at the colony level including exploratory growth. Suppressor mutations link these macrosocpic cvn1 phenotypes to developmental regulation and cyclic-di-GMP but show also that the effect on mycelial morphology is genetically distinct and mediated by different pathways. The results implicate two broadly conserved AGPSs in regulation of multicellular growth and morphology.

articles.title: Value-Oriented Design of Electrocatalytic PET Upcycling: Integrating Product Selection, Cathodic Pairing, and System Design
articles.abstract: The growing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste has intensified interest in upcycling strategies that recover its chemical value beyond conventional recycling. Electrocatalytic PET upcycling is particularly attractive because PET-derived terephthalic acid can be recovered while ethylene glycol (EG) is further valorized through anodic oxidation, with the additional possibility of replacing the oxygen evolution reaction and coupling PET conversion with useful cathodic transformations. Despite rapid progress in catalyst development, however, the field has largely been evaluated through activity, selectivity, and current-density metrics, whereas the broader value of the overall electrolysis process has received comparatively less attention. In this Analysis, we discuss electrocatalytic PET upcycling from a value-oriented and system-level standpoint. We consider how anodic product selection, catalyst requirements, energy demand, product economics, and cathodic reaction choice are interconnected, and use representative EG oxidation pathways to illustrate why catalytic performance alone is insufficient for assessing practical relevance. We further examine cathodic pairing as a coupled design problem that must account not only for electrochemical feasibility, but also for market relevance, technological maturity, and compatibility with PET-derived EG oxidation. By integrating catalyst-level performance with product- and system-level considerations, this Analysis aims to provide a framework for designing PET electrolysis systems that are not only electrochemically efficient but also practically and economically meaningful.

articles.title: A two-stage MPPT controller with energy-regret coordination and transition memory for PV systems under complex partial shading conditions
articles.abstract: Partial shading creates multiple peaks in the photovoltaic power--voltage characteristic and complicates maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Existing two-stage methods often ignore online probing losses and restart randomly after recurrent transitions. This study proposes ER-ISSA-IVY, a two-stage hybrid MPPT framework that combines an improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) for global exploration with the Ivy algorithm (IVY) for local refinement. An energy-regret-guided (ER) rule switches stages by comparing the uncertainty-adjusted marginal return of further exploration with the measured cost of off-MPP probing, and a training-free transition memory reuses verified peaks for recurrent power-change signatures while a globally initialized subpopulation preserves coverage of unseen conditions. Experiments show that ER-ISSA-IVY achieves 100% static efficiency, 94.35% dynamic efficiency under step irradiance, and 99.99% day-integrated efficiency on a satellite-derived profile, with the fewest first-hit evaluations among three recent hybrids, 0.77% overshoot and 0.07% ripple at the switching level, and complementary ablation-confirmed gains from both mechanisms under hidden change boundaries.

articles.title: The effect of frame roughness and geometry on an electrically rotating thin film
articles.abstract: Applying external crossed electric fields to a suspended liquid film induces rotational flow. In practice, the enclosing frame of the film has edge roughness and corner bluntness, particularly for rectangular frames. In this paper, we investigate the effects of frame shape, edge roughness, and corner sharpness on the rotational behavior of the film through experiments and simulations. By tracking a microscopic tracer embedded in the film, we show that the roughness and shape of the frame are initially sensed through the tracer’s trajectory and velocity, respectively. A frame-shape-dependent transition from circular fluidic streamlines to boundary-shaped streamlines is also observed. Simulations reveal that for rectangular frames, the curvature of the corners relative to the frame size governs this transition. The observations are explained using a model of charge induction in ohmic liquids coupled with hydrodynamic interactions. These findings may inform the design and application of integrated fluidic circuits.

articles.title: Illuminating early ZrC oxidation using ensemble small-cell DFT with dynamic gas management
articles.abstract: During zirconium carbide oxidation, liberated carbon can remain beneath the oxide or escape as gas, complicating the interpretation of mass measurements. We adapt the small-cell ensemble method using sixteen 140 ps ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories at 873--1273 K under a sustained high oxygen flux with gas removal. The average rates of net mass gain and total carbon transfer into gas or retained chains follow Arrhenius trends. Above 973 K, gas evolution levels off while total carbon transfer increases. The fraction of transferred carbon retained in chains rises from 40% at 973 K to 66% at 1273 K. Fits after 40 ps suggest declining carbon transfer rates over time, although not in every trajectory. These results show that carbon partitioning during early oxidation depends on temperature, with increasing temperature above 973 K favouring chain formation over gasification.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Challenges in AI-Enabled Car Rental Systems: Protecting Digital Booking, Fleet Management, and Customer Data
articles.abstract: The rapid digitalization of car-rental services has transformed booking, customer verification, demand prediction, fleet monitoring, predictive maintenance, and automated customer support. However, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, cloud platforms, and connected-vehicle technologies has simultaneously expanded the cybersecurity attack surface of car-rental operations (Mohammed, 2026; Suaprae et al., 2026; Potdar & Parikh, 2025). This article examines the cybersecurity challenges associated with AI-enabled car rental systems, focusing on risks to customer identity information, payment data, location records, booking information, telematics, application programming interfaces (APIs), cloud infrastructure, and AI models. A literature-based analytical approach was employed to synthesize evidence from recent research on AI-enabled car rental management, smart tourism, IoT-based fleet management, digital trust, and AI adoption. The analysis identifies interconnected cybersecurity challenges involving data privacy, unauthorized access, API vulnerabilities, connected-vehicle threats, AI-related risks, and weaknesses across digitally integrated enterprise systems. Based on these findings, the article develops a layered protection framework that integrates cybersecurity controls, AI governance, privacy protection, secure system architecture, and human oversight. The analysis indicates that cybersecurity in AI-enabled car rental systems should be addressed as a multidimensional organizational and technological challenge rather than solely as a conventional IT-security concern.

articles.title: Minimising Financial Risk under Enrolment Uncertainty: An Open-Source Entropy-Indexed POMDP Tool for University Governance
articles.abstract: Universities must commit resources years ahead of the enrolment outcomes that fund them; the UK regulator identifies persistently over-optimistic forecasting as a systemic planning weakness. The difficulty is structural: existing instruments require governing bodies to agree probability judgements about contested futures---which the literature shows they cannot reliably do. This paper reports an operational research response: an entropy-indexed partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), delivered as an open-source decision-support system for university financial planning. A Bayesian belief distribution over latent financial regimes is updated from each year's enrolment signal; its Shannon entropy serves as an uncertainty index that automatically constrains irreversible commitments while evidential ambiguity is high. The system is calibrated on a decade of open HESA data from four Russell Group institutions (2014/15--2024/25) with materially different trajectories; a five-level pathway takes a finance director from first use to a committee-ready Board Pack in under an hour. Monte Carlo evaluation across 500 enrolment futures shows the entropy-conditioned strategy achieving the highest mean financial reward with the lowest crisis probability among six comparators. Management implications are analysed across four institutional archetypes, including the post-2022 international shock, and transferability to other national systems facing similar volatility is assessed.

articles.title: High-Speed Steerable Polar Crystal Motors Powered by Photoinduced Inverse Piezoelectricity
articles.abstract: Energy conversion underpins both natural processes and modern technologies,1,2 yet direct conversion of light into mechanical motion remains comparatively rare.3–7 Existing photomechanical systems generally rely on intermediate chemical or thermal energy states, limiting their ability to generate rapid, directional mechanical motion from light. We report the first electrically mediated light-to-mechanical motion conversion, realized through polar and elastic crystal motors derived from a nonpolar heptazine. Under scanning light, two polymorphs move unidirectionally at up to 1.0 µm/s, 60-fold faster than prior photomotile crystals. Mechanistically, light irradiation generates a bulk photovoltaic effect that modulates the internal field of the crystals, inducing anisotropic inverse piezoelectric deformation. The resulting elastic energy is converted into sustained directional motion by the moving optical front, propelling the crystals antiparallel to the scanning direction. This inverse piezoelectric effect provides a direct pathway from light to mechanical motion without requiring photochemistry or photothermal effects. Beyond these classical approaches, this introduces a third photomechanical paradigm, enabling precise, fast, real-world wireless microactuation.

articles.title: Antagonistic Corners of Min-Selectors: Geometry, Switching Dynamics, and Nagumo Invariance
articles.abstract: We study selectors of the form beta(x) = minᵢ Deltaᵢ(x) with C¹ margin functions, focusing on the boundary corners where several margins become simultaneously minimal and the selector loses smoothness. At a corner, the Clarke subdifferential is the convex hull of the active gradients, and the recovery cone is empty precisely when this convex hull contains the origin -- the antagonistic case, which coincides with the Pareto-stationarity condition of multiobjective optimization. By Gordan's theorem of the alternative this is equivalent to the cone of active gradients not being pointed, or to the persistence cone having empty interior. We give a simple submanifold example in which antagonism is induced by admissibility constraints, with no obstruction present in the ambient space, and a three-margin instance on an adsorption frontier in which the induced antagonism is a sign-only statement. Using this geometry, we define a three-zone classification of first-order active-margin response at boundary points and show that full first-order recovery is unattainable at antagonistic corners for any vector field. We further characterize the contingent tangent cone of the collapse set as the complement of the recovery cone, so that Nagumo tangency is vacuous at antagonistic corners, and prove a Nagumo-type forward-invariance criterion. Since affine active margins force an empty viable region at an antagonistic corner, the existence of viable antagonistic corners is a second-order fact; we state the deciding conditions, transposed from second-order Pareto optimality theory, in terms of the Hessians of the active margins weighted by the antagonistic multipliers. Finally, a node and a saddle at the same antagonistic cusp show that whether collapse freezes or selects a breaking margin is decided by the stability type of the corner equilibrium, and we define the argmin-switch event and the exit point that a practitioner can observe. A synthetic cascading-failure benchmark illustrates the resulting behaviours: an adverse argmin switch preceding breach with positive lead time, margin freezing on the boundary, and a sharp viability boundary in parameter space. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary: 34A60; Secondary: 49J52, 49J53, 52A20.

articles.title: On-surface synthesis of indigo-based porphyrinoids and quadruply fused porphyrinoid oligomers with aromatic eight-membered rings
articles.abstract: Tailored porphyrinoid nanostructures are captivating and promising systems providing versatile optoelectronic and chemical properties or templates for complexed atoms. Here we report a novel Fe-porphyrinoid fabricated from indigo on Au(111). Its on-surface synthesis is mediated by Fe coordination driven isomerization affording a pocket template to position and spatially orient precursor moïeties, facilitating a regiospecific reaction pathway. Further deoxygenative and dehydrogenative C–C couplings steps yield oligomers with quadruple linkages featuring fused six-membered as well as aromatic eight-membered rings. The reaction steps and products are thoroughly characterized by a combination of scanning tunnelling microscopy, bond-resolving atomic force microscopy, and density functional theory investigations. These findings introduce a distinct strategy to realize macrocyclic tetrapyrroles and quadruply fused porphyrinoids, paving the way for the fabrication of novel interfacial nanostructures.

articles.title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints for hyperbolic lattices
articles.abstract: Author(s): G. Shankar and Joseph Maciejko The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem powerfully constrains the low-energy behavior of quantum many-body systems. In spin systems with spin rotation and conventional (Euclidean) lattice translation symmetries, it forbids a unique, gapped, symmetric ground state at half-odd-integer spin per unit cell. Here, the authors generalize this theorem to hyperbolic lattices — synthetic structures that emulate negatively curved space. articles.title: Orbital-pseudospin switching reconstructs the competing exchange network in monolayer VN
articles.abstract: Orbital degrees of freedom provide an efficient microscopic route for controlling exchange interactions in two-dimensional magnets, but a clear structural handle for switching orbital-polarized exchange networks remains rare. Here, using first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, we identify planar rectangular monolayer VN as an itinerant ferromagnet with an out-of-plane easy axis and an equilibrium Curie temperature of about 420 K. At equilibrium, the rectangular crystal field polarizes the d xz /d yz doublet, producing a direction-resolved exchange network in which strong ferromagnetic J a and diagonal J ab couplings coexist with an antiferromagnetic J b channel. By tuning the lattice parameter b at fixed a, the rectangular field is continuously varied through the square geometry, driving a d xz -to-d yz orbital-pseudospin reversal. This orbital redistribution converts J b from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic and reconstructs the competing exchange topology into a cooperative ferromagnetic network, raising T C to a broad plateau around 490 K, corresponding to an enhancement of about 18%. Orbital-resolved ICOHP analysis shows that the static V–N bonding and the p z -mediated π channel weaken overall under b-axis tuning, ruling out bond strengthening as the origin of the exchange enhancement. These results establish rectangular-distortion-driven orbital-pseudospin switching as a microscopic mechanism for engineering robust above-room-temperature ferromagnetism in two-dimensional metallic magnets.

articles.title: Effective Conservation and Bistability of Atomic Alignment under Strong Spin~Exchange
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.20741v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a phenomenological model of anomalous alignment signals in dense cesium vapor under linearly polarized pumping and fast spin exchange near zero magnetic field. Despite the absence of a conservation law for rank-2 angular momentum, our recent experiments reveal anisotropic narrow resonances, hysteresis, and bistability. We attribute these effects to a stretched state forming a collective mode in which orientation and alignment are bidirectionally coupled. This mode acts as a reservoir, preserving the essential properties of alignment despite rapid spin exchange.

articles.title: Computing shear viscosities from molecular dynamics simulations: Comparing the OrthoBoXY approach with the Green–Kubo method
articles.abstract: We calculated shear viscosities of 15 molecular liquids from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations using the OrthoBoXY approach and compared them to viscosities calculated via the Green–Kubo method. Data from both methods agree reasonably well. We discuss how to avoid pitfalls while computing the OrthoBoXY data to obtain optimal results. From simulations of multiple system sizes, we verify that the viscosity of molecular liquids is not influenced by finite size effects down to systems as small as 250 molecules. Moreover, we also demonstrate that the standard error of the viscosity is nearly independent of the system size. This is a consequence of a compensation effect of an increasing accuracy of the self-diffusion coefficients with increasing system size and the system-size dependent weighting according to the OrthoBoXY equation. Consequently, we suggest that it is preferable to run simulations of smaller systems with longer simulation times rather than larger systems with shorter simulation runs. Moreover, we discuss a refinement of the recently introduced “recipe” for OrthoBoXY simulations block-lengths: for highly viscous systems, the value of τ block might safely be scaled by a factor of 1/8, significantly reducing the computational resources. For less viscous systems, the value of τ block might safely be scaled by a factor of 1/4. For systems with high fluidity, the value of τ block should not be scaled down in order to achieve reliable results. When using a smaller system size of 250 molecules, these refinements are leading up to a 24-fold reduction in computational cost compared to the previous recommended setup without sacrificing numerical accuracy.

articles.title: Plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene across dispersive and flat bands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.20158v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamical dielectric response of twisted bilayer graphene is explored in large-angle dispersive-band and small-angle quasi-flat-band regimes using time-dependent density-functional theory within the random-phase approximation. At the reference bilayer-graphene interlayer distance, weak coupling in the largest-angle structures preserves Dirac dispersions and the intrinsic π plasmon. Electron doping activates a two-dimensional Dirac plasmon with energies obeying approximate geometric twist-angle scaling, while acoustic-like branches remain embedded in the single-particle continuum. The prohibitively large first-magic-angle supercell is represented by a tractable cell with its interlayer separation reduced to the angle-dependent magic distance, where four quasi-flat bands emerge around the Fermi level. Their partial occupation produces a dispersive low-energy plasmon-like excitation without a clear dielectric zero at resonance. A distinct interband plasmon is instead identified, supported by transitions involving the quasi-flat manifold and neighboring high-density-of-states regions. Band-energy rescaling places its characteristic energy in the mid-infrared range of interband collective excitations measured near the magic angle.

articles.title: Non-Thermal Effects in Fermionic Atoms Coupled to Open Cavities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.20434v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Fermi-Hubbard model coupled to a open dissipative single cavity mode. Using Keldysh diagrammatics we derive and solve the quantum kinetic equations for the fermions, taking the bosonic cavity mode as a source of non-equilibrium noise and dissipation. In absence of Hubbard interactions we show that the fermions reach generically a non-equilibrium steady-state, characterized by a non-thermal distribution function. Quite interestingly we demonstrate that the latter exactly nullifies the heat-current between fermions and cavity mode. We discuss the regimes of parameters where a low-frequency effective temperature description emerges and how the fluctuations affect the mean-field phase diagram for the superradiance phase transition. Finally we include Hubbard interaction in the weak-coupling regime and show that it leads to a crossover towards a full equilibrium distribution.

articles.title: Deep-penetration keyhole behaviour and weld pool morphology evolution mechanismsin K-TIG welding of low-carbon steel under variable inclination angles
articles.title_zh: 变倾角下低碳钢K-TIG焊深穿透小孔行为与焊池形貌演化机理
articles.abstract: To meet the demand for all-position welding of long-distance pipelines and thick-plate structures, the destabilisation of the K-TIG deep-penetration keyhole by welding inclination was investigated for 8 mm Q235 low-carbon steel, combining flat-position experiments with three-dimensional transient numerical simulation. A Fluent VOF multiphysics model coupling Gaussian arc pressure, surface tension and Marangoni shear, electromagnetic force, thermal buoyancy and spatial gravity decomposition was established and validated against the 0° experiment (relative errors of 2.5% and 4.8% for the top and back bead widths), then extrapolated to 10°, 20° and 30°. With increasing angle, the keyhole degrades through four stages: stable penetration, size shrinkage, near closure and complete closure. At 30°, after a brief penetration at 0.6 s, the keyhole closes prematurely at 2.5–3.2 mm from the plate bottom as the tangential gravity component drives directional backfilling of liquid metal. The pool flow switches from symmetric circulatory convection (≈ 0.11 m/s) to directional scouring opposite the welding direction (> 0.5 m/s at 30°, instantaneous peak 0.81 m/s). Keyhole closure blocks direct arc radiation to the plate bottom, degrading heat transfer to conduction and causing incomplete back penetration. The root cause is the tangential gravity component—the only force that appears with inclination—which breaks the "arc pressure–surface tension–gravity" balance of flat welding and cannot be offset by adjusting current or speed. These results reveal the full mechanistic chain across keyhole behaviour, flow pattern and heat transfer path, providing a theoretical basis for external-field regulation of all-position deep-penetration welding.
articles.abstract_zh: 为满足长输管道和厚板结构全位置焊接的需求，将平位试验与三维瞬态数值模拟相结合，研究了8 mm Q235低碳钢K-TIG深穿孔的焊接倾角失稳问题。建立了耦合高斯电弧压力、表面张力和Marangoni剪切、电磁力、热浮力和空间重力分解的Fluent VOF多物理场模型，并与0°实验进行了验证（上、后胎圈宽度的相对误差分别为2.5%和4.8% ） ，然后外推至10°、20°和30°。随着角度的增加，钥匙孔通过四个阶段退化：稳定的穿透、尺寸收缩、近封闭和完全封闭。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 为满足长输管道和厚板结构全位置焊接的需求，将平位试验与三维瞬态数值模拟相结合，研究了8 mm Q235低碳钢K-TIG深穿孔的焊接倾角失稳问题。建立了耦合高斯电弧压力、表面张力和Marangoni剪切、电磁力、热浮力和空间重力分解的Fluent VOF多物理场模型，并与0°实验进行了验证（上、后胎圈宽度的相对误差分别为2.5%和4.8% ） ，然后外推至10°、20°和30°。随着角度的增加，钥匙孔通过四个阶段退化：稳定的穿透、尺寸收缩、近封闭和完全封闭。在30°时，在0.6秒的短暂穿透后，由于切向重力分量驱动液态金属的定向回填，钥匙孔在距离板底2.5-3.2毫米处过早关闭。池流从对称循环对流（ ≈ 0.11 m/s ）切换到与焊接方向相反的定向冲刷（ 30°时> 0.5 m/s ，瞬时峰值0.81 m/s ）。钥匙孔封闭可阻挡电弧直接辐射到板底部，降低传导热量，导致不完全回穿。根本原因是切向重力分量-唯一出现倾斜的力-打破了平焊的“电弧压力-表面张力-重力”平衡，不能通过调整电流或速度来抵消。这些结果揭示了跨越小孔行为、流动模式和传热路径的全机械链，为全位置深穿透焊接的外场调节提供了理论基础。

articles.title: Interplay between spinodal decomposition and wetting in ternary to quinary mixtures
articles.title_zh: 三元到五元混合物中旋节线分解和润湿之间的相互作用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.06946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use two-dimensional phase-field simulations based on the Cahn--Hilliard description to study spinodal decomposition in N-component mixtures with N = 3, 4, 5. In particular, we consider surface-directed spinodal decomposition in which one of the coexisting phases serves as a filler particle, while the remaining components phase separate around its surface. We investigate both nonwetting and wetting conditions by varying the interfacial tensions between the particle and the other components. The competition between wetting kinetics and spinodal decomposition produces rich morphological evolution, including the formation of lattice, droplet, and target (or core-shell) morphologies. The target pattern consists of alternating component-rich rings around the particle. In the intermediate-to-late time regime, these structures undergo further morphological transitions driven by curvature-induced depletion of wetting layers and subsequent coarsening of the surrounding domains, resulting in the breakup of target patterns into isolated domains of the matrix components. We find that domain coarsening slows down systematically as the number of components increases, while wetting accelerates it in all cases. The resulting morphologies and phase-separation pathways demonstrate how particle--component interactions can be used to control microstructural evolution in multicomponent mixtures, with potential implications for systems ranging from industrial materials to cellular biology.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们使用基于 Cahn-Hilliard 描述的二维相场模拟来研究 N = 3、4、5 的 N 组分混合物中的旋节线分解。特别是，我们考虑表面定向旋节线分解，其中共存相之一充当填料颗粒，而其余组分在其表面周围相分离。我们通过改变颗粒和其他组分之间的界面张力来研究非润湿和润湿条件。润湿动力学和旋节线分解之间的竞争产生丰富的形态演化，包括晶格、液滴和目标（或核-壳）形态的形成。目标图案由颗粒周围交替的富含成分的环组成。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们使用基于 Cahn-Hilliard 描述的二维相场模拟来研究 N = 3、4、5 的 N 组分混合物中的旋节线分解。特别是，我们考虑表面定向旋节线分解，其中共存相之一充当填料颗粒，而其余组分在其表面周围相分离。我们通过改变颗粒和其他组分之间的界面张力来研究非润湿和润湿条件。润湿动力学和旋节线分解之间的竞争产生丰富的形态演化，包括晶格、液滴和目标（或核-壳）形态的形成。目标图案由颗粒周围交替的富含成分的环组成。在中后期阶段，这些结构在曲率引起的润湿层耗尽和随后周围域的粗化驱动下经历进一步的形态转变，导致目标图案分解成基质成分的孤立域。我们发现，随着组件数量的增加，域粗化会系统性地减慢，而润湿在所有情况下都会加速它。由此产生的形态和相分离途径证明了如何利用颗粒-组分相互作用来控制多组分混合物中的微观结构演化，这对从工业材料到细胞生物学的系统具有潜在的影响。

articles.title: PT-symmetry as Effective Time Reversal Symmetry for Anderson Localization in a Collinear Antiferromagnet
articles.title_zh: PT 对称性作为共线反铁磁体中安德森定位的有效时间反演对称性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.06951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that PT-symmetry acts as the effective time-reversal symmetry governing Anderson localization in the antiferromagnet BaMn₂Bi₂, whereas the general time-reversal symmetry is broken by its long-range magnetic order. The magnetoconductance follows the laws established from breaking time-reversal symmetry throuhg the orbital coupling of charge carriers to the magnet vector potential, however, the degrees of symmetry breaking are qualitatively modulated by the magnetocrystalline anisotropy stabilizing PT-related sublattices. The quantum interferences and hoping amplitudes governing the phenomena are drastically impaired by transverse magnetic fields, which readily cant PT-related magnetic sublattices. Accordingly, when the PT-related texture is weakly perturbed by longitudinal fields orienting along the sublattices, the localization is minutely affected. The robustness of the PT-enforced degeneracies is thus governed by exchange and magnetocrystalline interactions, in contrast to the exact PT-symmetry of the full Hamiltonian, which is broken by any finite field.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们证明，PT 对称性是反铁磁体 BaMn2Bi2 中控制安德森局域化的有效时间反演对称性，而一般时间反演对称性则被其长程磁序破坏。磁导遵循通过电荷载流子与磁体矢量势的轨道耦合打破时间反转对称性而建立的定律，然而，对称性破坏的程度由磁晶各向异性稳定 PT 相关的亚晶格定性地调制。控制这些现象的量子干涉和希望振幅受到横向磁场的严重损害，横向磁场很容易倾斜 PT 相关的磁性亚晶格。因此，当 PT 相关纹理受到沿子晶格定向的纵向场微弱扰动时，定位受到微小影响。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们证明，PT 对称性是反铁磁体 BaMn2Bi2 中控制安德森局域化的有效时间反演对称性，而一般时间反演对称性则被其长程磁序破坏。磁导遵循通过电荷载流子与磁体矢量势的轨道耦合打破时间反转对称性而建立的定律，然而，对称性破坏的程度由磁晶各向异性稳定 PT 相关的亚晶格定性地调制。控制这些现象的量子干涉和希望振幅受到横向磁场的严重损害，横向磁场很容易倾斜 PT 相关的磁性亚晶格。因此，当 PT 相关纹理受到沿子晶格定向的纵向场微弱扰动时，定位受到微小影响。因此，PT 强制简并性的鲁棒性由交换和磁晶相互作用控制，这与完整哈密顿量的精确 PT 对称性相反，后者会被任何有限场破坏。

articles.title: CrystalJev: thinking fast and slow with atomistic foundation models for materials discovery
articles.title_zh: CrystalJev：用原子基础模型快速和慢速思考材料发现
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.06985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomistic foundation models triage millions of hypothetical materials but are used as slow simulators, their thresholded energies taken at face value. They are better read as fast decision-makers. CrystalJev queries a frozen interatomic potential once per unrelaxed structure and answers typed questions with calibrated probabilities, finite-sample guarantees and a rule for when to think slowly. Across 65 Matbench Discovery models, a 'stable' call is a probability in disguise, explained by a model's errors and the candidate population. Once trained, one forward pass decides nearly as well as a relaxation at a thirtieth of its cost, and a value-of-information theory sends slower computation only where decisions can change. The same layer answers electronic, mechanical and molecular questions.
