Its NDVI–LST cooling slope was also consistently about twice as steep as Islamabad’s (slope z = 27–39, p < 0.0001), meaning each unit of vegetation cooled more where impervious cover was densest. Yet the multivariate model pointed to built-up density, not average greenness, as the dominant control on LST in both cities. Together, these results suggest that planning context and land-cover configuration, rather than vegetation abundance alone, govern how efficiently a city’s surface cools.

articles.title: Low-Cost Gold Nanoparticle-Coated Aluminium Foil for SERS Detection of Chlorpyrifos in Honey
articles.abstract: Rapid, low-cost detection of pesticide residues in honey remains challenging because its complex, sugar-rich matrix limits the performance of portable analytical techniques. Here, we integrate QuEChERS extraction with a surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) platform based on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) deposited on commercial aluminium foil (ALF) to enable sensitive detection of chlorpyrifos (CPY) in honey. Aluminium foil coated with unmodified gold nanoparticles (ALF@AuNP) demonstrated superior Raman enhancement owing to plasmonic coupling, as confirmed by both simulations and experimental data. Coupling QuEChERS with the ALF@AuNP substrate achieved a detection limit of 4.8 × 10⁻⁷ M for chlorpyrifos for CPY while simultaneously reducing matrix interference. Residual extraction salts also promoted AuNP aggregation, increasing SERS hotspot density and improving analytical sensitivity. Principal component analysis further discriminated CPY from structurally related organophosphate pesticides in honey extracts. This simple, inexpensive and portable SERS–QuEChERS platform provides a practical approach for rapid pesticide screening in complex food matrices.

articles.title: Criterion Uncertainty and the Limits of Framing: Identification and Parameter-Free Tests of a Quantum-Probabilistic Choice Model
articles.abstract: Latent-class choice models let a respondent apply one of several evaluative criteria but leave the assignment of criteria to contexts unrestricted: a separate class distribution may be fitted to every frame, wording, or question order. Such a specification records framing effects without restricting them. This paper asks what is gained by generating all frame-specific class distributions from one latent criterion state acted on by frame-specific measurements, using the mathematics of quantum probability, and answers it completely. Within a single frame the model is observationally equivalent to finite-mixture logit, its equivalent set of states has affine dimension (:K²-K), and its choice probabilities always admit a random-utility representation, so no single-frame test of stochastic rationality has power against it. Across frames the model becomes sharp. A Schur–Horn argument shows that the attainable set of criterion distributions is exactly the permutohedron generated by the state’s spectrum: framing can redistribute criterion probability but never push its entropy below that of the state, and certainty requires a pure state. The state is identified if and only if the frame projectors span the Hermitian operator space, which needs at least (:K+1) frames, and mutually unbiased frames deliver a parameter-free two-sided bound on an observable quadratic form. For sequential frames an exact order-effect law shows that order effects vanish both when frames commute and when they are maximally incompatible. Monte Carlo experiments confirm correct size, useful power, and out-of-sample predictive content. JEL classification: C25; C52; D01; D91

articles.title: Impedance spectroscopic studies on polyindole by the dispersion of CdS nanoparticles for solid state electronics applications
articles.abstract: In this research report, we have synthesized polyindole-cadmium sulfide nanocomposites by means of chemical oxidative polymerization technique. The analysis highlights the dispersion of cadmium sulfide (CdS) nanoparticles in polyindole (PIn) to enhance the dielectric characteristics of the synthesized nanocomposites. The structural evaluation of as-synthesized nanocomposites was carried out by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) techniques. The impedance spectroscopy technique in the frequency and temperature ranges 20 Hz – 1 MHz and 308–393 K respectively was employed to investigate the transport properties of as-synthesized composites under study. The frequency variation of AC electrical conductivity for the obtained samples obeys Jonscher power law. The complex electric modulus spectra indicated the non-Debye nature of the prepared materials.

articles.title: Congo red photocatalytic degradation on the copper nanoparticles deposited on carriers
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic removal of dyes from aqueous solutions is an important process in the context of environmental protection due to synthetic dyes are common pollutants that are difficult to biodegrade and have negative impacts on ecosystems. The aim of the present work was to compare photocatalytical properties of copper nanoparticles deposited on two inorganic carriers: gamma alumina and natural cliniptilolite type zeolite. Copper-containing samples (4.5 wt. % of Cu) were obtained by impregnation of copper nitrate and its reduction with ascorbic acid. Catalysts were characterized by means of XRD, XRF, TEM, SEM, and low temperature nitrogen adsorption/desorption. The formation of nanoparticles was confirmed by TEM images. Particles predominant dimension for both samples was 2–3 nm. However, zeolite sample possesses some bigger agglomerates of 30 nm. Based on XRD data it is suggested that nanoparticles have core-shell structure and consist of Cu0 core and Cu2O shell. Photocatalytic degradation of Congo Red solutions was carried out. Both catalysts were active in decolorization and can be used as effective photocatalysts, but Cu-alumina sample activity prevails under the Cu-zeolite ones. Its better performance supposed to be connected with better sample mesoporosity and higher part of nanoparticles of 2 nm dimension.

articles.title: Thermoring-driven cold activation of TRPM8
articles.abstract: Activation of TRPM8 in neurons by PIP2, either alone or in combination with the cooling agents menthol or icilin/Ca2+, is temperature-dependent.  However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this temperature sensitivity remain unclear.  Here, 3D cryo-EM structures of TRPM8 from three species, captured in states gated by PIP2 with or without cooling agents at low temperatures, were analyzed using a highly-sensitive thermoring energetic model.  The results showed that the open state has a lower matched melting threshold than the closed or inactivated states, which may account for specific cold sensitivity mediated by TRPM8.  The melting thresholds were determined by the weakest tertiary noncovalent bridges.  Although the weakest bridge in the inactivated state was located within the pore domain, the weakest bridges in the closed and open states were located on the surface of the N-terminal domain, which interacts with the C-terminal domain.  Thus, thermoring rearrangement throughout the entire polypeptide chain, together with the gating coupling of the N-terminal domain with the pore domain, is required for channel opening and matched cold sensitivity.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of Catalytic Methods for Soybean Oil Epoxidation: Physicochemical Characterization and Process Performance
articles.abstract: Epoxidized soybean oil (ESBO) is a valuable bio-based intermediate for plasticizers, adhesives, and biocomposites, yet the influence of catalytic system selection on its physicochemical properties remains insufficiently benchmarked under standardized conditions. This study comparatively evaluated three catalytic epoxidation systems for soybean oil (SBO); (i) 85% formic acid (FA) with 35% hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), (ii) FA combined with sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and H2O2, and (iii) glacial acetic acid (AA) with H2O2, under identical reaction conditions (65 °C, 600 rpm, H2O2 loading of 2 mol/mol of C=C, 50 min addition time (tadd), and 6 h stirring (tstr), for a total reaction time (t) of 6.8 h). The resulting epoxidized products (ESBO1, ESBO2, and ESBO3, respectively) were characterized for oxirane oxygen content (OOC), iodine value (IV), acid value (AV), viscosity (η), density (ρ), color, and conversion of unsaturation (XSBO). The AA system (ESBO3) achieved the highest OOC (6.8 wt%), the lowest IV (1.91 ± 0.01 g/100 g) and AV (0.60 ± 0.01 mg KOH/g), the highest η (332 ± 1 cP) and ρ (0.996 ± 0.001 g/mL), and the lightest product color, corresponding to an XSBO of 98.53% within 6.8 h. In contrast, the FA-only system (ESBO1) exhibited the lowest OOC (3.5 wt%) and the highest IV (8.65 ± 0.01 g/100 g) and AV (0.87 ± 0.01 mg KOH/g), while the mixed FA/ H2O2 system (ESBO2) showed intermediate performance (OOC 5.8 wt%; IV 3.12 ± 0.01 g/100 g). These results, which are comparable to or exceed literature benchmarks (OOC 6.2–7.45 wt%; XSBO 95.2–98.53% at t of 2.3–10.42 h), indicate that AA system provides a superior balance of epoxidation efficiency, product stability, and t relative to FA systems, and represents the most promising catalytic procedure for the epoxidation of SBO under the tested conditions.

articles.title: Resilience-Aware Multi-Objective Energy Management for Solar-Battery Microgrids Under Renewable Generation and Load Uncertainty
articles.abstract: Solar battery microgrids face operational challenges caused by variable photovoltaic generation, changing electricity demand, battery limitations, and utility grid interruptions. This study develops a resilience aware multi objective energy management framework that coordinates photovoltaic generation, battery storage, utility exchange, flexible demand, and critical loads under grid connected and islanded conditions. The framework represents renewable and load variation through operating scenarios and jointly considers operating cost, battery degradation, renewable curtailment, energy not served, and critical load service. A controlled simulation using the IEEE 33 Bus Distribution System evaluates the framework over a 24 hour horizon with an 8 kWh battery and outage durations of two, four, and six hours. For the six hour outage, the proposed strategy reduces grid import from 11.92 kWh to 4.86 kWh and renewable curtailment from 8.58 kWh to 0.00 kWh. Critical load energy not served decreases from 9.57 kWh to 4.04 kWh, while critical load service increases from 74.11% to 89.07%. These results indicate that the framework can allocate limited energy toward critical demand during islanded operation while reducing renewable curtailment and grid dependence.

articles.title: Green Synthesis, Characterization and Insecticidal Activity of Pelargonium graveolens-Mediated Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles Against the Stored-Product Pest Tribolium confusum
articles.abstract: Tribolium confusum Jacquelin du Val (Coleoptera: Tenebrionidae) is one of the most destructive pests of stored grain products worldwide. The present study aimed to synthesize zinc oxide nanoparticles (PG-ZnONPs) using Pelargonium graveolens essential oil through an eco-friendly green synthesis approach and to evaluate their insecticidal activity against T. confusum adults. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized using UV–Visible spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). UV–Vis analysis showed a characteristic absorption peak at 361 nm, confirming the formation of ZnO nanoparticles. SEM observations revealed predominantly quasi-spherical nanoparticles with sizes ranging from 6.7 to 24.6 nm and an average diameter of 14.9 nm. XRD analysis confirmed the crystalline hexagonal wurtzite structure of ZnO, while FTIR spectra demonstrated the involvement of essential oil phytochemicals in nanoparticle stabilization. Contact toxicity bioassays revealed significant insecticidal activity against T. confusum adults, with mortality increasing in a concentration-dependent manner and reaching 86.67% at 150 mg/mL after 24 h of exposure. Probit analysis estimated an LC50 value of 5.5 mg/mL. The findings demonstrate that PG-ZnONPs represent a promising eco-friendly alternative to conventional insecticides for the sustainable management of stored-product pests.

articles.title: Earthquake drainage and drought timing
articles.abstract: Earthquakes can increase river discharge while changing the subsurface stores that sustain subsequent low flows. Whether faster postseismic drainage necessarily increases drought vulnerability remains unresolved at catchment scale. We combine a transient storage-drainage model with 1,128 usable catchment-earthquake-sequence comparisons from 335 catchments in New Zealand and Chile. The model yields an exact condition for an initial flow increase to become a later deficit during uninterrupted recession: integrated drainage enhancement must exceed the logarithmic gain in accessible storage. Rapid recovery of drainage pathways can instead accelerate recession without producing a late deficit. An ensemble of 480,766 recharge and drought scenarios extends this distinction to delayed drought onset. Observations do not establish a general persistent loss of catchment memory. For Kaikoura, the best-supported exposure comparison, the strong-minus-light shaking contrast in log recession-rate change is -0.009, with a 95% spatial-block interval of -0.157 to 0.100. Most other sequences lack adequate exposure overlap or spatial replication. These results distinguish an observable recession change from the storage depletion required for earthquake-amplified drought and identify the measurements needed to connect them.

articles.title: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Mesoporous TiO₂ Nanoparticles Using Pluronic Copolymer and EDTA: Synthesis, Characterization, and Photocatalytic Studies
articles.abstract: The mesoporous TiO2 nanoparticles were synthesized with Pluronic F-127 non-ionic copolymer and EDTA surfactant by hydrothermal method. The structural, morphological optical and photocatalytic properties of the TiO2 nanoparticles were analyzed by X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, High Resolution Scanning Electron Microscopy, Transmission Electron Microscopy, BET surface area, UV-VIS absorption spectroscopy, photoluminescence spectroscopy, photocatalysis and decay time studies. The XRD and Raman spectroscopy confirmed the tetragonal anatase TiO2 nanoparticles. Raman spectroscopy revealed the phonon modes characteristic to the anatase TiO2 at 153.4, 204.7 and 638.2 cm− 1 is related to the E1vibrational modes, 394.6 cm− 1 for the B1g vibrational mode and 512.6 cm− 1 attributed to A1g mode. The optical absorption of the TiO2 is centered at 360 nm. At this UV light excitation, the TiO2 gives emission in the visible region, in which the emission at 427 nm is stronger than that occurred at 534 nm wavelength. FESEM examination showed the nanoparticles are agglomerated to form as spherical-nano clusters. TEM analysis shows that the average particle size of the prepared TiO2 was measured to be 11 nm along with that SAED pattern shows the interplanar distance of d (101) = 0.342nm. The BET nitrogen adsorption-desorption studies revealed a hysteresis loop consistent with type IV isotherm typical to mesoporous material. The BET surface area of the mesoporous TiO2 nanoparticle is 45.043m2g− 1 and the average pore diameter is 39 nm. The mesoporous TiO2 nanoparticle with high surface area and pore size, the dye degradation studies showed an efficiency of 76%, and the results show that mesoporous anatase TiO2 can be used for photocatalytic applications.

articles.title: Utilizing low-melting-point oxides for high-temperature solid state reaction to enhance the upconversion luminescence intensity
articles.abstract: In the traditional solid-state sintering method, the addition of low-melting-point (LMP) oxides (MoO₃, Sb₂O₃, TeO2) promotes tantalate crystal growth and significantly enhances the upconversion luminescence (UCL) intensity. Compared with the samples (S23 sample) without the addition of LMP oxides, the green UCL integral strength of S19 sample with Sb2O3 has increased by 20 times. The experiment proved that LMP oxides are prone to erode the corundum crucible at high temperatures, causing the aluminum element to enter the samples. Therefore, a series of samples by changing Er3+/Yb3+ doping concentrations and the holding time were synthesized using platinum crucibles. The experiments showed that the Sb-Ta-O:Er3+/Yb3+ sample (S26 sample) with the optimal 0.01Er3+/0.06Yb3+ concentration had the optimal UCL intensity. The main phase of S26 sample is L-Ta2O5, along with some (Er/Yb)Ta7O19 phases and (Er/Yb)TaO4 phases. The morphology of this sample is characterized by a porous structure, which is caused by the volatilization of cations in LMP oxides. The morphological results can indicate that the aforementioned three phases have a symbiotic characteristic. The application implementation examples demonstrate that the Sb-Ta-O:Er3+/Yb3+ phosphor can be applied in the fields of temperature sensing and UCL display.

articles.title: From Slots to Relations: Object-Centric Graph World-Action Models for Relational Robot Manipulation
articles.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple policy prediction with future-state prediction, but object-centric variants often leave pairwise structure implicit. We study whether explicitly representing continuous geometry and typed object relations improves relational manipulation when capacity, data, and conditioning are controlled. Object-Centric Graph World-Action Models (OC-GWAM) encode object graphs with an edge-aware graph transformer, temporal encoder, and separate policy and world adapters. Three synthetic benchmarks progressively increase relational difficulty. On RelGraph-v3, geometry-only input gives the lowest direct-action error, whereas OC-GWAM gives the best relation-prediction F1. With target identity withheld in RelComp-v1A, OC-GWAM achieves the best three-seed mean action error (0.01437), future-position error (0.00562), and edge micro-F1 (0.93591), and is best across all tested relations and object counts. On RelComp-v1B, Slot-WAM remains strongest for the simple direct-action mapping, while OC-GWAM has the highest edge F1 in every regime and improves held-out-composition action error over geometry-only and type-only ablations in all three seeds. We further evaluate all ten LIBERO-Spatial tasks through a frozen oracle-state graph interface. On 5,323 validation windows from trajectories excluded from gradient training, OC-GWAM obtains the best Action L1 (0.083132), position error (0.003256), and edge F1 (0.993989); because this split also selects checkpoints, these are not independent test estimates. A 240-episode closed-loop pilot yields comparable success for Geom-WAM (53.3%) and OC-GWAM (51.7%). Overall, explicit relations most consistently improve world-model fidelity and held-out relational composition, while direct control can remain competitive with implicit object attention or geometry alone.

articles.title: Tricking Turing: How to Build a Geometric Checkerboard on Living Tissue
articles.abstract: The snake’s head fritillary (Fritillaria meleagris) displays one of the rarest pigmentation motifs in the plant kingdom: a high-contrast checkerboard of alternating purple and white domains on its flowers. Standard reaction–diffusion theory does not generically produce this pattern: while Turing instabilities in isotropic media select a length scale, they impose no preferred orientation or strict alternation between neighbors.We show that a minimal set of three sequential physical mechanisms — a simulated Gray–Scott-type reaction–diffusion prepattern guided by vascular veins, anisotropic diffusion confined to interveinal corridors, and a threshold-switch Hill-type pigmentation response, each already documented separately in living systems — is sufficient to produce a square, alternating motif. We quantify agreement with biological measurements using a dedicated shape metric, the Square Index (SI [%]), capturing how closely a pigment domain approaches a perfect square. The full model raises SI from the classical Turing-spot value (≈ 76%) to ≈ 83%, closing roughly a third of the remaining gap to an ideal square lattice (100%); we instead account for the pattern’s strict two-dimensional alternation structurally, via vein-imposed staggering. These results show how tissue geometry and transport anisotropy can steer diffusion-driven instabilities into a non-canonical spatial pattern.

articles.title: Epoch-Level Astrometric Contamination versus False Cross-Epoch Association in Threshold-Limited Proper-Motion Surveys: A Validated Statistical Framework, a Real-Data Provenance Audit, and a Preliminary Multi-Field Test Against Cat WISE2020/unTimely
articles.abstract: Marocco et al. (2021) report, without a mechanistic explanation, that CatWISE2020 proper-motion uncertainties near W1 ≈ 17.2 mag are underestimated by a factor of ∼ 2.1× relative to their formal values, established via a median-χ 2 comparison against Gaia DR2. We develop a complete, first-principles statistical framework to test whether this discrepancy is attributable to genuine epoch-level astrometric contamination linked to an independently measured blending indicator (fracflux), after (i) deriving and validating a leverage-corrected studentized residual for weightedleast-squares proper-motion fits, (ii) showing analytically and numerically that pure epoch-count stochasticity from a threshold-limited detection process is quantitatively negligible (predicted inflation factor 1.00 ± 0.01 across W1 = 14.5–18.2), (iii) quantitatively excluding two simpler mechanisms (a uniform multiplicative rescaling and a fixed additive uncertainty floor) using literature-only parameters, and (iv) explicitly separating genuine single-source epoch contamination (H5) from an easily-confused but mechanistically distinct failure mode, false cross-epoch association of two real sources (H6). The resulting marginal logistic model, with cluster-robust (Huber–White/Liang–Zeger sandwich) inference, natural-cubic-spline covariate control, and a quasi-likelihood information criterion (QIC) appropriate to clustered data, is validated end-to-end on synthetic data with known ground truth, including a fully disclosed history of four real implementation defects discovered and corrected during that validation. We then execute the frozen, pre-registered pipeline on three genuine unTimely/CatWISE2020 fields, obtained via a manual per-file relay after direct programmatic archive access proved unavailable from our compute environment. The three fields yield heterogeneous results: null (βˆ 1 = −0.067 ± 0.198, p = 0.734), a significant, correctly-signed effect (βˆ 1 = −1.032 ± 0.083, p < 10−6 ), and a significant, oppositely-signed effect (βˆ 1 = +2.188 ± 0.108, p < 10−6 ). Cross-referencing real archival metadata reveals the third field lies within 2.7 ◦ of the Galactic plane, an extreme stellar-density regime affecting 5 of 20 pre-registered candidate tiles (25%), not anticipated by an ecliptic-latitude-only stratification. Against our pre-registered decision rule, which requires sign- and magnitude-consistent detection across at least eight independent fields before any contamination claim is made, this evidence neither confirms nor refutes the proposed mechanism. We report the result exactly as obtained, present the validated framework, its full real-data provenance audit, and this transparent partial execution as the contribution of this work, and specify precisely what remains to complete the preregistered test.

articles.title: Structural Absorptive Capacity and the Conditional Effectiveness of International Climate Finance: Evidence from Agricultural Labour Composition and Productivity
articles.abstract: International climate finance channeled to developing economies has expanded rapidly, yet the countries receiving the largest transfers are frequently those least equipped, structurally, to convert that capital into measurable emissions reductions. This study investigates whether two observable features of an economy's agricultural sector, the share of the labour force still engaged in agriculture and the value added generated per agricultural worker, systematically moderate the relationship between climate finance and carbon emissions. Using an unbalanced panel spanning more than one hundred developing and emerging economies between 2000 and 2019, and a two-way fixed effects framework subjected to a wide battery of standard-error and specification checks, the analysis finds that the marginal effect of climate finance reverses sign between agriculture-dependent and structurally advanced economies, a pattern that survives the inclusion of income and trade-openness controls, alternative structural thresholds, and estimation on absolute rather than per-capita emissions. A composite readiness indicator built from the same two structural markers reveals that a substantial share of major finance recipients rank poorly on absorptive capacity. Identification limitations, including an imperfect placebo test, are reported candidly. The findings point toward a structural dimension of climate finance allocation that existing governance-centred screening frameworks currently overlook.

articles.title: Structure property correlation and cyclic behaviour of microalloyed high strength structural steel
articles.abstract: Microalloyed structural steels are extensively used in load bearing applications that need superior weldability, as well as an optimum combination of strength, ductility, and fatigue resistance, according to carbon equivalent criteria. This study investigates the influence of microstructural characteristics, particularly grain size, microalloying, pearlite morphology, and phase fraction, on the tensile, and fatigue behaviour of three microalloyed steels. A combination of ferritic and pearlitic microstructure was observed in all the steels. Steel 1 exhibited the highest yield strength (582 ± 14 MPa) and ultimate tensile strength (662 ± 18 MPa), along with an impact energy of 61.51 ± 2.1 J, which was attributed due to combined effect of fine grain size, lower carbon content, lower crystallite size, higher microstrain and higher dislocation density. However, comparatively lower elongation (18.35 ± 2.5%) and microhardness (209 ± 5 HV0.2). In contrast, steel 3 demonstrated the highest elongation (26.89 ± 2.23%) and microhardness (280 ± 6 HV0.2), associated with its coarser grain structure, higher carbon content, reduced pearlitic interlamellar spacing, and phase fraction. Under cyclic loading, steel 2 exhibits the highest fatigue strength of 286 MPa at stress amplitude of 280 MPa for 10⁶ cycles, followed by steels 1 and 3. Microstructural analysis revealed extensive dislocation structures and intergranular deformation in steel 1, promoting localised slip accumulation and early crack initiation. Steel 2 exhibited more uniform cyclic deformation due to its fine pearlite spacing, enabling improved strain accommodation and superior fatigue performance. Conversely, steel 3 showed pronounced dislocation entanglement at pearlite ferrite interfaces, resulting in strain localisation and microcrack initiation.

articles.title: Effects of Substrate Temperature and Selenium to Gallium Flux Ratio on the Growth and Structure of MBE Grown GaSe Thin Films on c-Plane Sapphire
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals gallium selenide (GaSe) is a promising layered semiconductor for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic devices because of its tunable bandgap, high photoresponsivity, and strong optical anisotropy. However, realizing high-quality epitaxial GaSe films remains challenging because of the narrow growth window associated with selenium volatility and the sensitivity of crystal formation to growth conditions. In particular, the coupled effects of substrate temperature and Se/Ga flux ratio on the growth kinetics and resulting structural quality of MBE-grown GaSe remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we systematically investigate how these two parameters affect molecular beam epitaxy-grown GaSe thin films on c-plane sapphire. Four growth conditions were examined by combining substrate temperatures of 550 and 600°C with Se/Ga flux ratios of 400 and 500. In situ RHEED monitoring, complemented by AFM, XRD, and TEM characterization, revealed that increasing the substrate temperature substantially enhances surface diffusion and crystalline ordering, whereas the Se/Ga flux ratio governs the balance between nucleation and lateral coalescence. Among the investigated conditions, growth at 600°C with a Se/Ga flux ratio of 400 yielded the best overall structural and morphological quality, as evidenced by the lowest surface-protrusion coverage (1.50%), strong GaSe (00l) XRD reflections, and highly coherent layered stacking observed by HRTEM. These findings demonstrate that GaSe epitaxy is governed by the coupled effects of substrate temperature and selenium overpressure and establish a practical growth window for obtaining highly ordered GaSe films on c-plane sapphire.

articles.title: Bulk Superconductivity driven by Disorder-Induced Delocalization
articles.abstract: Delocalization transitions underlie many important problems in condensed matter physics, particularly unconventional superconductivity. The observation is that a system near a localized state (like a Mott or Kondo insulator), undergoes a small to large Fermi surface change that coincides with the highest superconducting critical temperatures. The implication is that understanding the mechanism behind the delocalization will point to the mechanism of superconductivity itself [1; 2; 3]. We explore this question in the unconventional superconductor 4Hb-TaS2, a system that interleaves Mott-like and metallic layers, and show that there is indeed a Fermi surface transition in a flat band that is correlated with the appearance of bulk superconductivity. We show that there is a surprising origin to this delocalization: dis- order. Although counter-intuitive at first, we explain that this process may be more common in nature than previously thought.

articles.title: A self-learning scientific agent for X-ray diffraction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge for scientific agents is to turn analytical experience into reusable expertise grounded in physical evidence. Here we introduce Gan Jiang, a self-learning agent for powder X-ray diffraction built on a diffraction-analysis ecosystem we developed: XMatcher, XQueryer, XDecomposer and WPEM. Together, these engines span phase identification, multiphase decomposition and physics-constrained whole-pattern modelling. Gan Jiang converts analytical experience into executable skills by diagnosing failures, revising skill instructions and code, and validating revisions before reuse, without retraining the language model or changing the underlying physical models. Skills selected using development data and frozen before held-out evaluation achieve higher refinement scores than the original expert-designed skills across FullProf, GSAS-II and PyWPEM. The agent resolves strongly overlapping reflections, quantifies a five-phase ancient Egyptian cosmetic, tracks lattice evolution in an operating battery and compares atomic configurations in a disordered oxide catalyst. On DeltaXRDbench, it leads the evaluated methods in single- and multiphase identification across simulated and experimental data. Without supplied composition, single-phase top-1 accuracies reach 96.30%, 81.78% and 40.83% on MP500, RRUFF and opXRD, respectively, compared with 58.00%, 58.47% and 26.45% for the strongest comparator. These results demonstrate how an integrated scientific tool ecosystem can support agents that extract structural knowledge from measurements while accumulating validated analytical expertise that transfers to new samples.

articles.title: Inference-Time Projection for Physically Valid Biomolecular Diffusion Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AlphaFold 3-style cofolding models predict biomolecular complexes with high structural accuracy, yet a large fraction of their outputs are physically invalid: chains overlap at interfaces, ligand bond lengths and angles are distorted, rings are non-planar, and stereocentres are inverted. Current approaches either steer the sampler with physics-informed potentials, which multiplies sampling cost and memory overhead making inference impossible on large complexes, or finetune the model, costing time and tying the fix to one architecture. We observe that, unlike structural accuracy, physical validity is fully verifiable at inference time from quantities the sampler already holds. We therefore treat physical validity as a constrained inference problem and introduce two closed-form projection operators applied to the diffusion model's denoised clean-coordinate estimate, hatx₀: an inter-chain van der Waals projection that pushes apart the most severely clashing atom pairs, and a ligand distance-geometry projection that restores bond lengths, angles, internal contacts, planarity and chirality. Both operators are local, sparse and displacement-capped, require no network evaluations, gradients or importance sampling, and leave the denoiser and its weights untouched, so they can be dropped into any AF3-style sampler without retraining. Applied to two independently developed models, Boltz-2 and OpenFold-3, across five benchmarks (CASP15, CASP16, the PoseBusters monomer and complex sets, and the Boltz physical-validity test set), our method recovers perfect physical validity while preserving structural-accuracy and ligand-placement metrics. These gains are achieved with negligible runtime and memory overhead, providing a practical, model-agnostic route to physically valid all-atom structure prediction.

articles.title: Smart Content Ingestion for Generative AI Workloads
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The evolution of machine learning has progressively changed where intelligence resides in an AI system. In conventional machine learning the task, data representation, labels and model architecture were tightly coupled, so data preparation was narrow, schema-bound and visible. Generative AI decouples the model from any single task: one foundation model serves open-ended downstream tasks, and the generality gained on the model side is matched by heterogeneity on the data side, because enterprise knowledge is authored in the formats people use (PDF, presentations, spreadsheets, scanned documents, forms, tables, diagrams and mixed-layout files) that carry textual, visual, geometric and structural information at once. A language model or retriever cannot reason reliably over information misrepresented at this interface, so content extraction becomes a lifecycle stage in its own right whose errors no downstream retriever or re-ranker can repair. This paper presents a production-ready content-extraction system that makes this stage explicit, configurable, and measurable. The system incorporates selective OCR routing, a scarcity-first curation engine with a reference-based extraction scorer that measures character, word, and table-structure accuracy, a deterministic structure-aware parent-child chunker, and a read-only retrieval evaluator that generates grounded questions from every page and reports Hit@k, mean reciprocal rank, and latency. On a 180-document corpus the best extractor scores 97.4 of 100 (character error rate 0.13%, table similarity 0.995) and the chunker reaches hit@1 of 68.6%, hit@10 of 92.8% and MRR 0.77 over 25,050 generated questions. We distil three design principles (structure before semantics, never mutate what you measure, budget your labels) and position measured content extraction as the perception layer of enterprise agentic systems.

articles.title: MemMux: Runtime Verification and Honest Resource Attribution for Fleets of Parallel Coding Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developers increasingly run a fleet of coding agents side by side on one workstation. The tools they reach for, terminal multiplexers like tmux and a new generation of agent managers, were built to arrange windows, not to govern memory. When ten agents each spawn language servers, test runners, and browsers, no standard tool can say how much memory belongs to which agent, confirm that a terminated agent's descendants are gone, notice a child that has escaped its agent, or keep the machine off the swap cliff when an OOM kill would silently discard uncommitted work. We treat these as runtime-verification problems: an agent-hosting substrate should continuously emit observable signals an operator or auditor can check while agents run. We present MemMux, a local runtime that turns resource governance into checkable signals (per-agent attribution, complete reclamation, escaped-process visibility, bounded footprint under overcommit, and monitoring overhead), with a claims-disciplined benchmark against tmux, a purpose-built agent multiplexer, and a raw-process baseline on identical workloads. Under a binding memory budget on a Linux host, MemMux keeps the fleet under budget (7.5 GiB) with zero swap by admitting a subset and reclaiming under pressure, while the ungoverned tools run every agent, pin the machine at its RAM ceiling (2x over budget), and spill about 2 GiB into swap. MemMux reclaims 100% of a terminated agent's process subtree where the raw baseline strands half of it, and it alone surfaces escaped children (10 of 10 detected). We report the cost: the 1 Hz attribution scan runs near 0.6% CPU at one agent but 2.7% at ten, above our 2% target. Running the harness on real Claude Code sessions shows 100% attribution and low overhead carry over to live agent trees. We release the engine, benchmark, and a one-command reproducer.

articles.title: Textual Environmental Context and Spatial Graphs for LLM-Based Regional SST Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) forecasting depends on local temporal persistence, regional spatial dependence, and environmental conditions that evolve with the forecast date. We study how these heterogeneous conditions can be presented to a large language model (LLM) for regional multi-step forecasting without serializing the full SST grid as text. We formulate forecasting as conditional numerical generation: historical SST and anomaly sequences, date-aligned environmental records, and static ocean knowledge form a textual context, while regional spatial state is supplied through continuous graph-derived prefixes. A static graph encodes persistent geographic--climatological relations, and a dynamic graph encodes recent SST correlations and localized tropical-cyclone influence. Two graph neural networks produce a target-node representation that is mapped by a spatial-prefix fusion and injected into the LLM input. On SST forecasting in the South China Sea, the complete configuration achieves the best MAE and Rtwo among the compared methods over ten forecast steps. Alongside the numerical forecast, a rule-based module matches predicted trends and environmental-factor directions with knowledge entries to return source-linked, post-hoc contextual explanations.

articles.title: Can Agents Work for Everyone? Cross-User Reliability for Mobile GUI Agents in Personalized User Interfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile GUI agents increasingly operate on interfaces influenced by users' histories and preferences, but their reliability across different users remains underexplored. We introduce PAIR (Personalized Application-state Instantiation and Rendering), a pipeline for constructing user-conditioned application states that enables controlled evaluation of the same task across different users. We further introduce RePAIR (Reinforcement learning with Personalization-Aware Interaction Rewards), a training approach that learns from cross-user differences in subgoal outcomes to improve reliability across user-conditioned mobile environments. Across six agents, we find substantial variation in task success across users and consistently lower subgoal achievement in user-conditioned UI contexts (6.98 to 15.4 pp). This gap further increases for personal targets drawn from each user's own content (8.77 to 22.0 pp). Failures in these contexts frequently involve selecting another item instead of the intended target, particularly before target exposure. Finally, RePAIR improves user-conditioned SAR (+5.87 pp), all-success (+7.50 pp), and overall Task SR (+9.42 pp) over its supervised fine-tuning parent on unseen users, providing initial evidence that explicitly learning from cross-user variation can improve GUI-agent reliability.

articles.title: Demo: Vision-Language Model-Guided Online Calibration of an Electromagnetic Digital Twin
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07081v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An electromagnetic (EM) digital twin gives mobile robots wireless situational awareness but depends on material conductivities that change with the environment. Online calibration faces initialization sensitivity and measurement travel costs. We demonstrate a vision-language model (VLM)-guided framework using a Unitree G1 robot and NVIDIA Sionna, with two VLM calls: material classification maps visible materials through ITU-R P.2040 to conductivity priors for Sionna's gradient descent on accumulated received signal strength (RSS) measurements; waypoint planning selects the next measurement location online using residual RSS calibration error and image coverage. In a real indoor scenario, the framework achieves a normalized mean absolute conductivity error of 1.74×10⁻⁴ within 20 m of travel; random initialization never converges, while random waypoints require over twice the travel.

articles.title: Solvation structure and dynamics of choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents with isomeric butanediol hydrogen bond donors
articles.abstract: Choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are being investigated as redox flow battery electrolytes, where solvent viscosity plays a central role in governing ionic mobility, mass transport, and pumping efficiency. In this combined experimental and computational study, a series of DESs formed from choline chloride and butanediol isomer hydrogen bond donors (HBDs) is examined to probe how HBD molecular geometry affects liquid structure and dynamics while holding the molecular formula and hydroxyl group count constant. Density, viscosity, ionic conductivity, and E T (30) polarity are measured experimentally, while molecular dynamics simulations are used to quantify coordination numbers, hydrogen-bond lifetimes, self-diffusivities, dynamic heterogeneity, and local packing. Although the dominant first-shell interaction motifs are preserved across all isomers, systematic differences in hydrogen-bond dynamics, diol–diol connectivity, and spatial heterogeneity give rise to distinct transport behaviors, including substantial variations in viscosity and conductivity, that cannot be attributed to changes in local coordination structure alone. These results establish hydroxyl group arrangement as a key structural parameter governing DES transport properties and provide a controlled molecular framework for the rational design of choline chloride-based electrolytes.

articles.title: Topology-Consistent Task Planning over Cellular Workflow Complexes for LLM-based Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task planning for LLM agents requires workflows that satisfy both user intent and complex sub-task dependencies. While existing planners work well for sequential or directed acyclic graph (DAG)-like structures, they struggle with workflow patterns such as verification-correction loops, convergent branch merging, and reusable intermediate states that arise naturally in real-world tool orchestration. We present TopoPlanner, a topology-consistent planning framework that lifts tool dependency graphs into cellular workflow complexes and uses them as topologyaware context for LLM tool planning. TopoPlanner retrieves a request-relevant closed subcomplex through cosheaf-consistent cellular retrieval, performs multidimensional structural reasoning over the retrieved topology, and interfaces the resulting cellular representation with the planner LLM for tool-sequence generation. Experiments on four tool-planning benchmarks with topology-guided loop, merge, and loop-merge workflows show consistent improvements over prompt-based and graph-enhanced baselines across different local LLM backbones.

articles.title: MARS: Multi-resolution Adaptive Routing for Sequential Recommendation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-history recommenders often compress each user's history into a compact, candidate-independent memory that is cached and reused to score large candidate pools. We show that real user histories exhibit multi-scale semantic structure, with short-lived intent, medium-term interests, and long-term preferences coexisting in one sequence, and that monolithic cached memories preserve these scales unevenly: linear probes recover recent and mid-range content far worse than long-range content. We call this failure mode temporal aliasing. We propose MARS, a multi-resolution user memory that writes the full history into recurrent state tracks anchored to different half-lives, and a sparse routing reader that materializes compact seed memories by selecting the relevant temporal resolutions for each seed, preserving fixed-size candidate scoring. MARS outperforms strong baselines on three public datasets, with gains that grow with history length. Component-matched ablations with paired tests show that temporal diversity and selective routing each contribute beyond what hard-window memories or added capacity provide. The advantage of MARS over its interface-matched baseline also widens after within-user behavioral shifts, at about 1.02× that baseline's warm-cache serving latency for 1,000 candidates per user.

articles.title: Matching Object or Relation? Tracing Abstract Reasoning Inside VLMs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) excel on visual benchmarks but fail systematically on tasks requiring abstract reasoning. Existing benchmarks document this failure but cannot say emphwhy it happens or which cognitive capability is missing. We close this gap by adopting the Relational Match-to-Sample (RMTS) paradigm from comparative and developmental psychology and pairing it with a mechanistic analysis of the model's internals. On a parametrically controlled stimulus set evaluated across frontier API models (GPT, Claude, Gemini) and three open-source families (Qwen3.5, Gemma-4, InternVL3), we identify four levers that shift VLMs toward the relational match---capability tier, model scale, the number of objects per scene, and the absence of per-object stimulus noise---together producing a developmental-like trajectory that mirrors the human emphrelational shift. Opening up the model, a per-layer representational similarity analysis and a causal mediation analysis reveal that VLM abstract reasoning is implemented by two competing circuits: an early circuit that organises images by their surface object features, and a late circuit that organises them by their abstract relation. Extending the analysis to ARC-AGI-1, we find that ablating the relational heads identified on RMTS degrades performance more than ablating random heads, indicating that the relational circuit is recruited beyond our controlled stimuli. We hope this mechanism-level view serves as a step toward understanding how abstract reasoning is implemented in VLMs.

articles.title: Natural Language Questions as an Interface for Knowledge Graphs: QRAKEN Graph Distillation and Semantic Self-Healing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural-language access to RDF knowledge graphs is a core Semantic Web ambition. Large language models (LLMs) have advanced Text-to-SPARQL, yet on unfamiliar graphs they often generate valid queries that misrepresent the populated data model. QRAKEN is a training-free, ontology-agnostic neurosymbolic pipeline grounding generation in empirical graph evidence rather than schema expectations. An offline distiller produces TTQL, a compact description of populated multi-hop patterns, conditional frequencies and path-conditioned literal examples, plus a class-property co-occurrence matrix. Online, TTQL guides the LLM, while deterministic syntax, vocabulary and data-model checks provide diagnostics for iterative refinement. On CK25 (First International Text2SPARQL Challenge), under matched-condition recomputation on a QLever snapshot, QRAKEN achieves strict F1 of 0.643 ± 0.026 with GPT-4.1 mini and 0.652 ± 0.012 with GPT-5.4: relative gains of 30% and 32% over the strongest recomputed participant, outperforming systems using the same base model family. Ablations identify TTQL patterns as the dominant driver (+0.31 strict F1 over a shape-only baseline); the refinement loop provides a cheap safety net, rejecting triple patterns unsupported by the co-occurrence matrix. Compared with auto-derived SHACL, TTQL yields 64% higher strict F1, supporting the value of empirical patterns beyond schema exposure. With two local 35B 4-bit open-weight models at zero marginal cost, the same pipeline matches the strongest recomputed participant, and TTQL advantages over shape-only and SHACL baselines persist. Results on a single, relatively small benchmark provide an initial empirical signal; monolithic TTQL injection on very open cross-domain graphs remains the main limitation.

articles.title: DSV-Mem: Evaluating Multimodal Memory in Professional Workflows for MLLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational MLLM agents are increasingly expected to assist in professional workflows, from AI research and engineering design to product management and business operations. Yet this capability remains underexplored: existing benchmarks largely focus on informal, everyday interactions and personal-life scenarios featuring photographic natural images, isolated static artifacts, and recall-oriented questions. In contrast, professional scenarios often involve structured, information-heavy artifacts that undergo frequent revisions and authority updates, and compositional queries requiring reconciliation of many artifact versions while tracking state precisely. To address these challenges, we introduce DSV-Mem, a benchmark for evaluating Dense Stateful Visual Memory. DSV-Mem comprises expert-reviewed scenarios and 1,000 questions across five user-oriented categories (Current State, Past State, Derived State, Change History, and Conflict/Refusal). A Hartley-inspired criterion favors questions with broader visual-evidence inspection demands. We also introduce a generation harness that produces evaluation suites by decoupling state-transition synthesis from conversation filling. Evaluation over 27 configurations spanning frontier and open-weight models and memory management methods reveals that the strongest baseline scores below 45% on DSV-Mem. Analysis surfaces findings: 1) multimodality and information density both contribute to difficulty, but state evolution, particularly the number of governing updates, is the dominant tested factor. Raw conversation/haystack length, OCR, and arithmetic are not the primary bottlenecks; 2) models often fail to verify user premises against prior state updates before answering; 3) increased reasoning effort and memory management methods yield limited gains, whereas state-aware designs prove more effective. The benchmark and code will be publicly released.

articles.title: Recursive Game Creator: An Agentic Product-Level Experience-Oriented Game Harness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent game design agents have made substantial progress in generating playable games. However, program correctness does not ensure an enjoyable experience for players. We present Recursive Game Creator, an experience-oriented harness to advance agentic game development from rough game prototypes into entertaining games. Recursive Game Creator organizes recursive development around four components: Designer, Builder, Player, and Reviewer. The Designer translates user instructions and Reviewer's feedback into detailed plans. The Builder turns these plans into candidate games. The coding-native Player creates and executes reusable policies through programmatic interfaces to efficiently collect diverse gameplay trajectories, mitigating evaluation bias caused by slow GUI-based collection. The Reviewer uses carefully designed trajectory-based metrics to induce player preferences, integrating with visual evidence and explicit textual preferences to evaluate games against game-specific criteria. Finally, the Reviewer accepts the better version and provides improvement reviews for the next round, closing the recursive loop. Our method achieves state-of-the-art overall performance of 77.89 on GameCraft-Bench. On GameASG-Bench, it achieves a strict task success rate of 53.2%, a 34.1% improvement over the same-model baseline, and the highest mean runtime-check pass rate at 93.4% among compared methods. A user study shows longer playtime and higher ratings. Code is coming soon.

articles.title: Parallel Predictive World Models for Accurate and Efficient Long-Horizon Planning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon world-model planning typically relies on autoregressive rollouts, where predicted states are repeatedly fed back into the model. This preserves temporal structure but creates a horizon-length sequential path and exposes later predictions to recursive decoded-state feedback. We introduce Parallel Predictive World Models (PPWM), which predict a finite-horizon trajectory in parallel while retaining causal interaction among future representations. Each horizon is conditioned on its causal action prefix, and future representations interact before decoding, separating temporal causality from state-by-state output recursion. We formalize this distinction by viewing autoregressive rollout as a causal trajectory map and identifying the decoded-state feedback pathway removed by PPWM. Across four visual-control tasks, PPWM achieves the lowest long-horizon prediction error and the highest Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) simulator success among the evaluated predictive interfaces. Meanwhile, PPWM achieves more than a 3× average CEM planning speedup over the autoregressive LeWM baseline. These results suggest that accurate and efficient long-horizon world-model planning does not require state-by-state autoregression, but can instead be achieved through parallel causal trajectory prediction.

articles.title: Geometry-enforced topological chiral fermions in amorphous chiral metals
articles.abstract: Author(s): Justin Schirmann, Adolfo G. Grushin, and Benjamin J. Wieder Chiral topological semimetals are phases of matter that host robust band crossings and topologically protected surface states. So far, their interesting properties have been believed to be restricted to the realm of perfect crystals. In this work, the authors show how they can survive strong structural disorder, challenging the view that disorder inevitably destroys this topological state. Using analytical theory, symmetry-group methods, numerical calculations, and a novel amorphous Wilson-loop technique, they demonstrate that Weyl and higher-charge chiral fermions can persist even in amorphous metals. Long-range order in local structural chirality stabilizes these phases. This understanding suggests pathways for engineering such geometry-enforced topological behavior in strongly disordered systems, opening up new possibilities for investigating these phases of matter and exploring their potential applications. [Phys. Rev. Materials 10, 104201] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026

articles.title: Unbiased large-N approach to competing vestigial orders of density-wave and superconducting instabilities
articles.abstract: Author(s): Grgur Palle and Rafael M. Fernandes Vestigial orders are partially melted versions of ordered states stabilized by fluctuations of the order parameter. Observed in several quantum materials, their theoretical description has often relied on a large- N approximation that suffers from ambiguities due to multiple interfering channels. Here, the authors uncover the structural reasons for the ambiguities and from them derive a large- N prescription that removes the ambiguities, yielding unequivocal physical results. This prescription is then applied to multicomponent density wave and superconducting instabilities, where they find exotic vestigial phases describing spin-quadrupolar, charge-4 e superconducting, and altermagnetic orders. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 245108] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026
